entries.text: Have you made any crafts with paper?

paragraphs: Yeah, but mostly when I was a kid. I used to fold simple things like paper cranes and paper airplanes at school, and I remember competing with my classmates to see whose plane could fly the farthest.
[ I haven't really made anything like that in years, though.]
paragraphsZh: 是的，不过主要是小时候。我以前在学校会折一些简单的东西，比如纸鹤和纸飞机，我还记得会和同学比赛，看谁的飞机能飞得最远。[不过这么多年我基本上没再做过这类东西了。]

entries.text: Do you still write physical letters?

paragraphs: Emm, no, not at all, actually. I can't even remember the last time I picked up a pen to write a full letter.
It just feels kind of outdated now, since everything's digital anyway. [ If I want to reach someone, I'd just send a quick text or an email, which is so much faster.]

entries.text: Do people still keep handwritten letters today?

paragraphs: Well, people probably receive far fewer handwritten letters these days, but I'd say if someone does get one, they're more likely to keep it than before. Because they're so rare nowadays, getting a handwritten letter feels way more special than a digital message.
[So when people do get one, they usually save it as a nice memory.]
paragraphsZh: 嗯，现在人们收到的手写信件可能少了很多，但我觉得如果有人真的收到了一封，反而更有可能把它保留下来，比以前更甚。因为现在这种信件太稀少了，收到一封手写信会让人觉得比数字信息特别得多。[所以当人们真的收到一封时，通常都会把它保存下来作为一份美好的回忆。]

paragraphs: Mostly simple things, like saying "please" and "thank you," greeting adults properly, and saying goodbye before leaving. I also remember being taught to wait my turn and not interrupt people when they were talking.

entries.text: What do you do when you see rubbish on the street?

paragraphs: Emm, I try to pick it up if I can, especially if there's a bin nearby. I think it's just a small thing that makes the area look nicer for everyone.
But if my hands are full or it looks kind of gross, I'll admit I just leave it there.
paragraphsZh: 嗯，如果可以的话我会尽量把它捡起来，尤其是附近有垃圾桶的时候。我觉得这只是一件小事，但能让这个地方对大家来说看起来更干净一点。但如果我手里拿满了东西，或者垃圾看起来很恶心，我得承认我就会直接不管它了。

source.label: 腾讯文档《雅思口语9-12月题库【Part123】》

entries.text: How do you recycle things like paper and plastic?

paragraphs: Since paper and plastic are both recyclables, I usually put them together in one bin at home, separate from food waste and other general trash. Once the recycling bin is full, I simply take it down to the recycling point.
[ It's honestly not that big of a deal once you get used to sorting things properly.]
paragraphsZh: 因为纸张和塑料都属于可回收物，所以我通常会把它们放在家里的同一个垃圾桶里，和厨余垃圾以及其他普通垃圾分开。等回收垃圾满了之后，我就会把它拿到回收点去。[说实话，一旦你养成了正确分类的习惯，这也没什么大不了的。]

entries.text: Did you recycle when you were a kid?

paragraphs: Not really, waste sorting wasn't really a thing back then, at least not where I grew up. We just threw everything into one bin.
The only thing close to recycling was saving old plastic bottles and cardboard boxes at home to sell them for a bit of money.
paragraphsZh: 不太会，那时候垃圾分类还不算是件普遍的事，至少在我长大的地方不是。我们就是把所有东西都扔进同一个垃圾桶。唯一算得上接近垃圾回收的事，就是把家里的旧塑料瓶和纸箱攒起来，卖了换点钱。

entries.text: Is there an advertisement that made an impression on you when you were a child?

paragraphs: Yeah, definitely, there's this one commercial that's honestly iconic in China, it's for a health supplement called 脑白金. The slogan was something like "don't give gifts this year, only give 脑白金", and it played on TV literally all the time.
[It was so repetitive that everyone just ended up memorizing it, whether they wanted to or not.]
paragraphsZh: 是的，肯定有，有一个广告在中国真的很标志性，是一款叫脑白金的保健品广告。它的广告语大概是"今年过节不收礼，收礼只收脑白金"，而且这个广告在电视上简直是无时无刻不在播。[它重复播放的次数太多了，以至于大家最后都不由自主地记住了它。]

entries.text: Did you have a long journey with your family as a child?

paragraphs: Yeah, actually we used to go on quite long journeys every New Year holiday to visit my grandparents, since they lived in a different city. It usually took around six or seven hours by car, and I remember getting pretty restless halfway through.

entries.text: What transport do you often use when travelling?

paragraphs: Emm, it really depends on the distance. For longer trips, I usually take a plane or high-speed train, since they're much faster and more comfortable for covering long distances.
For shorter trips within the city, I'll just use the metro or grab a shared bike instead.

entries.text: Do u prefer to study in the mornings or in the afternoon?

paragraphs: I prefer to study in the mornings because that’s when I feel most focused and productive. My mind is clearer and I can get more done in less time.
On average, I spend around 20 to 30 hours a week on my studies, including attending classes, reviewing notes, doing assignments, and preparing for exams.
paragraphsZh: 我更喜欢在早上学习，因为那时候我最专注、效率也最高。我的思路比较清晰，能在较短时间内完成更多事情。 通常我每周会花大约20到30小时在学习上，包括上课、复习笔记、做作业和准备考试。

entries.text: What requirements did u need to meet to get your current job?

paragraphs: To get my current job, I needed to show that I had both strong communication skills and a good understanding of digital tools. At work, I often use tools like Excel, Notion, and some editing software.
Technology plays a big role in improving efficiency and helping me stay organized.

entries.text: What do u think is the most important at the moment?

paragraphs: Right now, I think the most important thing for me is gaining practical experience and building a strong foundation in my field. In the next five years, I plan to work on long-term projects that allow me to grow steadily, improve my skills, and eventually take on more responsibility.
I also hope to find a workplace that values creativity and personal development.
paragraphsZh: 我认为目前对我来说最重要的是积累实践经验，在我的专业领域打下坚实的基础。 来五年，我打算参与一些长期项目，稳步成长，提升自己的能力，并逐渐承担更多责任。我也希望能找到一个重视创造力和个人成长的工作环境。

entries.text: Do u miss being a student?

paragraphs: 为什么？ Yes, I do miss being a student, especially because during that time, one of my teachers really helped me a lot. He always encouraged me to speak up in class and gave me confidence when I doubted myself.
His support made me believe in my abilities and shaped the way I handle challenges now. That’s why those student years are so special and unforgettable for me.
paragraphsZh: 是的，我确实怀念学生时代，尤其是因为那段时间有一位老师对我帮助很大。他总是鼓励我在课堂上发言，在我怀疑自己的时候给我信心。他的支持让我相信自己的能力，也影响了我现在面对困难的方式。这也是为什么学生时代对我来说那么特别、那么难忘。

entries.text: Do u live in a noisy or a quiet area?

paragraphs: 注：问题较多考官提问语音单独 以下题目相同 I’m currently a student and I live in a dorm right on campus. It’s a bit noisy because there are teaching buildings and supermarkets nearby, but I really like it.
Life is super convenient, and I get to share my daily life with my roommates. When I have free time, I love hanging out at the supermarket near my dorm.
They have all kinds of things, and the prices are pretty cheap for students.
paragraphsZh: 我目前是一名学生，住在校园内的宿舍里。因为附近有教学楼和超市，所以有点吵闹，但我真的很喜欢这里。生活非常便利，我可以和室友们分享我的日常生活。 有空的时候，我喜欢在宿舍附近的超市闲逛。那里有各种各样东西，而且对学生来说价格相当便宜。

entries.text: Where is your hometown?

paragraphs: 注：问题较多考官提问语音单独 以下题目相同 My hometown is [补充家乡名称], located in [补充家乡身份] province. It’s a relatively small place.
In terms of nature, the environment is very good and the surroundings are pleasant. Besides that, my hometown also has some important local industries, like farming and small factories.
It’s famous for its ancient buildings, which attract people who want to learn about the local history and culture. I like living there because of the calm lifestyle and friendly people.
However, it lacks job opportunities, which is not very convenient for young people. I left after growing up and going to university.
I don’t think I will live there for a long time in the future.
paragraphsZh: 我的家乡是XXX，位于XXX省。那是一个相对较小的城市。从自然方面来看，环境非常好，周围环境宜人。除此之外，我的家乡还有一些重要的本地产业，如农业和小型工厂。它因古老的建筑而闻名，吸引着想要了解当地历史和文化的人们。 我喜欢住在那里，因为那里的生活方式很平静，人们很友好。然而，那里缺乏工作机会，这对年轻人来说不太方便。我在长大并上了大学后离开了。我认为将来我不会在那里长期居住。

entries.text: Is your hometown a good place for young people to pursue their careers?

paragraphs: No, it’s not really a good place for young people to pursue their careers. The town is peaceful and friendly, but it lacks job opportunities and career development options.
Most young people, including me, leave for university or work elsewhere.

entries.text: Have u learned anything about the history of your hometown?

paragraphs: Yes, I know quite a lot about the history and culture of my hometown. When I was a kid, we learned mostly in school through lessons from our teachers.
Also, our teachers would take us out to visit old buildings and some historical sites. I felt really proud to see that my hometown has so many valuable historical resources.
paragraphsZh: 是的，我对我的家乡的历史和文化了解很多。当我还是个孩子的时候，我们主要通过在学校上老师的课程来学习。此外，我们的老师还会带我们去参观老建筑和一些历史遗迹。看到我的家乡有这么多宝贵的文化遗产，我感到非常自豪。

entries.text: Who do u live with?

paragraphs: 注：问题较多考官提问语音单独 以下题目相同 Well, I’m currently living in a university dorm with my roommates. Actually, since it’s right on campus, it’s super convenient for me to get to my classes—and having supermarkets and study rooms nearby is really handy.

To get around, I usually ride a bike or an electric scooter on campus, but if I’m going out, I just take a bus.The public transport is actually great, and there are plenty of options, so it’s really easy to get anywhere. Speaking of houses or apartments, I don't really have a choice right now, but I’d definitely prefer an apartment in the future because I think they're safer and more comfortable.
I've lived here for a few years now, ever since I started school, but I’m gonna leave after I graduate. I'm sure I’ll really miss how easy life is here.
paragraphsZh: 我现在和室友住在大学宿舍里。实际上，因为它就在校园里，所以对我来说去上课非常方便——附近有超市和学习室，真的很方便。 为了出行，我通常在校园里骑自行车或电动车，但如果要出去，我就坐公交车。公共交通其实很棒，选择很多，所以去哪里都很方便。 说到房子或公寓，我现在真的没有太多选择，但将来我肯定会更喜欢公寓，因为我觉得它们更安全、更舒适。我现在已经在这里住了几年了，自从我开始上学以来，但我毕业后就要离开了。我确信我会非常怀念这里的生活有多轻松。

phrases: 引入背景: living in a university dorm

entries.text: How long have u lived here?

paragraphs: 注：问题较多考官提问语音单独 以下题目相同 Well, I’m currently living in a university dorm with my roommates. Actually, since it’s right on campus, it’s super convenient for me to get to my classes—and having supermarkets and study rooms nearby is really handy.

To get around, I usually ride a bike or an electric scooter on campus, but if I’m going out, I just take a bus.The public transport is actually great, and there are plenty of options, so it’s really easy to get anywhere. Speaking of houses or apartments, I don't really have a choice right now, but I’d definitely prefer an apartment in the future because I think they're safer and more comfortable.
I've lived here for a few years now, ever since I started school, but I’m gonna leave after I graduate. I'm sure I’ll really miss how easy life is here.
paragraphsZh: 我现在和室友住在大学宿舍里。实际上，因为它就在校园里，所以对我来说去上课非常方便——附近有超市和学习室，真的很方便。 为了出行，我通常在校园里骑自行车或电动车，但如果要出去，我就坐公交车。公共交通其实很棒，选择很多，所以去哪里都很方便。 说到房子或公寓，我现在真的没有太多选择，但将来我肯定会更喜欢公寓，因为我觉得它们更安全、更舒适。我现在已经在这里住了几年了，自从我开始上学以来，但我毕业后就要离开了。我确信我会非常怀念这里的生活有多轻松。

entries.text: Please describe the room u live in?

paragraphs: My dorm is a shared room for four, and it’s got a loft bed design—the bed is on top and my desk is underneath. We have a small balcony, but the restroom and shower are actually outside the room.
To be honest, I don’t really have a separate room to choose from. I only have this tiny space, so my favorite part is definitely my desk.
I basically spend all day there studying, eating, or playing on my computer. Even though it’s small, it’s my own little world that makes me feel super relaxed.
paragraphsZh: 我的宿舍是一个四人间的，它有一个上床下桌的设计——床在上面，我的书桌在下面。我们有一个小阳台，但洗手间和淋浴间实际上在房间外面。 说实话，我并没有一个可以自由选择的独立房间。我只拥有这个小空间，所以我最喜欢的地方当然是我的书桌。我基本上整天都在那里学习、吃饭或玩电脑。虽然它很小，但它是我自己的小世界，让我感觉非常放松。

entries.text: What's the difference between where u live now and where u have lived in the past?

paragraphs: Currently, I live in a shared room for four, so my personal space is quite small and things can get pretty crowded. It’s very different from the past when I lived at home and had my own room with much more space.

To be honest, I believe a comfortable environment is really important because it helps me stay relaxed and in a good mood. That’s why in the future, I’d love to live in a cozy flat with a balcony and lots of sunlight.
paragraphsZh: 目前，我住在四人房间里，所以我的个人空间相当小，东西也相当拥挤。这和过去我住在家里，有自己的房间，空间大得多的情况非常不同。 说实话，我认为舒适的环境真的很重要，因为它能帮助我保持放松和好心情。这就是为什么在将来，我希望住在带阳台、阳光充足的舒适公寓里。

paragraphs: I’ve been living in [城市] for a few months/years. The weather is quite humid and unpredictable — hot summers, cold winters, and frequent rain.

Even though the weather isn't always ideal, I really like this city because of its fast pace, career opportunities, and mix of traditional and modern culture. [城市] has changed a lot in recent years — new buildings, better transport systems, and a growing international community.

entries.text: Are there people of different ages living in this city?

paragraphs: Well, of course, there are people of all ages in this city. Every time I walk around my neighborhood, I always see young couples with babies, students, working adults, and elderly people taking a walk.

As for how friendly people are, I'd say it's pretty decent — like neighbors usually say hi to each other, and shopkeepers are quite chatty when you stop by. Also, I think the city is quite friendly to kids and old people too — there are playgrounds in parks for kids, and also things like benches and community centers for old people to relax and hang out.
So yeah, it's a place that really thinks about everyone.
paragraphsZh: 嗯，当然，这座城市里有各个年龄段的人。每次我在社区里散步的时候，总是能看到带着宝宝的年轻夫妻、学生、上班族，还有出来散步的老人。 至于这里的人友不友善，我觉得还挺不错的——比如说邻居之间平时会互相打招呼，店主跟你买东西的时候也挺爱聊天的。 另外，我觉得这座城市对小孩和老人也很友好——公园里有给小孩玩的游乐场，还有长椅、社区中心之类的地方给老人休息、聊天。所以整体来说，这是一个真的会照顾到每个人的地方。

entries.text: What do you usually do when there is a traffic jam?

paragraphs: Well, I usually just stay calm and listen to music or podcasts to pass the time. Sometimes I check my phone for messages or browse social media if the traffic isn't moving at all.
There's not much else you can do, so I just try to make the best of it.

entries.text: How are the parks today different from those you visited as a kid?

paragraphs: I think parks today have way more facilities and modern equipment compared to when I was a kid. Back then, parks were pretty basic — just some simple swings and slides.
Now they have things like fitness equipment, basketball courts, and walking trails. [The parks are also much better maintained and cleaner than they used to be.]

paragraphs: I'd say I prefer happy music most of the time. It just puts me in a good mood and gives me energy, especially when I'm working out or hanging out with friends.

entries.text: Do you prefer online shopping or in-store shopping?

paragraphs: I prefer online shopping. It's just so much more convenient — I can browse anytime from home and compare prices easily.
Plus, there are usually better deals and more variety online. I rarely shop in stores anymore.
paragraphsZh: 我更喜欢网购。它方便得多——我可以随时在家浏览并轻松比较价格。而且，网上通常有更好的优惠和更多的选择。我现在很少在实体店购物了。

entries.text: How do you keep your work or study space tidy?

paragraphs: I try to put things away right after I use them, so they don't pile up. I also do a quick clean-up at the end of each day to make sure everything is back in its place.
Keeping things organized helps me stay focused and productive, so it's worth the effort.
paragraphsZh: 我尽量在用完东西后立即把它们放好，这样它们就不会堆积。我还会在每天结束时做一次快速清理，确保一切都回到原位。保持东西有序帮助我保持专注和高效，所以这是值得的努力。

entries.text: What do you think of the people who are not very tidy?

paragraphs: I think it really depends on the person. Some people are just a bit messy, but that doesn't necessarily mean they're lazy.
They might simply have a lot on their plate and not have enough time to keep everything organized. [As long as their mess doesn't affect other people, I don't think it's a big deal.]
paragraphsZh: 我觉得这真的因人而异。有些人只是有点邋遢，但这并不一定意味着他们懒惰。他们可能只是有很多事情要处理，没有足够的时间把所有东西都整理得井井有条。[只要他们的杂乱不会影响到别人，我觉得这就不是什么大问题。]

entries.text: Is wearing headphones comfortable?

paragraphs: Well, I think it really depends on the quality and fit of the headphones. If they're well-designed and fit properly, they can be pretty comfortable, even for long periods.
But if they're poorly made or too tight, they can become really uncomfortable after a while.

entries.text: Do you prefer getting information from websites or books?

paragraphs: I'd say websites, to be honest. They're much more convenient and faster when I need to find information quickly.

Plus, the information is usually up-to-date, which is important for things like news or current events. [Books are great for in-depth reading, but for quick searches, websites are way more practical.]
paragraphsZh: 我会说网站，说实话。当我需要快速查找信息时，它们更方便、更快。而且，信息通常是最新的，这对于新闻或时事之类的事情很重要。[书籍非常适合深度阅读，但对于快速搜索，网站更实用。]

entries.text: Describe a noisy place you have been to

paragraphs: A noisy place I've been to is a scenic spot near my home. It is a bit far from the city, about a two-hour drive, so it counts as a short trip.

Whenever relatives or friends come to visit, they always want to check out this place since it's a well-known local spot, so I end up being the one to take them there. This time was no different — some relatives of mine came to visit during a holiday, I took them there and showed them around.

We basically just walked around the old streets, popped into a few shops, and grabbed some snacks along the way. It's actually an ancient water town, done in this kind of traditional southern-China style — it's supposed to have a lot of charm.

But a lot of the old houses have been turned into, like, bubble tea shops, chain stores, and souvenir shops. The stuff inside doesn't really have any local character — you could buy the exact same things anywhere.
My relatives and I all found it pretty boring. And because it was a holiday, the place was packed — there were people everywhere, we could barely move.

At the same time, shops on both sides kept blasting loudspeakers trying to pull in customers, and with all the noise mixed together — people talking, kids crying, music blasting from different shops. I could barely stand it, I just wanted to get out of there right away.
And to make things worse, it was in all that chaos that I lost my wallet. With so many people pushing and squeezing past, I didn't even notice at the time.
I immediately retraced my steps, going back through all the shops and streets we'd walked through, but there was no sign of it. In the end, I had no choice but to report it to the police.
Luckily, the police managed to pull up the security footage and actually helped me get it back. Such a relief——otherwise I would have lost everything inside, my ID, my bank cards, all of it.
So overall, it's crowded, noisy, boring, and I even lost my wallet there. I really don't want to go back.
It's kind of sad, really — these places end up chasing quick money instead of keeping what made them special. And once that charm is gone, there's really no reason to go back.
paragraphsZh: 我去过的一个嘈杂的地方，是我家附近的一个景区。 这个景区离市区有点远，开车大概要两个小时，算是一次短途旅行。
每次有亲戚朋友来玩，他们总是想来看看这个地方，因为它是一个挺有名的本地景点，所以我总是被叫去带他们过去。 这次也不例外——有几个亲戚在假期过来玩，我就带他们去逛了逛。
我们基本上就是在老街上走走，进了几家店，还顺便吃了点小吃。 这里其实是一个江南水乡古镇，是那种传统的南方水乡风格，本来应该挺有韵味的。
但很多老房子都被改成了奶茶店、连锁店和纪念品店。 里面卖的东西根本没有什么本地特色——在哪里都能买到一样的东西。
我和亲戚们都觉得挺无聊的。 而且因为是假期去的，人特别多，到处都是人，我们几乎没法动。
同时，街边的店铺还一直用喇叭招揽顾客，各种声音混在一起——聊天声、小孩哭声、不同店铺放的音乐声。 我实在受不了了，只想赶紧离开那里。
更糟糕的是，就在那片混乱中，我弄丢了我的钱包。 人群不断推挤，当时我根本没有察觉。
我立刻原路返回，重新走过之前经过的每一家店和街道，但根本找不到。 最后我不得不去报警。
幸运的是，警察调取了监控录像，帮我找回了钱包。 真是松了一口气——否则里面的东西就全没了，我的身份证、银行卡，什么都没了。
总体来说，那里拥挤、嘈杂、无聊，我甚至还在那里丢了钱包。 我真的不想再去了。
说起来也挺可惜的——这些地方最终都在追逐快钱，而不是保留原本让它们特别的东西。 一旦那种韵味消失了，真的就没有理由再回去了。

entries.text: How can people consider others' feelings when chatting in public?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think the simplest way is to keep your voice down and stay aware of who's around you.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得最简单的方式就是压低音量，并留意周围有谁在场。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Public spaces are shared environments, so what feels normal to one person, like laughing loudly, might feel disruptive to someone else nearby who's trying to focus or relax.
ideaNotes.textZh: 公共场所是共享的空间，所以对一个人来说很正常的行为，比如大声笑，对旁边正想专心或放松的人来说可能会觉得很打扰。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, someone talking on the phone in a quiet café might notice people glancing over, and take that as a cue to either lower their voice or step outside.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，一个在安静咖啡馆打电话的人可能会注意到有人在看自己，把这当作一个信号，选择压低声音或者走出去接电话。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: Beyond volume, it also helps to think about timing, like avoiding loud conversations early in the morning or late at night when others might be sleeping.
ideaNotes.textZh: 除了音量之外，考虑时机也很有帮助，比如避免在清晨或深夜大声交谈，因为那时其他人可能正在休息。

keyPhrases.phrase: Stay aware of who's around you

paragraphs: I think the simplest way is to keep your voice down and stay aware of who's around you.
Public spaces are shared environments, so what feels normal to one person, like laughing loudly, might feel disruptive to someone else nearby who's trying to focus or relax.
For instance, someone talking on the phone in a quiet café might notice people glancing over, and take that as a cue to either lower their voice or step outside.
Beyond volume, it also helps to think about timing, like avoiding loud conversations early in the morning or late at night when others might be sleeping.
paragraphsZh: 我觉得最简单的方式就是压低音量，并留意周围有谁在场。
公共场所是共享的空间，所以对一个人来说很正常的行为，比如大声笑，对旁边正想专心或放松的人来说可能会觉得很打扰。
比如，一个在安静咖啡馆打电话的人可能会注意到有人在看自己，把这当作一个信号，选择压低声音或者走出去接电话。
除了音量之外，考虑时机也很有帮助，比如避免在清晨或深夜大声交谈，因为那时其他人可能正在休息。

entries.text: How would people usually respond to noises in your country?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I'd say most people in China tend to just tolerate noise rather than confront it directly.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得大多数中国人面对噪音时，往往会选择忍受，而不是直接对抗。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Confronting someone directly can feel awkward or confrontational, so many people would rather just put up with it than risk an uncomfortable conversation.
ideaNotes.textZh: 直接找人对峙会让人感觉尴尬或有冲突感，所以很多人宁愿选择忍一忍，也不想冒险面对一场让人不自在的对话。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, if a neighbor is being loud late at night, someone might just put on headphones or try to fall asleep anyway, instead of knocking on their door to complain.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，如果邻居深夜很吵，有人可能只是戴上耳机，或者干脆试着睡过去，而不是去敲门抱怨。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: That said, when the noise becomes too much to bear, people will sometimes go through more formal channels, like reporting it to the building management.
ideaNotes.textZh: 不过，当噪音实在无法忍受时，人们有时也会通过更正式的渠道处理，比如向物业投诉。

paragraphs: I'd say most people in China tend to just tolerate noise rather than confront it directly.
Confronting someone directly can feel awkward or confrontational, so many people would rather just put up with it than risk an uncomfortable conversation.
For instance, if a neighbor is being loud late at night, someone might just put on headphones or try to fall asleep anyway, instead of knocking on their door to complain.
That said, when the noise becomes too much to bear, people will sometimes go through more formal channels, like reporting it to the building management.
paragraphsZh: 我觉得大多数中国人面对噪音时，往往会选择忍受，而不是直接对抗。
直接找人对峙会让人感觉尴尬或有冲突感，所以很多人宁愿选择忍一忍，也不想冒险面对一场让人不自在的对话。
比如，如果邻居深夜很吵，有人可能只是戴上耳机，或者干脆试着睡过去，而不是去敲门抱怨。
不过，当噪音实在无法忍受时，人们有时也会通过更正式的渠道处理，比如向物业投诉。

entries.text: Which area is exposed to noise more, the city or the countryside?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think cities are definitely more exposed to noise than the countryside.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得城市肯定比乡村更容易受到噪音影响。

ideaNotes.label: 解释

entries.text: What kinds of noises are there in our life?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think the most common noises in daily life come from traffic, construction, and just people talking.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得日常生活中最常见的噪音来自交通、施工，还有就是人们说话。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: These are all unavoidable parts of everyday life, especially in busy areas, so people end up hearing them constantly whether they want to or not.
ideaNotes.textZh: 这些都是日常生活中不可避免的部分，尤其是在繁忙地区，所以人们不管愿不愿意都会一直听到这些声音。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, living near a main road means dealing with constant engine noise, while living close to a building site means hearing drilling or hammering almost every day.

entries.text: Should children not be allowed to make noise under any circumstances?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: No, I don't think children should be completely banned from making noise.
ideaNotes.textZh: 不，我不认为应该完全禁止孩子发出噪音。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Making noise is often just a natural part of being a child — running, laughing, playing — and forcing them to be silent all the time could actually hold back their normal development.
ideaNotes.textZh: 发出噪音往往只是孩子天性的一部分——跑、笑、玩耍——如果强迫他们一直保持安静，反而可能会阻碍他们正常的成长发育。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, a child playing at a park or laughing during a game shouldn't be told to stay quiet, since that kind of energy is a completely normal part of childhood.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，一个在公园玩耍或在游戏中大笑的孩子，不应该被要求保持安静，因为这种活力是童年很正常的一部分。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: That said, there are certain settings, like libraries or late-night apartments, where children should still be gently reminded to keep it down.
ideaNotes.textZh: 不过，在某些场合，比如图书馆或深夜的公寓里，还是应该温和地提醒孩子小声一点。

entries.text: Do you think it is good for children to make noise?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: Yes, I think it's actually a healthy sign when children make noise, at least to a certain extent.
ideaNotes.textZh: 是的，我觉得孩子发出噪音其实是一种健康的表现，至少在一定程度上是这样。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Noise like laughing or shouting during play is usually a sign of genuine excitement and engagement, and children who are too quiet or withdrawn all the time might actually be a bigger concern.
ideaNotes.textZh: 玩耍时大笑或喊叫的声音通常代表着真实的兴奋和投入，而那些总是很安静、内向的孩子，反而可能更需要关注。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, kids shouting with joy while playing tag in the yard shows they're having fun and being physically active, which is exactly what childhood should look like.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，孩子们在院子里玩捉人游戏时兴奋地大喊大叫，说明他们玩得开心，也很活跃，这正是童年应有的样子。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: Of course, there's a difference between playful noise and disruptive behavior, so parents just need to guide kids on when and where it's appropriate.
ideaNotes.textZh: 当然，玩乐时的吵闹和捣乱行为是有区别的，所以父母只需要引导孩子明白什么时候、什么场合这样做是合适的。

entries.text: Describe a crowded place you went to

paragraphs: A crowded place I've been to is a scenic spot near my home. It is a bit far from the city, about a two-hour drive, so it counts as a short trip.

Whenever relatives or friends come to visit, they always want to check out this place since it's a well-known local spot, so I end up being the one to take them there. This time was no different — some relatives of mine came to visit during a holiday, I took them there and showed them around.

We basically just walked around the old streets, popped into a few shops, and grabbed some snacks along the way. It's actually an ancient water town, done in this kind of traditional southern-China style — it's supposed to have a lot of charm.

But a lot of the old houses have been turned into, like, bubble tea shops, chain stores, and souvenir shops. The stuff inside doesn't really have any local character — you could buy the exact same things anywhere.
My relatives and I all found it pretty boring. And because it was a holiday, the place was packed — there were people everywhere, we could barely move.

At the same time, shops on both sides kept blasting loudspeakers trying to pull in customers, and with all the noise mixed together — people talking, kids crying, music blasting from different shops. I could barely stand it, I just wanted to get out of there right away.
And to make things worse, it was in all that chaos that I lost my wallet. With so many people pushing and squeezing past, I didn't even notice at the time.
I immediately retraced my steps, going back through all the shops and streets we'd walked through, but there was no sign of it. In the end, I had no choice but to report it to the police.
Luckily, the police managed to pull up the security footage and actually helped me get it back. Such a relief——otherwise I would have lost everything inside, my ID, my bank cards, all of it.
So overall, it's crowded, noisy, boring, and I even lost my wallet there. I really don't want to go back.
It's kind of sad, really — these places end up chasing quick money instead of keeping what made them special. And once that charm is gone, there's really no reason to go back.
paragraphsZh: 我去过的一个拥挤的地方，是我家附近的一个景区。 这个景区离市区有点远，开车大概要两个小时，算是一次短途旅行。
每次有亲戚朋友来玩，他们总是想来看看这个地方，因为它是一个挺有名的本地景点，所以我总是被叫去带他们过去。 这次也不例外——有几个亲戚在假期过来玩，我就带他们去逛了逛。
我们基本上就是在老街上走走，进了几家店，还顺便吃了点小吃。 这里其实是一个江南水乡古镇，是那种传统的南方水乡风格，本来应该挺有韵味的。
但很多老房子都被改成了奶茶店、连锁店和纪念品店。 里面卖的东西根本没有什么本地特色——在哪里都能买到一样的东西。
我和亲戚们都觉得挺无聊的。 而且因为是假期去的，人特别多，到处都是人，我们几乎没法动。
同时，街边的店铺还一直用喇叭招揽顾客，各种声音混在一起——聊天声、小孩哭声、不同店铺放的音乐声。 我实在受不了了，只想赶紧离开那里。
更糟糕的是，就在那片混乱中，我弄丢了我的钱包。 人群不断推挤，当时我根本没有察觉。
我立刻原路返回，重新走过之前经过的每一家店和街道，但根本找不到。 最后我不得不去报警。
幸运的是，警察调取了监控录像，帮我找回了钱包。 真是松了一口气——否则里面的东西就全没了，我的身份证、银行卡，什么都没了。
总体来说，那里拥挤、嘈杂、无聊，我甚至还在那里丢了钱包。 我真的不想再去了。
说起来也挺可惜的——这些地方最终都在追逐快钱，而不是保留原本让它们特别的东西。 一旦那种韵味消失了，真的就没有理由再回去了。

entries.text: Do you think it is a good trend to have more big cities?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I don't think it's entirely a good trend, even though big cities do offer more opportunities.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我不认为这完全是一个好趋势，尽管大城市确实提供了更多机会。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: As more people move into cities, the existing infrastructure and resources often can't keep up, and this creates problems like overcrowding that didn't exist before at that scale.
ideaNotes.textZh: 随着越来越多的人涌入城市，现有的基础设施和资源往往跟不上，这会带来一些以前没有的问题，比如过度拥挤。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, cities that grow too fast often struggle with housing shortages and packed public transport, making daily life more stressful for residents.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，发展过快的城市常常会面临住房短缺和拥挤的公共交通，让居民的日常生活变得更加有压力。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: A better trend might be developing mid-sized cities more evenly, so opportunities aren't so concentrated in just a few massive urban centers.
ideaNotes.textZh: 一个更好的趋势可能是更均衡地发展中型城市，这样机会就不会只集中在少数几个特大城市。

paragraphs: I don't think it's entirely a good trend, even though big cities do offer more opportunities.
As more people move into cities, the existing infrastructure and resources often can't keep up, and this creates problems like overcrowding that didn't exist before at that scale.
For instance, cities that grow too fast often struggle with housing shortages and packed public transport, making daily life more stressful for residents.
A better trend might be developing mid-sized cities more evenly, so opportunities aren't so concentrated in just a few massive urban centers.

随着越来越多的人涌入城市，现有的基础设施和资源往往跟不上，这会带来一些以前没有的问题，比如过度拥挤。
比如，发展过快的城市常常会面临住房短缺和拥挤的公共交通，让居民的日常生活变得更加有压力。
一个更好的趋势可能是更均衡地发展中型城市，这样机会就不会只集中在少数几个特大城市。

entries.text: Do you think there are some people who enjoy crowded places?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: Yes, I definitely think some people enjoy crowded places, even though it's not for everyone.
ideaNotes.textZh: 是的，我确实认为有些人喜欢拥挤的地方，虽然这不是每个人都喜欢的。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: For certain people, being surrounded by lots of others creates a sense of energy and excitement, and that buzzing atmosphere can actually feel comforting rather than overwhelming.
ideaNotes.textZh: 对某些人来说，被很多人围绕能带来一种活力和兴奋感，这种热闹的氛围实际上会让人感到安心，而不是不知所措。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, someone who loves festivals or concerts often thrives in a packed crowd, getting more excited the bigger and louder it gets, instead of feeling stressed.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，一个喜欢节日活动或演唱会的人，往往在拥挤的人群中反而更来劲，场面越大越吵反而让他们更兴奋，而不是感到有压力。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: This might also connect to personality — extroverts in particular tend to gain energy from being around lots of people, unlike introverts who need quiet to recharge.
ideaNotes.textZh: 这也可能和性格有关——尤其是外向的人往往能从人群中获得能量，而内向的人则需要安静的环境来恢复精力。

entries.text: Why do people go to crowded places?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think people go to crowded places mostly because those spots usually offer something worth experiencing.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得人们去拥挤的地方，主要是因为这些地方通常有一些值得体验的东西。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: A crowd is often a signal that something good is happening there, whether it's a great view, good food, or a popular event, so people are naturally drawn to follow the crowd.
ideaNotes.textZh: 人群往往是一种信号，表明那里正在发生一些好事，可能是绝美的风景、美食，或者受欢迎的活动，所以人们自然会被吸引跟随人群。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, tourists will happily stand in a long line at a famous attraction, assuming that if so many people want to see it, it must be worth the wait.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，游客会心甘情愿地在热门景点排长队，觉得既然这么多人想看，肯定值得等。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: Sometimes it's also simply about convenience — popular places tend to have better transport links and more facilities nearby, making them easier to get to.
ideaNotes.textZh: 有时候也只是出于便利性——热门的地方往往交通更便捷，周边设施也更完善，去起来更方便。

entries.text: Will people use bikes more or less in cities in the future?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think people will actually use bikes more in cities in the future, not less.

entries.text: Which cities are overcrowded in your country?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I'd say cities like Beijing and Shanghai are probably the most overcrowded in China.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得像北京和上海这样的城市大概是中国最拥挤的。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: These cities concentrate the best job opportunities, education, and healthcare, so people from all over the country keep moving there, and the population just keeps outpacing the space available.
ideaNotes.textZh: 这些城市集中了最好的就业机会、教育和医疗资源，所以全国各地的人不断涌入，人口增长速度一直超过了可用的空间。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, in Shanghai, it's common to see packed subway trains during rush hour, with people barely able to fit inside the doors.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，在上海，早晚高峰时常能看到挤满人的地铁，人们几乎挤不进车门。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: To ease this pressure, the government has been encouraging development in smaller surrounding cities, hoping to spread the population out more evenly.
ideaNotes.textZh: 为了缓解这种压力，政府一直在鼓励发展周边的小城市，希望能让人口分布更均衡一些。

entries.text: Describe a short trip you often take but do not like

paragraphs: A short trip I often take but don't really enjoy is going to a scenic spot near my home. It is a bit far from the city, about a two-hour drive, so it counts as a short trip.

Whenever relatives or friends come to visit, they always want to check out this place since it's a well-known local spot, so I end up being the one to take them there. This time was no different — some relatives of mine came to visit during a holiday, I took them there and showed them around.

We basically just walked around the old streets, popped into a few shops, and grabbed some snacks along the way. It's actually an ancient water town, done in this kind of traditional southern-China style — it's supposed to have a lot of charm.

But a lot of the old houses have been turned into, like, bubble tea shops, chain stores, and souvenir shops. The stuff inside doesn't really have any local character — you could buy the exact same things anywhere.
My relatives and I all found it pretty boring. And because it was a holiday, the place was packed — there were people everywhere, we could barely move.

At the same time, shops on both sides kept blasting loudspeakers trying to pull in customers, and with all the noise mixed together — people talking, kids crying, music blasting from different shops. I could barely stand it, I just wanted to get out of there right away.
And to make things worse, it was in all that chaos that I lost my wallet. With so many people pushing and squeezing past, I didn't even notice at the time.
I immediately retraced my steps, going back through all the shops and streets we'd walked through, but there was no sign of it. In the end, I had no choice but to report it to the police.
Luckily, the police managed to pull up the security footage and actually helped me get it back. Such a relief——otherwise I would have lost everything inside, my ID, my bank cards, all of it.
So overall, it's crowded, noisy, boring, and I even lost my wallet there. I really don't want to go back.
It's kind of sad, really — these places end up chasing quick money instead of keeping what made them special. And once that charm is gone, there's really no reason to go back.
paragraphsZh: 我经常去但不太喜欢的一次短途旅行，是去我家附近的一个景区。 这个景区离市区有点远，开车大概要两个小时，算是一次短途旅行。
每次有亲戚朋友来玩，他们总是想来看看这个地方，因为它是一个挺有名的本地景点，所以我总是被叫去带他们过去。 这次也不例外——有几个亲戚在假期过来玩，我就带他们去逛了逛。
我们基本上就是在老街上走走，进了几家店，还顺便吃了点小吃。 这里其实是一个江南水乡古镇，是那种传统的南方水乡风格，本来应该挺有韵味的。
但很多老房子都被改成了奶茶店、连锁店和纪念品店。 里面卖的东西根本没有什么本地特色——在哪里都能买到一样的东西。
我和亲戚们都觉得挺无聊的。 而且因为是假期去的，人特别多，到处都是人，我们几乎没法动。
同时，街边的店铺还一直用喇叭招揽顾客，各种声音混在一起——聊天声、小孩哭声、不同店铺放的音乐声。 我实在受不了了，只想赶紧离开那里。
更糟糕的是，就在那片混乱中，我弄丢了我的钱包。 人群不断推挤，当时我根本没有察觉。
我立刻原路返回，重新走过之前经过的每一家店和街道，但根本找不到。 最后我不得不去报警。
幸运的是，警察调取了监控录像，帮我找回了钱包。 真是松了一口气——否则里面的东西就全没了，我的身份证、银行卡，什么都没了。
总体来说，那里拥挤、嘈杂、无聊，我甚至还在那里丢了钱包。 我真的不想再去了。
说起来也挺可惜的——这些地方最终都在追逐快钱，而不是保留原本让它们特别的东西。 一旦那种韵味消失了，真的就没有理由再回去了。

entries.text: What problems does it cause for transportation when everyone commutes at the same time?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think the biggest problem is that roads and public transport become overcrowded all at once.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得最大的问题是道路和公共交通会一下子变得极度拥挤。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: When everyone travels during the same narrow window, the transportation system simply can't handle that much demand at once, so things slow down and get congested.
ideaNotes.textZh: 当所有人都在同一个狭窄的时间段出行时，交通系统根本无法一下子承受这么大的需求，于是一切都会变慢、变得拥堵。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, during rush hour, subway trains get so packed that people can barely fit inside, while roads turn into long lines of stopped cars.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，在高峰时段，地铁车厢会挤得几乎塞不下人，而道路也会变成一长串停滞不前的车。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: This kind of congestion also increases air pollution, since cars stuck in traffic keep running their engines without actually going anywhere.
ideaNotes.textZh: 这种拥堵也会加剧空气污染，因为堵在路上的汽车一直发动着引擎，却根本没往前挪动。

paragraphs: I think the biggest problem is that roads and public transport become overcrowded all at once.
When everyone travels during the same narrow window, the transportation system simply can't handle that much demand at once, so things slow down and get congested.
For instance, during rush hour, subway trains get so packed that people can barely fit inside, while roads turn into long lines of stopped cars.
This kind of congestion also increases air pollution, since cars stuck in traffic keep running their engines without actually going anywhere.
paragraphsZh: 我觉得最大的问题是道路和公共交通会一下子变得极度拥挤。
当所有人都在同一个狭窄的时间段出行时，交通系统根本无法一下子承受这么大的需求，于是一切都会变慢、变得拥堵。
比如，在高峰时段，地铁车厢会挤得几乎塞不下人，而道路也会变成一长串停滞不前的车。
这种拥堵也会加剧空气污染，因为堵在路上的汽车一直发动着引擎，却根本没往前挪动。

entries.text: What are the benefits of travelling abroad?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think the biggest benefit of travelling abroad is getting to experience different cultures firsthand.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得出国旅行最大的好处是能亲身体验不同的文化。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Seeing how people in other countries live and think differently helps break down assumptions someone might have grown up with, making their view of the world more open.
ideaNotes.textZh: 看到其他国家的人如何以不同的方式生活和思考，能帮助打破一个人从小就有的固有想法，让他们对世界的看法变得更加开放。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, someone who visits Japan might be surprised by how much emphasis is placed on punctuality and cleanliness, which could change how they see their own daily habits back home.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，一个去日本旅行的人可能会惊讶于那里对准时和整洁的重视程度，这可能会改变他们对自己国内日常习惯的看法。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: Beyond cultural exposure, travelling abroad can also improve someone's language skills, since being surrounded by a foreign language forces real, practical communication.
ideaNotes.textZh: 除了文化体验之外，出国旅行也能提升一个人的语言能力，因为身处外语环境会迫使人进行真实、实际的交流。

entries.text: How much time do you think people should spend on a trip abroad?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think one to two weeks is generally a good amount of time to spend on a trip abroad.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得一到两周通常是出国旅行比较合适的时长。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: A trip that's too short doesn't leave enough time to really settle into a place beyond the main tourist spots, but a trip that's too long can start to feel exhausting, since constantly moving and exploring is actually quite tiring over time.
ideaNotes.textZh: 太短的行程没有足够时间真正深入体验一个地方，而不只是打卡主要景点，但太长的行程也会开始让人觉得疲惫，因为长期不停地移动、探索其实相当累人。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, a three-day trip might only allow time for the top landmarks, while a month-long trip without any rest days could leave a traveler feeling burnt out by the end, wanting nothing more than to go home.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，一次三天的旅行可能只够去几个热门地标打卡，而一次长达一个月、中间完全没有休息日的旅行，到最后可能会让旅行者感到精疲力竭，只想赶紧回家。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: That said, the ideal length really depends on the destination — a small country might only need a few days, while a large one could take weeks to properly explore.
ideaNotes.textZh: 不过，理想的时长其实取决于目的地——一个小国可能只需要几天，而一个大国可能要花好几周才能真正探索完。

entries.text: Do Chinese people like travelling abroad?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: Yes, I think a growing number of Chinese people enjoy travelling abroad, especially compared to a couple of decades ago.
ideaNotes.textZh: 是的，我觉得越来越多中国人喜欢出国旅行，尤其是和二十年前相比。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: As people's income levels have risen and it's become easier to get a passport or visa, international travel has shifted from being a luxury to something much more accessible for ordinary families.
ideaNotes.textZh: 随着人们的收入水平提高，办理护照和签证也变得更容易，出国旅行已经从一种奢侈行为变成了普通家庭更容易负担得起的事情。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, destinations like Thailand or Japan have become extremely popular among Chinese tourists, especially during holidays like Chinese New Year.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，像泰国或日本这样的目的地，在中国游客中变得非常受欢迎，尤其是在春节这样的假期期间。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: That said, some people still prefer travelling within China, since the country itself already offers such a wide variety of landscapes and cultures to explore.
ideaNotes.textZh: 不过，也有些人仍然更喜欢在国内旅行，因为中国本身就已经拥有非常多样的自然风光和文化可以探索。

For instance, destinations like Thailand or Japan have become extremely popular among Chinese tourists, especially during holidays like Chinese New Year.
That said, some people still prefer travelling within China, since the country itself already offers such a wide variety of landscapes and cultures to explore.

比如，像泰国或日本这样的目的地，在中国游客中变得非常受欢迎，尤其是在春节这样的假期期间。
不过，也有些人仍然更喜欢在国内旅行，因为中国本身就已经拥有非常多样的自然风光和文化可以探索。

entries.text: Describe a boring place

paragraphs: A place I find pretty boring is a scenic spot near my home. It is a bit far from the city, about a two-hour drive, so it counts as a short trip.

Whenever relatives or friends come to visit, they always want to check out this place since it's a well-known local spot, so I end up being the one to take them there. This time was no different — some relatives of mine came to visit during a holiday, I took them there and showed them around.

We basically just walked around the old streets, popped into a few shops, and grabbed some snacks along the way. It's actually an ancient water town, done in this kind of traditional southern-China style — it's supposed to have a lot of charm.

But a lot of the old houses have been turned into, like, bubble tea shops, chain stores, and souvenir shops. The stuff inside doesn't really have any local character — you could buy the exact same things anywhere.
My relatives and I all found it pretty boring. And because it was a holiday, the place was packed — there were people everywhere, we could barely move.

At the same time, shops on both sides kept blasting loudspeakers trying to pull in customers, and with all the noise mixed together — people talking, kids crying, music blasting from different shops. I could barely stand it, I just wanted to get out of there right away.
And to make things worse, it was in all that chaos that I lost my wallet. With so many people pushing and squeezing past, I didn't even notice at the time.
I immediately retraced my steps, going back through all the shops and streets we'd walked through, but there was no sign of it. In the end, I had no choice but to report it to the police.
Luckily, the police managed to pull up the security footage and actually helped me get it back. Such a relief——otherwise I would have lost everything inside, my ID, my bank cards, all of it.
So overall, it's crowded, noisy, boring, and I even lost my wallet there. I really don't want to go back.
It's kind of sad, really — these places end up chasing quick money instead of keeping what made them special. And once that charm is gone, there's really no reason to go back.
paragraphsZh: 一个我觉得很无聊的地方，是我家附近的一个景区。 这个景区离市区有点远，开车大概要两个小时，算是一次短途旅行。
每次有亲戚朋友来玩，他们总是想来看看这个地方，因为它是一个挺有名的本地景点，所以我总是被叫去带他们过去。 这次也不例外——有几个亲戚在假期过来玩，我就带他们去逛了逛。
我们基本上就是在老街上走走，进了几家店，还顺便吃了点小吃。 这里其实是一个江南水乡古镇，是那种传统的南方水乡风格，本来应该挺有韵味的。
但很多老房子都被改成了奶茶店、连锁店和纪念品店。 里面卖的东西根本没有什么本地特色——在哪里都能买到一样的东西。
我和亲戚们都觉得挺无聊的。 而且因为是假期去的，人特别多，到处都是人，我们几乎没法动。
同时，街边的店铺还一直用喇叭招揽顾客，各种声音混在一起——聊天声、小孩哭声、不同店铺放的音乐声。 我实在受不了了，只想赶紧离开那里。
更糟糕的是，就在那片混乱中，我弄丢了我的钱包。 人群不断推挤，当时我根本没有察觉。
我立刻原路返回，重新走过之前经过的每一家店和街道，但根本找不到。 最后我不得不去报警。
幸运的是，警察调取了监控录像，帮我找回了钱包。 真是松了一口气——否则里面的东西就全没了，我的身份证、银行卡，什么都没了。
总体来说，那里拥挤、嘈杂、无聊，我甚至还在那里丢了钱包。 我真的不想再去了。
说起来也挺可惜的——这些地方最终都在追逐快钱，而不是保留原本让它们特别的东西。 一旦那种韵味消失了，真的就没有理由再回去了。

entries.text: Why do most children think education is boring?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think the main reason is that the way children are taught is often too rigid and one-sided — it's mostly just a teacher talking at them rather than actually getting them involved.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我认为主要原因是教孩子的方式往往太死板和单向，大多数时候只是老师在对他们讲话，而不是真正让他们参与进来。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: I mean, kids naturally love to play, explore, and discover things on their own, but school often forces them to just sit still, memorise facts, and do the same thing over and over again. After a while that just feels really dull and pointless to them.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我的意思是，孩子天生喜欢玩耍、探索和自己发现事物，但学校往往强迫他们只是坐着不动、死记硬背、反复做同样的事情。时间长了，这对他们来说感觉真的很枯燥和没有意义。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For example, I remember in primary school I used to love science until it became all about copying notes and remembering formulas for tests — the fun completely disappeared once it stopped feeling like discovery and started feeling like work.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，我记得在小学时我曾经很喜欢科学，直到它变成了全是抄笔记和记忆公式来应付考试，一旦它不再感觉像探索而开始感觉像工作，乐趣就完全消失了。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸
ideaNotes.textZh: 可选】 Also, a lot of children find it hard to stay focused when they can't see why any of it matters to their real life — if a subject feels completely disconnected from the real world, it's really hard to care about it. 另外，很多孩子发现当他们看不到这些内容与现实生活有什么关系时很难保持专注，如果一个科目感觉与现实世界完全脱节，就真的很难对它感兴趣。

entries.text: Why aren’t young people willing to listen to the experiences of older people?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think the main reason is that young people feel the world has changed so much that the advice from older people just doesn't feel relevant anymore.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我认为主要原因是年轻人觉得世界已经变化太大，老年人的建议感觉不再适用了。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Well, older people grew up in a completely different era — different job markets, different technology, different social rules — so when they give advice it often sounds like it's based on a world that no longer exists. Young people hear that and just think — that doesn't apply to my situation.
ideaNotes.textZh: 嗯，老年人是在一个完全不同的时代长大的，不同的就业市场、不同的技术、不同的社会规则，所以当他们给出建议时，听起来往往像是基于一个已经不存在的世界。年轻人听到这些就会想，这不适用于我的情况。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, when my parents tell me to just walk into a company and hand in a CV to get a job, I know they mean well but that's just not how hiring works anymore — everything is online now and that kind of advice feels really out of touch.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，当我父母告诉我只要走进一家公司递交简历就能找到工作时，我知道他们是好意，但这已经不是现在招聘的方式了，现在一切都在网上，这种建议感觉真的脱离实际。• 转折【可选】 However, I do think young people sometimes miss out because of this attitude — some things like handling failure, being patient, and building real relationships never really change, and older people actually have a lot of wisdom in those areas. 然而，我确实认为年轻人有时因为这种态度而错失良机，一些事情比如应对失败、保持耐心和建立真实的关系从未真正改变，老年人在这些方面实际上有很多智慧。📢 语音跟读202.mp3

entries.text: What can people do when they feel bored?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think when people feel bored, the best thing they can do is use that time to try something new and different rather than just scrolling on their phone.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我认为当人们感到无聊时，最好的事情是利用那段时间尝试一些新的不同的事情，而不是只是刷手机。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Honestly, boredom is actually a sign that your brain needs something to engage with, and if you just fill that gap with social media you never really deal with it. But if you pick up a new hobby or activity, you end up feeling much more satisfied and energised.
ideaNotes.textZh: 说实话，无聊实际上是你的大脑需要某些东西来投入的信号，如果你只是用社交媒体填补那个空白，你从未真正解决它。但如果你开始一个新的爱好或活动，你最终会感到更加满足和充满活力。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: Like, I used to reach for my phone every time I felt bored, but then I started going for walks or cooking something new, and honestly those things made me feel so much better than mindlessly watching videos ever did.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，我以前每次感到无聊就拿起手机，但后来我开始出去散步或尝试做新菜，说实话这些事情让我感觉比无意识地看视频好多了。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸
ideaNotes.textZh: 可选】 Plus, sometimes just sitting with the boredom for a bit is actually really good for you — it gives your mind a chance to rest and wander, and a lot of people find that's actually when their best ideas come to them. 而且，有时候只是坐着感受无聊一会儿实际上对你真的很有好处，它给你的思维一个休息和漫游的机会，很多人发现那实际上是他们最好的想法出现的时候。

entries.text: Why do some young people feel bored when talking with old people?

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Young people are usually interested in things like social media, new trends, games, and current pop culture, while older people tend to talk about things from the past, health, or topics that feel quite distant from a young person's daily life. When the conversation keeps going back to things you have no connection to, it's natural to start zoning out or losing interest.
ideaNotes.textZh: 年轻人通常对社交媒体、新趋势、游戏和当前流行文化感兴趣，而老年人倾向于谈论过去的事情、健康或感觉与年轻人日常生活相当遥远的话题。当对话不断回到你没有联系的事情时，自然会开始走神或失去兴趣。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, I love my grandparents but sometimes when they start talking about things that happened decades ago or give long advice about life, I find it hard to stay engaged — not because I don't care about them, but because I just can't relate to what they're saying.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，我很爱我的祖父母，但有时当他们开始谈论几十年前发生的事情或给出长篇人生建议时，我发现很难保持投入，不是因为我不关心他们，而是因为我无法理解他们说的话。• 转折【可选】 Even so, I think young people who make the effort to really listen and ask questions often end up finding the conversation much more interesting than they expected — older people have a lot of real stories and wisdom that you genuinely can't get anywhere else. 即便如此，我认为那些努力真正倾听和提问的年轻人往往发现对话比他们预期的有趣得多，老年人有很多真实的故事和智慧，是你真的无法从其他地方获得的。

entries.text: Do most people think news about celebrities is boring?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I don't think most people find it boring — actually a lot of people are genuinely interested in celebrity news, even if they wouldn't always admit it.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我不认为大多数人觉得它无聊，实际上很多人对名人新闻真正感兴趣，即使他们不总是会承认。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Celebrity news gives people something light and entertaining to follow — it's easy to consume, doesn't require much thinking, and feels like a fun escape from everyday stress. That's why it gets so many clicks and views. But at the same time, some people do get tired of it, especially when it dominates the news and pushes out more serious and important stories about things that actually affect people's lives.
ideaNotes.textZh: 名人新闻给人们提供了一些轻松有趣的内容，它容易消化，不需要太多思考，感觉像是从日常压力中有趣地逃脱。这就是为什么它获得如此多的点击和浏览量。但同时，一些人确实对它感到厌倦，尤其是当它主导新闻，把更严肃和重要的、真正影响人们生活的故事挤出去的时候。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, I notice that whenever something happens involving a famous actor or singer, it immediately floods social media and everyone starts talking about it — which shows that a huge number of people are clearly paying attention and not finding it boring at all. But I also have friends who actively avoid that kind of content because they find it pointless and would rather read about real world events.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，我注意到每当涉及著名演员或歌手的事情发生时，它立即充斥社交媒体，每个人都开始谈论它，这表明大量人在关注，完全不觉得无聊。但我也有朋友主动回避那类内容，因为他们觉得毫无意义，宁愿阅读真实世界的事件。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸
ideaNotes.textZh: 可选】 And also, I think it depends on who the celebrity is — news about someone you genuinely admire or follow feels exciting and personal, while news about a celebrity you've never heard of feels completely irrelevant and easy to ignore. 另外，我认为这取决于名人是谁，关于你真正钦佩或关注的人的新闻感觉令人兴奋且有个人感，而关于你从未听说过的名人的新闻感觉完全无关紧要且容易忽视。

keyPhrases.phrase: Light and entertaining easy fun escape
Famous actor singer floods social media paying attention
Avoid that kind of content pointless real world events

paragraphs: I don't think most people find it boring — actually a lot of people are genuinely interested in celebrity news, even if they wouldn't always admit it.

Celebrity news gives people something light and entertaining to follow — it's easy to consume, doesn't require much thinking, and feels like a fun escape from everyday stress. That's why it gets so many clicks and views. But at the same time, some people do get tired of it, especially when it dominates the news and pushes out more serious and important stories about things that actually affect people's lives.

For instance, I notice that whenever something happens involving a famous actor or singer, it immediately floods social media and everyone starts talking about it — which shows that a huge number of people are clearly paying attention and not finding it boring at all. But I also have friends who actively avoid that kind of content because they find it pointless and would rather read about real world events.
paragraphsZh: 我不认为大多数人觉得它无聊，实际上很多人对名人新闻真正感兴趣，即使他们不总是会承认。
名人新闻给人们提供了一些轻松有趣的内容，它容易消化，不需要太多思考，感觉像是从日常压力中有趣地逃脱。这就是为什么它获得如此多的点击和浏览量。但同时，一些人确实对它感到厌倦，尤其是当它主导新闻，把更严肃和重要的、真正影响人们生活的故事挤出去的时候。
例如，我注意到每当涉及著名演员或歌手的事情发生时，它立即充斥社交媒体，每个人都开始谈论它，这表明大量人在关注，完全不觉得无聊。但我也有朋友主动回避那类内容，因为他们觉得毫无意义，宁愿阅读真实世界的事件。

可选】 And also, I think it depends on who the celebrity is — news about someone you genuinely admire or follow feels exciting and personal, while news about a celebrity you've never heard of feels completely irrelevant and easy to ignore. 另外，我认为这取决于名人是谁，关于你真正钦佩或关注的人的新闻感觉令人兴奋且有个人感，而关于你从未听说过的名人的新闻感觉完全无关紧要且容易忽视。

entries.text: Describe a time when you received good service in a shop/store

paragraphs: A time I received really good service in a shop was actually during a trip to Chengdu. Chengdu is located in southwest China, in Sichuan Province.
I first heard about it from a friend. She kept telling me the food and culture there were really amazing, so I decided to check it out myself.

I went there last month and stayed for three days. Once I got to Chengdu, I went straight to the famous Giant Panda Research Base — there were so many adorable pandas there, some just lying around, others climbing trees.

Then I tried Chengdu's famous hotpot — it was spicy, but in a really good way, and everything from the meat to the vegetables soaked up all that flavour. I also heard that Sichuan is famous for its tea, so on my second day, I went to a really well-known local tea shop — it's in an old residential area, and it's the kind of place locals often go to buy tea.
The staff member there was really patient and friendly. She told me about the differences between different types of tea, and invited me to try a few of them.
She even offered me a small discount at the end. The whole process felt really enjoyable, not rushed at all, and I ended up leaving with a few boxes of really nice tea.

From the wildlife to the food to the people, everything about Chengdu just felt super slow-paced and easy-going — which is totally different from most busy cities I've been to. I really want to go back there — and this time, I'd love to stay for a whole week instead of just three days, to really explore more of its scenery and culture, and meet more people there.
This is a place I'd recommend to others — I think everyone would have a great time there.
paragraphsZh: 我一次收到很好的服务的经历，其实就发生在去成都旅行的时候。 成都位于中国西南部，四川省。
我第一次听说这个地方是从一个朋友那里，她一直跟我说那里的美食和文化特别棒，所以我决定自己去看看。 我上个月去的，待了三天。
一到成都，我就直接去了著名的大熊猫研究基地——那里有好多可爱的熊猫，有的就趴着，有的慢慢地爬树。 然后我尝了成都著名的火锅——很辣，但是那种很好吃的辣，从肉到蔬菜，每样东西都吸满了味道。
我还听说四川的茶很有名，所以第二天，我去了一家挺有名的本地茶叶店——它在一个老居民区里，是那种本地人经常去买茶的地方。 店员特别耐心、特别热情。
她跟我讲了不同茶的种类之间的区别，还邀请我试喝了几种。 最后她还给了我一点优惠。
整个过程感觉特别愉快，一点也不赶，最后我带走了好几盒特别不错的茶叶。 从野生动物到美食再到人，成都给我的感觉特别悠闲、特别自在——跟我去过的大多数繁忙的城市完全不一样。
我真的很想再去一次——这次我想待上一整周，而不只是三天，好好再多探索一下那里的风景和文化，认识更多当地人。 这是一个我会推荐给别人的地方——我觉得每个人在那里都会玩得很开心。

entries.text: Can consumption drive economic growth?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: Yes, I think consumption can definitely drive economic growth, since it's one of the main forces keeping the economy moving.
ideaNotes.textZh: 是的，我认为消费确实能推动经济增长，因为它是维持经济运转的主要动力之一。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: When people spend more, businesses see higher demand, so they need to produce more, hire more staff, and invest more, and this chain reaction keeps the whole economy active.
ideaNotes.textZh: 当人们花钱更多时，企业会看到更高的需求，于是需要生产更多、雇佣更多员工、投入更多资金，这一连串反应会让整个经济保持活跃。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, during big shopping events like Double Eleven, sales surge so much that factories increase production and delivery companies hire extra workers just to keep up.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，在双十一这样的购物活动期间，销量激增，工厂会增加生产，快递公司也会雇佣额外的员工来应付需求。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: That said, consumption alone isn't enough — if people spend without saving, it can also lead to financial instability down the line.
ideaNotes.textZh: 不过，光靠消费还不够——如果人们只花不存，长期下去也可能导致经济不稳定。

entries.text: What are the advantages and disadvantages of shopping online?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think the main advantage of shopping online is the convenience, while the biggest disadvantage is not being able to check the product in person.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得网购最大的优点是方便，而最大的缺点是无法亲自检查商品。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Online shopping lets people buy anything from home at any time, but without seeing or touching the item first, there's always a risk that it doesn't match expectations once it arrives.
ideaNotes.textZh: 网购能让人们随时在家买到任何东西，但因为无法事先看到或摸到商品，收到货后总有可能出现和预期不符的情况。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, buying a pair of shoes online without trying them on can easily result in a size that's too tight or a fit that just feels off, something you'd immediately catch in a physical store.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，在网上买鞋子，没有试穿就直接下单，很容易出现尺码太紧或者穿起来感觉不对的情况，而这种问题在实体店里能立刻发现。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: On top of that, online shopping also makes it too easy to overspend, since browsing endless products with just a swipe can lead to impulse buying.
ideaNotes.textZh: 除此之外，网购也会让人很容易过度消费，因为只需滑动屏幕就能浏览无穷无尽的商品，容易导致冲动购物。

entries.text: What are the differences between online shopping and in-store shopping?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think the main difference is that online shopping focuses on efficiency, while in-store shopping focuses on experience.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得主要区别在于网购注重效率，而实体店购物更注重体验。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Buying online means you can compare and purchase quickly without leaving your seat, but shopping in a physical store lets you see, touch, and try things before deciding, which online simply can't offer.
ideaNotes.textZh: 网购意味着不用离开座位就能快速比较和购买，而实体店购物能让你在决定之前看到、摸到、试用商品，这是网购没法提供的。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, buying shoes online only takes a minute, but you're just guessing the size, while buying the same shoes in a store takes longer, but you get to try them on and make sure they actually fit.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，网上买鞋子只需要一分钟，但你只能靠猜尺码，而在实体店买同一双鞋会花更长时间，但能试穿，确保真的合脚。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: In-store shopping also offers something online can't — instant gratification, since you walk out with the product right away instead of waiting for delivery.
ideaNotes.textZh: 实体店购物还有一点是网购给不了的——即时满足感，因为你可以马上拿着商品走出店门，而不用等快递。

entries.text: Why do some people not like shopping in small shops?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think some people dislike small shops mainly because of limited choices and often higher prices.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得有些人不喜欢小商店，主要是因为选择有限，而且价格往往更高。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Small shops usually have less inventory space, so they can't stock as many options as bigger stores, and because they can't buy in bulk, their prices tend to be less competitive.
ideaNotes.textZh: 小商店通常库存空间有限，所以没办法像大商店那样储备那么多选择，而且因为不能大量批发，价格往往没那么有竞争力。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, a small local shop might only carry one brand of a certain product at a higher price, while a large supermarket offers multiple brands to compare and choose the cheapest.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，一家小商店可能只卖一个牌子的某种商品，而且价格更高，而大型超市能提供多个品牌供人比较、选最便宜的。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: That said, some people actually prefer small shops for the personal service, since owners often remember regular customers and treat them more warmly.
ideaNotes.textZh: 不过，也有人反而更喜欢小商店，因为那里的个人化服务更好，店主常常会记得老顾客，对待他们也更热情。

ideaNotes.label: 观点

entries.text: Why are shopping malls so popular in China?

ideaNotes.text: I think shopping malls are so popular in China mainly because they offer a one-stop experience for both shopping and entertainment.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得购物中心在中国这么受欢迎，主要是因为它们提供了购物和娱乐一站式的体验。

ideaNotes.text: Instead of just selling products, malls combine shops, restaurants, and entertainment all in one place, so people can spend an entire day there without needing to go anywhere else.

entries.text: Describe a place you have travelled to that you would like to recommend to others

paragraphs: The place I'd like to recommend is Chengdu. Chengdu is located in southwest China, in Sichuan Province.
I first heard about it from a friend. She kept telling me the food and culture there were really amazing, so I decided to check it out myself.

I went there last month and stayed for three days. Once I got to Chengdu, I went straight to the famous Giant Panda Research Base — there were so many adorable pandas there, some just lying around, others climbing trees.

Then I tried Chengdu's famous hotpot — it was spicy, but in a really good way, and everything from the meat to the vegetables soaked up all that flavour. I also heard that Sichuan is famous for its tea, so on my second day, I went to a really well-known local tea shop — it's in an old residential area, and it's the kind of place locals often go to buy tea.
The staff member there was really patient and friendly. She told me about the differences between different types of tea, and invited me to try a few of them.
She even offered me a small discount at the end. The whole process felt really enjoyable, not rushed at all, and I ended up leaving with a few boxes of really nice tea.

From the wildlife to the food to the people, everything about Chengdu just felt super slow-paced and easy-going — which is totally different from most busy cities I've been to. I really want to go back there — and this time, I'd love to stay for a whole week instead of just three days, to really explore more of its scenery and culture, and meet more people there.
This is a place I'd recommend to others — I think everyone would have a great time there.
paragraphsZh: 我想推荐的地方是成都。 成都位于中国西南部，四川省。
我第一次听说这个地方是从一个朋友那里，她一直跟我说那里的美食和文化特别棒，所以我决定自己去看看。 我上个月去的，待了三天。
一到成都，我就直接去了著名的大熊猫研究基地——那里有好多可爱的熊猫，有的就趴着，有的慢慢地爬树。 然后我尝了成都著名的火锅——很辣，但是那种很好吃的辣，从肉到蔬菜，每样东西都吸满了味道。
我还听说四川的茶很有名，所以第二天，我去了一家挺有名的本地茶叶店——它在一个老居民区里，是那种本地人经常去买茶的地方。 店员特别耐心、特别热情。
她跟我讲了不同茶的种类之间的区别，还邀请我试喝了几种。 最后她还给了我一点优惠。
整个过程感觉特别愉快，一点也不赶，最后我带走了好几盒特别不错的茶叶。 从野生动物到美食再到人，成都给我的感觉特别悠闲、特别自在——跟我去过的大多数繁忙的城市完全不一样。
我真的很想再去一次——这次我想待上一整周，而不只是三天，好好再多探索一下那里的风景和文化，认识更多当地人。 这是一个我会推荐给别人的地方——我觉得每个人在那里都会玩得很开心。

entries.text: Where do people in your country often go for holidays?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think people in China tend to go to either famous scenic spots within the country or popular destinations abroad like Japan, Thailand, or Europe.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我认为中国人倾向于去国内的著名景点或者热门的海外目的地，比如日本、泰国或欧洲。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Basically, for people who don't want to deal with visas and long flights, there are already so many beautiful places within China itself — mountains, ancient towns, beaches — that you could spend a lifetime exploring. But for younger people especially, going overseas feels exciting and like a real adventure.
ideaNotes.textZh: 基本上，对于不想处理签证和长途飞行的人来说，中国本身已经有很多美丽的地方——山脉、古镇、海滩——你可以花一辈子去探索。但尤其对年轻人来说，去海外感觉很刺激，像是一次真正的冒险。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: Like, every national holiday you see people flooding into places like Zhangjiajie, Chengdu, or Sanya, and the crowds are absolutely massive. My family once went to Hainan during Golden Week and the beach was so packed we could barely find a spot to sit.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，每个国家假日你都会看到人们涌入张家界、成都或三亚等地，人群绝对是超级多。我家人曾经在黄金周去海南，海滩上人太多了，我们几乎找不到地方坐。

entries.text: Where do young people in your country often go for holidays?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think young people in China these days tend to go for places that are either really visually stunning or somewhere that feels fresh and different from their everyday life.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我认为如今中国年轻人倾向于去那些视觉上非常震撼或者感觉与日常生活新鲜不同的地方。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: After all, for a lot of young people, holidays are not just about resting — they also want to post great photos, try local food, and have stories to talk about when they get back. So places that are photogenic or have a strong local vibe tend to be really popular.
ideaNotes.textZh: 毕竟，对很多年轻人来说，假期不仅仅是休息，他们还想发好看的照片、尝试当地美食，回来后有故事可以分享。所以那些上镜或者有浓厚地方氛围的地方往往非常受欢迎。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, places like Chengdu, Xiamen, and Dali have become incredibly popular with young travellers because they have this laid-back vibe, cute cafes that make for great content.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，成都、厦门和大理等地在年轻旅行者中变得非常受欢迎，因为它们有一种悠闲的氛围、可爱的咖啡馆，能拍出很好的内容。

entries.text: What is the ideal length for a holiday?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think around one week is probably the ideal length for a holiday — long enough to actually relax and explore, but not so long that you start missing home.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我认为大约一周可能是度假的理想时长，足够放松和探索，但又不会长到开始想家。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Well, a short trip of just two or three days often feels really rushed — you spend half the time travelling and barely get to settle in before it's time to leave. But if a holiday goes on for too long, most people start to lose that excited feeling and just want to get back to their routine.
ideaNotes.textZh: 嗯，只有两三天的短途旅行往往感觉非常匆忙，你花了一半时间在路上，还没来得及安顿下来就要离开了。但如果假期太长，大多数人开始失去那种兴奋感，只想回到日常生活。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: I remember once I took a ten-day trip and by the last few days I was honestly just tired of eating out and sleeping in hotels — I just wanted my own bed and my own home-cooked food.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我记得有一次我去了十天，到最后几天我说实话已经厌倦了外出就餐和住酒店，只想要自己的床和自己的家常菜。• 转折【可选】 However, it really depends on the person — some people love long slow travel where they stay in one place for weeks and really soak up the culture, and for them a week would feel way too short. 然而，这真的因人而异，有些人喜欢长时间慢旅行，在一个地方待上几周，真正融入当地文化，对他们来说一周可能感觉太短了。

entries.text: How do people usually plan holidays?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think most people these days plan their holidays by going online and looking things up on social media, travel apps, and review platforms before deciding anything.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我认为如今大多数人通过上网，在社交媒体、旅行应用和点评平台上查找信息来规划假期。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: I mean, nobody really asks a travel agent anymore or just shows up somewhere without doing research first. People want to know exactly what to expect — the best places to eat, where to stay, how to get around — and all of that is just a few clicks away now.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我的意思是，现在没有人真的去问旅行社，或者不做任何研究就直接出发。人们想确切地知道会遇到什么，最好的餐厅、住宿地点、如何四处走动，而这一切现在只需几次点击就能找到。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: Like, whenever I plan a trip I always start by searching on Xiaohongshu or watching travel vlogs on Bilibili to get a feel for the place, and then I book everything through apps like Ctrip or Airbnb.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，每当我计划旅行时，我总是先在小红书上搜索或在B站看旅行视频来了解当地情况，然后通过携程或Airbnb等应用预订一切。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸
ideaNotes.textZh: 可选】 Not only that, a lot of people also ask friends who have already been there for recommendations, because hearing from someone you actually trust feels much more reliable than just reading random reviews online. 不仅如此，很多人还会向去过那里的朋友寻求建议，因为听取你真正信任的人的意见比只看网上的随机评论感觉可靠得多。

entries.text: Is it important to plan a holiday ahead?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think planning ahead is pretty important, especially if you want to make the most of your time and avoid unnecessary stress while you're away.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我认为提前计划相当重要，尤其是如果你想充分利用时间，避免在外出时产生不必要的压力。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: After all, things like flights, hotels, and popular attractions can get fully booked really quickly, and if you leave everything to the last minute you either end up paying way more than you should or missing out on the things you actually wanted to do.
ideaNotes.textZh: 毕竟，机票、酒店和热门景点可能很快就会订满，如果你把所有事情都留到最后一刻，你要么最终花了远超应该的钱，要么错过你真正想做的事情。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, I once tried to book a trip to Zhangjiajie just a week before a national holiday and basically everything was either sold out or three times the normal price — it was a complete disaster.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，我曾经在国家假日前一周才尝试预订张家界的行程，基本上所有东西要么售罄，要么是正常价格的三倍，简直是一场灾难。• 转折【可选】 That said, I don't think you need to plan every single detail — leaving a bit of room to wander and be spontaneous is actually what makes a holiday feel like a real break from routine, rather than just another schedule to follow. 话虽如此，我不认为你需要计划每一个细节，留一些随意漫步和随性而为的空间，实际上才是让假期感觉像是真正从日常中解脱出来的原因，而不是只是另一个需要遵循的行程。

entries.text: Why do many countries try to attract people to visit?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think the main reason is money — tourism brings in a huge amount of income and creates jobs, which is really valuable for a country's economy.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我认为主要原因是钱，旅游业带来大量收入并创造就业机会，这对一个国家的经济非常有价值。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: When tourists visit, they spend money on hotels, food, transport, and shopping, and all of that flows into the local economy. For some countries, especially smaller ones without many other industries, tourism is actually one of their biggest sources of income. But beyond money, attracting visitors also helps a country build its image and reputation on the world stage, which can lead to other benefits like stronger trade relationships.
ideaNotes.textZh: 当游客来访时，他们在酒店、食物、交通和购物上花钱，所有这些都流入当地经济。对一些国家来说，尤其是没有太多其他产业的较小国家，旅游业实际上是他们最大的收入来源之一。但除了金钱，吸引游客也帮助一个国家在世界舞台上建立形象和声誉，这可以带来其他好处，比如更强的贸易关系。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, a country like Thailand relies heavily on tourism — millions of visitors come every year and the money they spend keeps a huge number of local businesses and families going. Without tourists, a lot of those hotels, restaurants, and tour operators would simply not survive.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，像泰国这样的国家严重依赖旅游业，每年数百万游客前来，他们花的钱维持着大量当地企业和家庭的生计。没有游客，很多酒店、餐厅和旅行社根本无法生存。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸
ideaNotes.textZh: 可选】 And also, tourism helps countries share their culture with the world — when people visit and experience local food, history, and traditions, it creates a kind of connection and understanding between different nations that is hard to achieve any other way. 另外，旅游帮助国家与世界分享文化，当人们来访并体验当地食物、历史和传统时，它在不同国家之间创造了一种难以通过其他方式实现的联系和理解。

paragraphs: I think the main reason is money — tourism brings in a huge amount of income and creates jobs, which is really valuable for a country's economy.

When tourists visit, they spend money on hotels, food, transport, and shopping, and all of that flows into the local economy. For some countries, especially smaller ones without many other industries, tourism is actually one of their biggest sources of income. But beyond money, attracting visitors also helps a country build its image and reputation on the world stage, which can lead to other benefits like stronger trade relationships.

For instance, a country like Thailand relies heavily on tourism — millions of visitors come every year and the money they spend keeps a huge number of local businesses and families going. Without tourists, a lot of those hotels, restaurants, and tour operators would simply not survive.
paragraphsZh: 我认为主要原因是钱，旅游业带来大量收入并创造就业机会，这对一个国家的经济非常有价值。

例如，像泰国这样的国家严重依赖旅游业，每年数百万游客前来，他们花的钱维持着大量当地企业和家庭的生计。没有游客，很多酒店、餐厅和旅行社根本无法生存。

entries.text: How do people decide when to travel?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think most people decide when to travel based on two main things — when they're free and what the weather is like at the destination.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我认为大多数人根据两个主要因素决定何时旅行，什么时候有空以及目的地的天气如何。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: For most people, travel happens around public holidays, school breaks, or annual leave because those are the only windows they have. Within those times, people then look at factors like weather, peak season pricing, and how crowded the place will be — most people want good weather but also don't want to pay a fortune or be surrounded by massive crowds.
ideaNotes.textZh: 对大多数人来说，旅行发生在公共假日、学校假期或年假前后，因为那是他们仅有的时间窗口。在这些时间内，人们然后考虑天气、旺季价格以及地方会有多拥挤等因素，大多数人想要好天气，但也不想花大钱或被大量人群包围。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, my family always tries to avoid Golden Week when planning trips inside China because everywhere is absolutely packed and prices go through the roof — we'd rather take time off at a less popular time and have a much more relaxed and affordable experience.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，我家在计划中国境内旅行时总是尽量避开黄金周，因为到处都人满为患，价格也飙升，我们宁愿在不那么热门的时间休假，获得更加轻松实惠的体验。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸
ideaNotes.textZh: 可选】 And also, some people now deliberately choose to travel in the off-season — the weather might not be perfect, but the prices are lower, there are fewer tourists, and you often get a much more genuine and local experience than you would during peak times. 另外，一些人现在刻意选择在淡季旅行，天气可能不完美，但价格更低，游客更少，你往往能获得比旺季更真实的本地体验。

entries.text: Describe a natural place in your city that you enjoy visiting

paragraphs: The place I'd like to talk about is my grandparents' house — it's on the outskirts of my city, surrounded by open fields. Their home is a typical Chinese village house with a few rooms built around a small courtyard.
My parents and I go back almost every month. There's something about that place I really love — it's just so different from the city.

I mean, city life can be really overwhelming sometimes — the constant noise, the car fumes. And most importantly, there's always so much pressure from work/school — every single day there's a long list of things to get through.
But the moment I get to my grandparents' place, all of that just fades away. It's so quiet — just birds chirping and the wind.
The air smells so clean and fresh. I can just sit in the courtyard and do nothing for a while.

Sometimes I'd help my grandma in the garden — everything we eat there is grown right there — fresh, natural, no additives. It just gives you that real, hands-on connection with nature that you can never get in the city.
But as much as I love visiting, I don't think I could live there long term. Since it's on the outskirts, entertainment is pretty limited — no shopping malls, no cinemas.
Besides, the houses are old and the living conditions are quite basic. The bad internet connection and lack of public transport also make daily life a bit of a hassle.

I think for a short visit it's perfect, but for everyday life I really need the energy and convenience of the city. So overall, my grandparents' place is somewhere I really treasure — being there just reconnects me with nature in a way that city life never can.
I'd love to keep going back as often as I can.
paragraphsZh: 我想说的这个地方是我爷爷奶奶的家——它在我所在城市的郊区，周围都是开阔的田野。 他们家是一座典型的中国农村房子，几间屋子围绕着一个小院子建成。
我和爸爸妈妈几乎每个月都会回去一次。 我真的很喜欢那个地方——它和城市完全不同。
城市生活有时真的让人感到很压抑——到处都是噪音，还有汽车尾气。 最重要的是，工作/学习的压力总是如影随形——每天都有一长串事情要处理。
但是一到爷爷奶奶家，这一切就全部消失了。 那里非常安静——只有鸟叫声和风声。
空气闻起来那么清新。 我可以就坐在院子里，什么都不做，放空一会儿。
有时候我会帮奶奶打理花园——我们在那里吃的东西都是就地种的——新鲜、天然、没有任何添加剂。 那种真正亲近自然的感觉，是在城市里永远体会不到的。
但尽管我很喜欢去那里，我觉得自己没办法长期住在那里。 因为地处郊区，娱乐选择很有限——没有购物中心，没有电影院。
而且房子比较老旧，居住条件也比较基础。 糟糕的网络和缺乏公共交通也让日常生活有些不便。
我觉得短暂的拜访是完美的，但对于日常生活，我还是需要城市的活力和便利。 总体来说，爷爷奶奶的家是我非常珍视的地方——在那里能以一种城市生活永远给不了的方式重新亲近自然。
我希望能尽可能多地回去。

entries.text: Which is more important, protecting the environment or developing the economy?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think this is a tough question, but if I had to choose, I'd lean towards protecting the environment being more important in the long run.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得这是个很难的问题，但如果一定要选，我会倾向于认为保护环境从长远来看更重要。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Economic growth can bring short-term benefits, but if the environment is destroyed in the process, it eventually limits how much the economy can keep growing at all, since resources and health both suffer.
ideaNotes.textZh: 经济增长能带来短期的好处，但如果在这个过程中破坏了环境，最终会限制经济能持续增长的空间，因为资源和人们的健康都会受影响。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, a factory that pollutes a river to cut costs might boost local profits at first, but once the water becomes unusable, it can hurt farming, fishing, and even tourism in that same area for decades.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，一家为了省钱而污染河流的工厂，一开始可能会提升当地利润，但一旦河水无法使用，可能会让这个地区的农业、渔业甚至旅游业受损几十年。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: That said, I don't think it has to be one or the other — many countries are now proving that green technology can actually drive economic growth too.
ideaNotes.textZh: 不过，我觉得这不一定是非此即彼的选择——很多国家现在正在证明，绿色科技其实也能推动经济增长。

keyPhrases.phrase: Limits how much the economy can keep growing

That said, I don't think it has to be one or the other — many countries are now proving that green technology can actually drive economic growth too.

entries.text: Do you think staying in a natural place would help change people’s mood?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: Yes, I definitely think spending time in nature can improve someone's mood.
ideaNotes.textZh: 是的，我确实认为待在大自然中能改善一个人的心情。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Natural environments give the brain a break from constant stimulation, like noise and screens, and this kind of mental rest is what allows stress to fade and mood to lift.
ideaNotes.textZh: 自然环境能让大脑从持续的刺激中得到休息，比如噪音和电子屏幕，而这种精神上的放松正是让压力消退、心情变好的原因。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, someone who spends a stressful week at work might feel noticeably calmer and lighter after just a short walk in a park or forest.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，一个在工作中忙碌了一整周的人，哪怕只是在公园或树林里散一小段步，也会明显感觉更平静、更放松。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: Interestingly, even just looking at greenery through a window has been shown to have a small positive effect on mood, without needing to actually go outside.
ideaNotes.textZh: 有意思的是，即使只是透过窗户看看绿色植物，也已经被证明对心情有小小的积极影响，并不需要真的走到户外。
