entries.text: What are the advantages and disadvantages of advertisements?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think advertising has its good side — it helps people find out about products they actually need — but it also has a pretty manipulative side that pushes people to buy things they don't really need.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我认为广告有好的一面，它帮助人们了解他们真正需要的产品，但它也有相当操控性的一面，推动人们购买他们并不真正需要的东西。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: On the good side, without advertising most people would never know about new products, deals, or services that might genuinely improve their lives. But the problem is that a lot of advertising is designed to make you feel like you're missing out or not good enough without the product — which creates a lot of unnecessary desire and pressure to spend money.
ideaNotes.textZh: 好的方面是，没有广告，大多数人永远不会知道可能真正改善他们生活的新产品、优惠或服务。但问题是很多广告被设计成让你感觉没有这个产品你就会错过什么或不够好，这造成了很多不必要的欲望和消费压力。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, I've noticed that after scrolling through social media for a while, I suddenly feel like I need things I wasn't even thinking about before — a new skincare product, a new outfit — and that feeling is almost entirely created by ads targeting me based on what I've been looking at.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，我注意到在刷了一段时间社交媒体后，我突然感觉需要以前根本没想过的东西，新的护肤品、新衣服，这种感觉几乎完全是由根据我浏览记录针对我的广告造成的。• 转折【可选】 Even so, for small businesses especially, advertising is genuinely important — without it, a good product might just never reach the people who would actually want it. 即便如此，尤其对小企业来说，广告确实很重要，没有它，一个好产品可能永远无法触达真正想要它的人。

entries.text: What is the most important factor in an advertisement?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think the most important thing in an advertisement is that it makes people feel something — whether that's happy, curious, or like the product actually relates to their life.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我认为广告中最重要的是让人们有所感触，无论是快乐、好奇，还是感觉产品确实与他们的生活相关。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: A good ad doesn't need to be flashy or expensive — it just needs to connect with the right people in the right way. If someone watches an ad and thinks "that's me" or "I actually need that", then it's done its job. But if it's just loud and attention-grabbing without any real message, people will just scroll past it and forget it immediately.
ideaNotes.textZh: 好的广告不需要华而不实或昂贵，它只需要以正确的方式与合适的人产生联系。如果有人看了广告然后想"那就是我"或"我真的需要那个"，那么它就完成了它的工作。但如果它只是大声且吸引眼球而没有任何真实信息，人们只会划过去立刻忘记。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, some of the most memorable ads I've seen aren't the ones with the biggest budgets or the most famous celebrities — they're the ones that tell a short but touching story that makes you feel something and then you just naturally remember the brand afterwards.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，我见过的一些最令人难忘的广告不是预算最大或最著名明星的，而是那些讲述简短但感人故事的广告，让你有所感触，然后你自然而然地记住了品牌。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸
ideaNotes.textZh: 可选】 And also, being clear and simple matters a lot — if people can't even tell what the ad is selling after watching it, then no matter how creative it is, it's basically failed at its job. 另外，清晰简单也很重要，如果人们看完广告后甚至不知道它在卖什么，那么无论它多有创意，基本上都失败了。

entries.text: Why are some advertisements boring?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think ads become boring when they're just saying the same things in the same way as every other ad — there's nothing surprising or interesting that makes you want to keep watching.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我认为当广告只是以和其他广告相同的方式说相同的话时，广告就变得无聊，没有任何令人惊喜或有趣的东西让你想继续看。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: A lot of ads just follow a very predictable formula — show the product, say it's the best, have someone smile at the camera — and people have seen that so many times that their brain just automatically tunes it out. If an ad doesn't do anything unexpected or make you feel something different, it just blends into the background noise.
ideaNotes.textZh: 很多广告只是遵循非常可预见的套路，展示产品、说它是最好的、让人对着镜头微笑，人们已经见过太多次了，以至于他们的大脑只是自动屏蔽它。如果广告没有做任何出乎意料的事或让你感受到不同的东西，它只是融入背景噪音中。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, I honestly can't remember a single thing about most ads I've seen recently — they just all look the same and say nothing interesting. But I do remember one ad that told a really funny and unexpected story that had nothing to do with the product until the very end — that one stuck in my head because it actually surprised me.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，说实话我对最近看过的大多数广告一件事都不记得，它们看起来都一样且什么有趣的都没说。但我确实记得一个广告，它讲了一个非常有趣且出乎意料的故事，直到最后才与产品有关，那个广告留在我脑海中是因为它真的让我感到惊喜。

paragraphs: I think ads become boring when they're just saying the same things in the same way as every other ad — there's nothing surprising or interesting that makes you want to keep watching.

A lot of ads just follow a very predictable formula — show the product, say it's the best, have someone smile at the camera — and people have seen that so many times that their brain just automatically tunes it out. If an ad doesn't do anything unexpected or make you feel something different, it just blends into the background noise.

For instance, I honestly can't remember a single thing about most ads I've seen recently — they just all look the same and say nothing interesting. But I do remember one ad that told a really funny and unexpected story that had nothing to do with the product until the very end — that one stuck in my head because it actually surprised me.

entries.text: Which is more effective, online advertising or offline advertising?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think for most businesses today, online advertising is more effective simply because it can reach the right people at the right time in a way that traditional offline ads just can't.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我认为对今天的大多数企业来说，网络广告更有效，仅仅是因为它能以传统线下广告无法做到的方式在正确的时间接触到正确的人。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Online ads can be targeted really specifically — by age, location, interests, even what you've been searching for — so the ad actually reaches someone who might genuinely want the product. Offline ads like billboards or TV commercials just show to everyone and hope the right person sees it, which is much less efficient and harder to measure.
ideaNotes.textZh: 网络广告可以非常具体地定向，按年龄、位置、兴趣，甚至你一直在搜索的内容，所以广告实际上能接触到可能真正想要产品的人。像广告牌或电视广告这样的线下广告只是向所有人展示并希望合适的人看到，这效率低得多且更难衡量。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For example, I constantly see ads on Douyin or WeChat for things that are actually relevant to me — and sometimes I do end up clicking and buying something. But I honestly can't remember the last time a billboard or a flyer made me actually want to buy something.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，我经常在抖音或微信上看到与我真正相关的广告，有时我确实最终点击并购买了东西。但说实话，我不记得上次广告牌或传单让我真正想买东西是什么时候了。• 转折【可选】 Even so, offline advertising still has its place — a big billboard in a busy location or a TV ad during a popular show reaches a huge number of people all at once and builds brand awareness in a way that feels more solid and trustworthy than a pop-up ad on your phone. 即便如此，线下广告仍然有其价值，繁忙地点的大广告牌或热门节目期间的电视广告一次接触大量人群，以感觉比手机上的弹出广告更加稳固和可信的方式建立品牌知名度。

entries.text: Describe a live sports event you watched and liked

paragraphs: I'd like to talk about a Su Super football match I attended as a volunteer. Not long ago, I came across a report on a local WeChat public account about the Su Super football league.
It's a football competition between 13 cities in Jiangsu Province, where amateur and professional players compete together. It attracted huge crowds and a lot of media coverage.
After reading about it, I was really intrigued and decided to sign up as a volunteer. On the day of the match, I got up really early — probably the earliest I had in a long time.

Volunteers had to show up really early, and I had to commute there on top of that, so I ended up waking up at around five or six in the morning. I was pretty sleepy, but once I got there and things got busy, the tiredness just disappeared.
Volunteering at a big event like this isn't something one person can do alone — you really need a team to make it work. In our volunteer team, my main job was to guide the crowd.

But at one point way more people showed up than expected and things got really crowded at the entrance. We quickly figured out a plan, split into smaller groups, and each took charge of a different area — everyone just stepped up, and it worked out pretty well.

That's when I truly understood what teamwork really means. Apart from the match itself, what really stayed with me was an ad that played on the big screen during half-time — Mbappé promoting an electrolyte drink, saying "我是姆巴佩，补水啦" in this really funny Chinese accent.

You know, Mbappé is known for being so intense and focused on the field, so seeing him say something that playful and goofy in Chinese was just so unexpected. Everyone around me just burst out laughing.
I was so curious that I actually went and bought a bottle afterwards. Pretty refreshing — maybe that's the power of a good advertisement.

After the match, the organisers arranged for all the volunteers to make Suzhou-style mooncakes together — it was coming up to Mid-Autumn Festival, a time when families come together and share mooncakes as a symbol of reunion. Suzhou mooncakes are quite different from the regular kind — the outside is made of this really crispy, layered pastry skin, with fillings like rose paste and red bean.
It was already a pretty special experience just being there as a volunteer, but making mooncakes together at the end made it feel even more memorable.
paragraphsZh: 我想说的是我作为志愿者参加的一场苏超足球比赛。 不久前，我在本地的微信公众号上看到了一篇关于苏超足球联赛的报道。
这是江苏省13个城市之间的足球联赛，业余球员和职业球员同场竞技。 比赛吸引了大量的人群和很多媒体报道。
看完之后，我非常感兴趣，于是决定报名参加志愿者。 比赛当天，我起得非常早——可能是很长时间以来起得最早的一次。
志愿者需要很早到场，加上我还需要通勤，所以我最终在早上大概五六点就起床了。 当时挺困的，但一到现场事情忙起来之后，困意就完全消失了。
在这样的大型活动中做志愿者，不是一个人能完成的——真的需要一个团队。 在我们的志愿者团队里，我的主要工作是引导人群。
但在某个时刻，来的人比预期多得多，入口处变得非常拥挤。 我们很快制定了一个计划，分成几个小组，各自负责不同的区域——每个人都主动承担，最后顺利解决了。
就是那一刻，我真正理解了团队合作的意义。 除了比赛本身，让我印象最深的是中场休息时大屏幕上播放的一个广告——姆巴佩代言电解质水，用非常搞笑的中文口音说"我是姆巴佩，补水啦"。
要知道，姆巴佩在场上一向专注而认真，所以看到他用这么可爱、这么搞怪的方式说中文，真的太出乎意料了。 周围的人都哄堂大笑。
我太好奇了，之后真的去买了一瓶。 喝起来还挺清爽的——也许这就是一个好广告的力量。
比赛结束后，主办方安排所有志愿者一起做苏式月饼——因为那时候快到中秋节了，那是一个家人团聚、共享月饼、象征团圆的节日。 苏式月饼和普通月饼很不一样——外皮是非常酥脆、层层叠叠的酥皮，馅料有玫瑰和豆沙等口味。
光是作为志愿者参与其中就已经是一次很特别的经历了，而最后大家一起做月饼，让这次经历变得更加难忘。

entries.text: Why do some people like to watch sports events?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think people love watching sports because it's genuinely exciting and unpredictable — you never know what's going to happen, and that keeps you completely hooked.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我认为人们喜欢看体育比赛是因为它真的令人兴奋且充满未知，你永远不知道接下来会发生什么，这让你完全着迷。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: I mean, watching sports isn't just about the game itself — it's about the atmosphere, the emotion, and feeling connected to something bigger than yourself. When your team scores or wins, you feel this huge rush of happiness, and sharing that moment with other fans around you makes it feel even more special and memorable.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我的意思是，看体育不仅仅是关于比赛本身，而是关于氛围、情感和感觉与比自己更大的东西相连。当你的队伍得分或获胜时，你会感到巨大的喜悦，与周围其他球迷分享那一刻让它感觉更加特别和难忘。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For example, I remember watching a basketball game live once and the energy in the stadium was just incredible — everyone was standing up, shouting, and cheering together, and it felt nothing like watching it at home on TV.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，我记得有一次现场观看篮球比赛，体育场里的气氛简直令人难以置信，每个人都站起来一起喊叫和欢呼，感觉完全不像在家里看电视。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸
ideaNotes.textZh: 可选】 And also, for a lot of people watching sports is a way to bond with friends and family — going to a game together or watching it at home with people you care about just makes the whole experience so much more fun and meaningful. 另外，对很多人来说，看体育是一种与朋友和家人增进感情的方式，一起去看比赛或和你在乎的人在家观看，整个体验就会更加有趣和有意义。

entries.text: Where do people normally watch sports events?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think most people watch sports at home on TV or their phone, but a smaller group of fans prefer going to the stadium in person for the real experience.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我认为大多数人在家里通过电视或手机看体育比赛，但少数球迷更喜欢亲自去体育场感受真实体验。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Watching at home is just so much more convenient and cheap — you can sit on your sofa, eat whatever you want, and pause if you need to. But nothing really compares to being there live — the noise, the crowd, the energy — it's a completely different experience that you just can't get from a screen.
ideaNotes.textZh: 在家看只是更加方便和便宜，你可以坐在沙发上，吃任何你想吃的，需要时还可以暂停。但没有什么真的能与现场相比，噪音、人群、能量，这是一种完全不同的体验，是从屏幕上无法获得的。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, my dad watches almost every football match at home, but last year he went to a live game for the first time and he said the experience was so much more intense and emotional than anything he'd felt watching from his sofa.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，我爸爸几乎每场足球比赛都在家里看，但去年他第一次去看现场比赛，他说这种体验比他在沙发上看到的任何东西都要更强烈和感人。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸
ideaNotes.textZh: 可选】 And also, with so many sports bars and public screenings these days, people have another option that sits somewhere in the middle — you get the social atmosphere without having to pay for stadium tickets. 另外，如今有这么多体育酒吧和公共放映，人们有了另一个介于两者之间的选择，你可以获得社交氛围而不必支付体育场门票。

entries.text: What are the advantages of watching sports events online?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think the biggest advantage of watching sports online is that it's incredibly convenient and flexible — you can watch from anywhere, at any time, on any device.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我认为在线观看体育赛事最大的优势是它非常方便和灵活，你可以在任何地方、任何时间、用任何设备观看。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: You don't need to travel to a venue or even sit in front of a TV — you can watch on your phone during your lunch break, or catch a replay if you missed the live game. And online platforms often offer things like multiple camera angles and live stats that actually make watching more interesting and informative than traditional TV.
ideaNotes.textZh: 你不需要前往场馆甚至坐在电视前，你可以在午休时用手机观看，或者如果错过了直播可以看回放。在线平台通常还提供多个摄像角度和实时数据，实际上让观看比传统电视更加有趣和信息丰富。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For example, I watched a big tennis match last year completely on my phone while I was travelling on a train — I would have completely missed it otherwise, so having that option was really great.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，我去年在坐火车旅行时完全用手机观看了一场重要网球比赛，否则我会完全错过，所以有这个选择真的太好了。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸
ideaNotes.textZh: 可选】 And also, watching online is usually cheaper or even free compared to buying tickets or paying for cable TV, which makes sport much more accessible to everyone regardless of their budget. 另外，与买票或付费有线电视相比，在线观看通常更便宜甚至免费，这使体育对每个人都更容易获得，无论他们的预算如何。

例如，我去年在坐火车旅行时完全用手机观看了一场重要网球比赛，否则我会完全错过，所以有这个选择真的太好了。

可选】 And also, watching online is usually cheaper or even free compared to buying tickets or paying for cable TV, which makes sport much more accessible to everyone regardless of their budget. 另外，与买票或付费有线电视相比，在线观看通常更便宜甚至免费，这使体育对每个人都更容易获得，无论他们的预算如何。

entries.text: What sports matches are suitable for children to attend?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think sports that are easy to understand, fast-paced, and full of energy are the most suitable for children — things like basketball, football, and swimming competitions.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我认为容易理解、节奏快、充满活力的运动最适合孩子，比如篮球、足球和游泳比赛。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Children have short attention spans, so they need something that keeps moving and has clear moments of excitement — like a goal, a slam dunk, or a race finish. Sports that are very slow or complicated to follow, like some forms of cricket or golf, are probably going to lose their interest pretty quickly.
ideaNotes.textZh: 孩子的注意力持续时间短，所以他们需要持续运动且有明确兴奋时刻的东西，比如进球、扣篮或比赛终点。非常缓慢或复杂的运动，比如某些形式的板球或高尔夫，可能会很快失去他们的兴趣。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, I think taking a child to a basketball or football game is a great idea because the pace is fast, the crowd is loud, and there are always exciting moments happening — kids tend to get really into it without even knowing the rules properly.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，我认为带孩子去看篮球或足球比赛是个好主意，因为节奏快、观众声音大，总有令人兴奋的时刻发生，孩子往往会非常投入，甚至不需要真正了解规则。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸
ideaNotes.textZh: 可选】 And also, it's worth thinking about safety and the environment — family-friendly venues where the crowd isn't too rowdy or aggressive are much better for kids, so they can enjoy the experience without feeling scared or uncomfortable. 另外，值得考虑安全和环境，观众不太粗鲁或有攻击性的家庭友好场馆对孩子来说要好得多，这样他们就可以享受体验而不感到害怕或不舒适。

entries.text: Why do some people spend a lot going to other countries to watch sports events?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think for real sports fans, travelling abroad to watch a big event is about much more than just the game — it's about being part of a once-in-a-lifetime experience.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我认为对于真正的体育迷来说，出国观看大型赛事不仅仅是关于比赛本身，而是成为一生一次体验的一部分。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Some sporting events like the World Cup, the Olympics, or major tennis and basketball finals only happen in certain places and you simply can't get that experience anywhere else. For passionate fans, the chance to be there in person — surrounded by fans from all over the world — is something they're willing to save up and sacrifice for.
ideaNotes.textZh: 像世界杯、奥运会或重大网球和篮球决赛这样的体育赛事只在特定地方举办，你根本无法在其他地方获得那种体验。对于热情的球迷来说，亲身在场，被来自世界各地的球迷包围，是他们愿意存钱和牺牲的事情。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, I know someone who flew all the way to Qatar for the World Cup and he said despite the cost and the long journey, being in that stadium and experiencing the atmosphere was something he will never forget for the rest of his life.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，我认识一个人飞了很远去卡塔尔看世界杯，他说尽管花费很大、旅途很长，但身在那个体育场感受那种氛围是他余生永远不会忘记的事情。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸
ideaNotes.textZh: 可选】 And also, for many people it's not just about the sport — it's also a chance to travel, explore a new country, and meet people from completely different backgrounds, so the whole trip becomes a big adventure beyond just the game itself. 另外，对很多人来说，这不仅仅是关于体育，也是一个旅行、探索新国家和认识人的机会，来自完全不同背景的人，所以整个旅程成为一场大冒险，超越了比赛本身。

entries.text: What sports games are popular in your country?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think the most popular sports in China are basketball, table tennis, and badminton — you see people playing them everywhere, from schools to parks to local sports centres.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我认为中国最受欢迎的运动是篮球、乒乓球和羽毛球，你到处都能看到人们在玩，从学校到公园再到当地体育中心。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Basketball is huge especially among younger people — partly because of the influence of the NBA and Chinese basketball stars, and it's easy to play with just a ball and a hoop. Table tennis is popular with all age groups because it's something almost every Chinese person grows up playing, and it's a sport where China has always been world-class.
ideaNotes.textZh: 篮球在年轻人中非常流行，部分原因是NBA和中国篮球明星的影响，而且只需要一个球和一个篮筐就可以玩。乒乓球在各年龄段都很受欢迎，因为这是几乎每个中国人从小就玩的运动，也是中国一直处于世界顶级水平的运动。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For example, in almost every school or community park in China you'll find a table tennis table — it's just part of everyday life here in a way that it isn't in most other countries.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，在中国几乎每所学校或社区公园里你都能找到乒乓球桌，这在这里只是日常生活的一部分，而在大多数其他国家则不然。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸
ideaNotes.textZh: 可选】 And also, football has been growing a lot in popularity over the past few years, especially since the government started putting more money and attention into developing the sport, so it wouldn't surprise me if it becomes even bigger in the future. 另外，足球在过去几年越来越受欢迎，尤其是自从政府开始投入更多资金和关注发展这项运动，所以如果它未来变得更加流行，我不会感到惊讶。

entries.text: Describe a piece of local news that people are interested in

paragraphs: I'd like to talk about a report about the Su Super football match. Not long ago, I came across a report on a local WeChat public account about the Su Super football league.
It's a football competition between 13 cities in Jiangsu Province, where amateur and professional players compete together. It attracted huge crowds and a lot of media coverage.
After reading about it, I was really intrigued and decided to sign up as a volunteer. On the day of the match, I got up really early — probably the earliest I had in a long time.

Volunteers had to show up really early, and I had to commute there on top of that, so I ended up waking up at around five or six in the morning. I was pretty sleepy, but once I got there and things got busy, the tiredness just disappeared.
Volunteering at a big event like this isn't something one person can do alone — you really need a team to make it work. In our volunteer team, my main job was to guide the crowd.

But at one point way more people showed up than expected and things got really crowded at the entrance. We quickly figured out a plan, split into smaller groups, and each took charge of a different area — everyone just stepped up, and it worked out pretty well.

That's when I truly understood what teamwork really means. Apart from the match itself, what really stayed with me was an ad that played on the big screen during half-time — Mbappé promoting an electrolyte drink, saying "我是姆巴佩，补水啦" in this really funny Chinese accent.

You know, Mbappé is known for being so intense and focused on the field, so seeing him say something that playful and goofy in Chinese was just so unexpected. Everyone around me just burst out laughing.
I was so curious that I actually went and bought a bottle afterwards. Pretty refreshing — maybe that's the power of a good advertisement.

After the match, the organisers arranged for all the volunteers to make Suzhou-style mooncakes together — it was coming up to Mid-Autumn Festival, a time when families come together and share mooncakes as a symbol of reunion. Suzhou mooncakes are quite different from the regular kind — the outside is made of this really crispy, layered pastry skin, with fillings like rose paste and red bean.
It was already a pretty special experience just being there as a volunteer, but making mooncakes together at the end made it feel even more memorable.
paragraphsZh: 我想说的是关于苏超足球联赛的一篇报道。 不久前，我在本地的微信公众号上看到了一篇关于苏超足球联赛的报道。
这是江苏省13个城市之间的足球联赛，业余球员和职业球员同场竞技。 比赛吸引了大量的人群和很多媒体报道。
看完之后，我非常感兴趣，于是决定报名参加志愿者。 比赛当天，我起得非常早——可能是很长时间以来起得最早的一次。
志愿者需要很早到场，加上我还需要通勤，所以我最终在早上大概五六点就起床了。 当时挺困的，但一到现场事情忙起来之后，困意就完全消失了。
在这样的大型活动中做志愿者，不是一个人能完成的——真的需要一个团队。 在我们的志愿者团队里，我的主要工作是引导人群。
但在某个时刻，来的人比预期多得多，入口处变得非常拥挤。 我们很快制定了一个计划，分成几个小组，各自负责不同的区域——每个人都主动承担，最后顺利解决了。
就是那一刻，我真正理解了团队合作的意义。 除了比赛本身，让我印象最深的是中场休息时大屏幕上播放的一个广告——姆巴佩代言电解质水，用非常搞笑的中文口音说"我是姆巴佩，补水啦"。
要知道，姆巴佩在场上一向专注而认真，所以看到他用这么可爱、这么搞怪的方式说中文，真的太出乎意料了。 周围的人都哄堂大笑。
我太好奇了，之后真的去买了一瓶。 喝起来还挺清爽的——也许这就是一个好广告的力量。
比赛结束后，主办方安排所有志愿者一起做苏式月饼——因为那时候快到中秋节了，那是一个家人团聚、共享月饼、象征团圆的节日。 苏式月饼和普通月饼很不一样——外皮是非常酥脆、层层叠叠的酥皮，馅料有玫瑰和豆沙等口味。
光是作为志愿者参与其中就已经是一次很特别的经历了，而最后大家一起做月饼，让这次经历变得更加难忘。

entries.text: Do people read the newspaper where you live?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: Honestly, almost nobody reads physical newspapers anymore — it's become quite rare and old-fashioned, and most people get their news entirely from their phones.
ideaNotes.textZh: 说实话，几乎没有人再读实体报纸了，它已经变得相当少见和过时，大多数人完全从手机获取新闻。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: The thing is, you can barely even find newspapers to buy these days — most newsstands have closed down, and even the ones that remain don't sell many. News apps and platforms like WeChat, Weibo, and Toutiao have completely taken over because they're instant, free, and personalised — you get exactly the kind of news you're interested in without having to flip through pages of things you don't care about.
ideaNotes.textZh: 问题在于，这些天你几乎找不到报纸可买，大多数报摊已经关闭，即使还存在的也卖得很少。微信、微博和今日头条等新闻应用和平台已经完全取而代之，因为它们即时、免费且个性化，你可以得到你感兴趣的新闻，而不必翻阅你不关心的页面。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, even older generations who used to buy papers every morning have mostly switched to phones now — it's common to see elderly people in parks or on the subway scrolling through news feeds just like younger people do. The newspaper habit has pretty much died out across all age groups.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，即使是以前每天早上买报纸的老一辈，现在大多数也转向了手机，经常可以看到老年人在公园或地铁上浏览新闻推送，就像年轻人一样。看报纸的习惯几乎在所有年龄段都消失了。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸
ideaNotes.textZh: 可选】 And also, some newspapers have tried to survive by going digital, but even their online versions struggle to compete with social media platforms that deliver news in a much more engaging and fast-paced way. 另外，一些报纸试图通过转向数字化来生存，但即使是他们的在线版本也难以与以更加吸引人和快节奏方式传递新闻的社交媒体平台竞争。

可选】 And also, some newspapers have tried to survive by going digital, but even their online versions struggle to compete with social media platforms that deliver news in a much more engaging and fast-paced way. 另外，一些报纸试图通过转向数字化来生存，但即使是他们的在线版本也难以与以更加吸引人和快节奏方式传递新闻的社交媒体平台竞争。

entries.text: Do people prefer local or international news?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think most people are more drawn to local news on a daily basis — it just feels more directly relevant to their actual lives.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我认为大多数人在日常生活中更倾向于本地新闻，它对他们的实际生活感觉更加直接相关。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Local news covers things that actually affect people's day-to-day lives — things like new policies in their city, road closures, job market changes, or community events. International news, while interesting, often feels quite distant and hard to connect with personally. That said, when something really big happens globally — like a pandemic, a major war, or a serious economic crisis — people suddenly pay a lot more attention because they know it could eventually affect them too.
ideaNotes.textZh: 本地新闻报道实际上影响人们日常生活的事情，比如他们城市的新政策、道路封闭、就业市场变化或社区活动。国际新闻虽然有趣，但往往感觉相当遥远且难以个人联系。话虽如此，当全球发生真正重大的事情时，比如大流行病、重大战争或严重经济危机，人们突然更加关注，因为他们知道它最终也可能影响到他们。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, most people would be far more interested in reading about a new housing policy or a change in local transport than about an election in a country they've never visited. But something like a global financial crisis immediately gets everyone's attention because people start worrying about their own jobs and savings.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，大多数人对阅读新住房政策或当地交通变化的兴趣，远比对他们从未去过的国家的选举更大。但像全球金融危机这样的事情立即引起每个人的注意，因为人们开始担心自己的工作和储蓄。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸
ideaNotes.textZh: 可选】 And also, younger people do tend to follow international news more than older generations — partly because social media constantly exposes them to global events, and partly because they feel more internationally minded and curious about the wider world. 另外，年轻人确实比老一辈更倾向于关注国际新闻，部分原因是社交媒体不断让他们接触全球事件，部分原因是他们感到更加具有国际视野，对更广泛的世界感到好奇。

entries.text: Do you think it's important to have a national identity?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: Yes, I think having a national identity is genuinely important — it gives people a sense of belonging and connection to something bigger than just themselves or their immediate community.
ideaNotes.textZh: 是的，我认为拥有国家认同感真的很重要，它给人们一种归属感和联系，与比自己或直接社区更大的东西相连。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: When people feel connected to their country — its history, its culture, and its values — they tend to feel more responsible for each other and more willing to work together towards common goals. This becomes especially important during tough times, like natural disasters or economic difficulties, when society needs people to pull together rather than just look out for themselves. Without any shared identity, it's much harder for a country to function as a united and cooperative community.
ideaNotes.textZh: 当人们感到与他们的国家，其历史、文化和价值观有联系时，他们往往对彼此更有责任感，更愿意为共同目标合作。这在艰难时期变得尤为重要，比如自然灾害或经济困难，当社会需要人们齐心协力而不只是顾及自己时。没有任何共同认同，一个国家作为团结合作的社区运作就困难得多。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, after the Sichuan earthquake in 2008, people from all over China came together in a way that was really moving — strangers donated money, volunteers travelled across the country to help, and there was this powerful sense that everyone was part of the same family facing the same tragedy. That kind of response only happens when people feel a genuine shared identity.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，2008年四川地震后，来自全国各地的人们以一种真正令人感动的方式聚集在一起，陌生人捐款，志愿者跨越全国去帮忙，有一种强烈的感觉，每个人都是同一个大家庭的一部分，面对同样的悲剧。这种回应只有在人们感到真正共同认同时才会发生。• 转折【可选】 Even so, national identity becomes a problem when it turns into extreme nationalism — feeling proud of your country is completely healthy, but when it starts leading to hostility towards outsiders or blind loyalty regardless of what's actually right or wrong, that's where it crosses a line. 即便如此，当国家认同变成极端民族主义时就成了问题，为自己的国家感到自豪是完全健康的，但当它开始导致对外来者的敌意或盲目忠诚，不管实际上对错，那就越界了。

entries.text: How can people develop their national identity?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think national identity develops most naturally through education, shared cultural experiences, and simply growing up within a country's traditions.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我认为国家认同最自然地通过教育、共同的文化体验以及在一个国家的传统中成长而发展。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Schools play a really important role — learning about a country's history, important figures, and achievements helps young people understand where they come from and feel a sense of pride and connection. But it's not just about formal education — things like celebrating festivals together, supporting national sports teams, and sharing food and cultural traditions all quietly build that sense of identity over time without people even realising it. The key is that it feels natural and genuine rather than something being forced on you.
ideaNotes.textZh: 学校起着非常重要的作用，学习一个国家的历史、重要人物和成就帮助年轻人了解自己从哪里来，感到自豪和有联系。但不只是正式教育，像一起庆祝节日、支持国家体育队、分享食物和文化传统这样的事情都在随着时间推移悄悄建立认同感，人们甚至没有意识到。关键是它感觉自然而真实，而不是被强加于你的东西。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, in China things like celebrating Spring Festival with family, watching the National Day parade, or learning about figures like Lei Feng at school all plant the seeds of national identity from a very young age — people grow up sharing the same stories, the same traditions, and the same cultural references, which naturally makes them feel part of something shared.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，在中国，像与家人庆祝春节、观看国庆节阅兵式，或在学校学习雷锋这样的人物，都从很小的年纪就播下了国家认同的种子，人们在分享相同故事、相同传统和相同文化参照中成长，这自然使他们感到是共同事物的一部分。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸
ideaNotes.textZh: 可选】 And also, travelling within your own country can be a surprisingly powerful way to build national identity — seeing different regions, meeting people from different backgrounds, and realising how much you share despite the differences makes people feel genuinely proud and connected in a very real way. 另外，在自己国家内旅行可以是建立国家认同出人意料有力的方式，看到不同地区、遇见来自不同背景的人，并意识到尽管有差异但你们有多少共同点，使人们以非常真实的方式感到真正自豪和有联系。

entries.text: Describe a food that people eat on special occasions/events

paragraphs: I'd like to talk about Suzhou-style mooncakes — I actually made them by hand during my volunteering at a Su Super match. Not long ago, I came across a report on a local WeChat public account about the Su Super football league.
It's a football competition between 13 cities in Jiangsu Province, where amateur and professional players compete together. It attracted huge crowds and a lot of media coverage.
After reading about it, I was really intrigued and decided to sign up as a volunteer. On the day of the match, I got up really early — probably the earliest I had in a long time.

Volunteers had to show up really early, and I had to commute there on top of that, so I ended up waking up at around five or six in the morning. I was pretty sleepy, but once I got there and things got busy, the tiredness just disappeared.
Volunteering at a big event like this isn't something one person can do alone — you really need a team to make it work. In our volunteer team, my main job was to guide the crowd.

But at one point way more people showed up than expected and things got really crowded at the entrance. We quickly figured out a plan, split into smaller groups, and each took charge of a different area — everyone just stepped up, and it worked out pretty well.

That's when I truly understood what teamwork really means. Apart from the match itself, what really stayed with me was an ad that played on the big screen during half-time — Mbappé promoting an electrolyte drink, saying "我是姆巴佩，补水啦" in this really funny Chinese accent.

You know, Mbappé is known for being so intense and focused on the field, so seeing him say something that playful and goofy in Chinese was just so unexpected. Everyone around me just burst out laughing.
I was so curious that I actually went and bought a bottle afterwards. Pretty refreshing — maybe that's the power of a good advertisement.

After the match, the organisers arranged for all the volunteers to make Suzhou-style mooncakes together — it was coming up to Mid-Autumn Festival, a time when families come together and share mooncakes as a symbol of reunion. Suzhou mooncakes are quite different from the regular kind — the outside is made of this really crispy, layered pastry skin, with fillings like rose paste and red bean.
It was already a pretty special experience just being there as a volunteer, but making mooncakes together at the end made it feel even more memorable.
paragraphsZh: 我想说的是苏式月饼——是我在参加苏超比赛志愿者活动期间亲手做的。 不久前，我在本地的微信公众号上看到了一篇关于苏超足球联赛的报道。
这是江苏省13个城市之间的足球联赛，业余球员和职业球员同场竞技。 比赛吸引了大量的人群和很多媒体报道。
看完之后，我非常感兴趣，于是决定报名参加志愿者。 比赛当天，我起得非常早——可能是很长时间以来起得最早的一次。
志愿者需要很早到场，加上我还需要通勤，所以我最终在早上大概五六点就起床了。 当时挺困的，但一到现场事情忙起来之后，困意就完全消失了。
在这样的大型活动中做志愿者，不是一个人能完成的——真的需要一个团队。 在我们的志愿者团队里，我的主要工作是引导人群。
但在某个时刻，来的人比预期多得多，入口处变得非常拥挤。 我们很快制定了一个计划，分成几个小组，各自负责不同的区域——每个人都主动承担，最后顺利解决了。
就是那一刻，我真正理解了团队合作的意义。 除了比赛本身，让我印象最深的是中场休息时大屏幕上播放的一个广告——姆巴佩代言电解质水，用非常搞笑的中文口音说"我是姆巴佩，补水啦"。
要知道，姆巴佩在场上一向专注而认真，所以看到他用这么可爱、这么搞怪的方式说中文，真的太出乎意料了。 周围的人都哄堂大笑。
我太好奇了，之后真的去买了一瓶。 喝起来还挺清爽的——也许这就是一个好广告的力量。
比赛结束后，主办方安排所有志愿者一起做苏式月饼——因为那时候快到中秋节了，那是一个家人团聚、共享月饼、象征团圆的节日。 苏式月饼和普通月饼很不一样——外皮是非常酥脆、层层叠叠的酥皮，馅料有玫瑰和豆沙等口味。
光是作为志愿者参与其中就已经是一次很特别的经历了，而最后大家一起做月饼，让这次经历变得更加难忘。

entries.text: Why are there special foods on special occasions or events ?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think special foods exist on special occasions because food is one of the most powerful ways to mark that something is different from an ordinary day — it signals that this moment actually matters.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我认为特殊场合有特别食物是因为食物是标志某事与普通日子不同的最有力方式之一，它表明这个时刻真的很重要。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Food carries a lot of cultural and emotional meaning — certain dishes are tied to specific celebrations and have been passed down for generations, so when you eat them you're not just having a meal, you're connecting with something bigger — your family, your culture, your history. It also just makes the occasion feel more special and memorable compared to a regular day.
ideaNotes.textZh: 食物承载着很多文化和情感意义，某些菜肴与特定庆典相关联，已经传承了几代人，所以当你吃它们时，你不只是在吃饭，你在与更大的东西联系，你的家庭、文化、历史。它也使场合感觉比普通日子更加特别和难忘。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, in China eating dumplings during Chinese New Year isn't just about the food — it's about the whole family sitting together, making them from scratch, and continuing a tradition that has been going on for hundreds of years. If you just ate normal food that day it would feel like something was missing.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，在中国春节吃饺子不只是关于食物，而是关于全家人坐在一起、从头开始制作，延续一个已经进行了数百年的传统。如果那天只是吃普通食物，感觉会缺少什么。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸
ideaNotes.textZh: 可选】 And also, special food creates shared memories — years later when you smell or taste something, it instantly takes you back to a specific moment or celebration, and that kind of emotional connection is really hard to replace with anything else. 另外，特别食物创造共同记忆，多年后当你闻到或尝到某种东西时，它立刻将你带回到特定的时刻或庆典，这种情感联系真的很难被任何其他东西替代。

paragraphs: I think special foods exist on special occasions because food is one of the most powerful ways to mark that something is different from an ordinary day — it signals that this moment actually matters.

entries.text: What are the differences between everyday food and festival food ?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think the biggest differences are the effort, variety, and meaning behind the food — festival food is just on a completely different level from what people eat on a normal day.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我认为最大的区别是食物背后的用心程度、多样性和意义，节日食物与人们日常吃的东西完全不同。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: On a regular day, most people just want something quick, simple, and filling — they're not going to spend hours in the kitchen. But for festivals, families will spend the whole day cooking elaborate dishes, using special ingredients, and putting real care into the presentation because the meal itself is part of the celebration. The food is no longer just fuel — it becomes the centrepiece of the whole occasion.
ideaNotes.textZh: 在普通的一天，大多数人只想要快速、简单和饱腹的东西，他们不会在厨房花几个小时。但对于节日，家人会花一整天烹饪精致的菜肴，使用特殊食材，真正用心摆盘，因为这顿饭本身就是庆典的一部分。食物不再只是燃料，它成为整个场合的核心。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For example, during Chinese New Year my family always makes dumplings together from scratch — everyone sits around the table folding them, which we would never do on a normal day. The whole process takes hours but that's kind of the point — it's not just about the food, it's about being together and doing something as a family.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，在春节期间，我家总是一起从头开始包饺子，每个人围坐在桌边包饺子，这是我们在普通日子里永远不会做的事。整个过程需要几个小时，但这正是重点，不只是关于食物，而是关于一起做一件事、作为一家人。

entries.text: Are there any differences between the food people eat today and the food people ate in the past ?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think food today is so much more varied and convenient than in the past, but at the same time some of the traditional home-cooked culture has slowly faded away.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我认为今天的食物比过去更加多样和方便，但同时一些传统家常饮食文化已经慢慢消失。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: In the past, people mostly ate simple, seasonal, home-cooked meals — whatever was locally available — and families would sit together and cook from scratch every day. Nowadays people have access to food from all over the world, and with things like food delivery apps and ready meals, a lot of people barely cook at all. It's more convenient but also a lot less personal and meaningful.
ideaNotes.textZh: 过去，人们主要吃简单、应季、家常饭菜，当地有什么就吃什么，家人每天会坐在一起从头开始烹饪。如今人们可以获得来自世界各地的食物，有了外卖应用和即食食品，很多人几乎根本不做饭。更方便但也少了很多个人感和意义。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For example, my grandparents' generation would wake up early and spend hours preparing every meal from scratch using fresh ingredients from the market — it was a big part of daily life. But most people my age just order food on their phone and it arrives in twenty minutes — cooking feels like something you do occasionally rather than every day.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，我祖父母那一代人会早起，用从市场买的新鲜食材花几个小时从头开始准备每顿饭，这是日常生活的重要部分。但我这个年龄的大多数人只是用手机点外卖，二十分钟就到了，做饭感觉像是偶尔做的事情而不是每天都做。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸
ideaNotes.textZh: 可选】 And also, people today are much more aware of health and nutrition than before — things like calories, protein, and dietary choices are talked about constantly, whereas in the past people just ate what was available and didn't overthink it. 另外，现代人比以前更加关注健康和营养，卡路里、蛋白质和饮食选择等话题不断被讨论，而过去人们只是吃有什么就吃什么，不会想太多。

entries.text: Do people today prefer eating at home or in a restaurant ?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think it really depends on the situation — younger people tend to eat out a lot more, but most people still value a home-cooked meal when they have the time.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我认为这真的取决于情况，年轻人倾向于更多外出就餐，但大多数人在有时间时仍然珍视家常饭。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Eating out is just so much more convenient and social — you don't have to shop, cook, or clean up, and there's a huge variety of options to choose from. But a lot of people also feel that home-cooked food is healthier and more comforting — you know exactly what's in it, the portions are right, and there's something about eating at home that just feels more relaxed and personal.
ideaNotes.textZh: 外出就餐更加方便和社交，你不需要购物、做饭或清洁，有大量选择。但很多人也觉得家常饭更健康、更有安慰感，你确切知道里面有什么，分量合适，在家吃饭有一种感觉更加轻松和个人化的东西。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, during the week most of my friends just order takeaway or eat out because nobody has the energy to cook after work. But on weekends when families get together, almost everyone would rather eat at home — my mum always says the food just tastes better when someone makes it for you with care.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，工作日大多数朋友只是点外卖或外出就餐，因为下班后没有人有精力做饭。但周末家人聚在一起时，几乎每个人都宁愿在家吃，我妈妈总说当有人用心为你做饭时，食物味道更好。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸
ideaNotes.textZh: 可选】 And also, with food delivery apps being so cheap and easy now, there's actually a third option that's become really popular — ordering in — where you get restaurant food without leaving the house, which kind of gives you the best of both worlds. 另外，现在外卖应用这么便宜方便，实际上出现了第三种变得非常流行的选择，叫外卖，你不用离开家就能吃到餐厅的食物，这在某种程度上给了你两全其美的效果。

entries.text: Describe a time you watched a famous person being interviewed

paragraphs: The person I'd like to talk about is an old man in my hometown, Mr Wang. About a month ago, I came across a local TV interview with him online.

Through that interview, I found out that he used to be a history teacher — that's actually why he loves history so much, it's been part of his life for decades. After retiring, he started doing hands-on research instead of just reading books.

It wasn't easy — a lot of the old people who lived through that time were very old, some had already passed away, so it got harder to find information. He didn't have much money or support from his family, but he just kept going, little by little, year after year, and eventually published a book and held an exhibition about his research — and that's how he became popular in my hometown.
That interview really stayed with me for a long time. I realized his success didn't come from luck, but from genuine passion for history.
Later, I went to his exhibition and got to meet him in person. We talked for a bit, but I still wanted to know more about how he'd kept going all these years.

Mr Wang was really friendly — he invited me to his house, and we spent some time going through his old photos together, listening to him talk about the stories behind them. I really admire this old man — what he did wasn't easy, there was no money or fame in it, just real passion, and he succeeded in the end.
He saved a lot of local history that could've been forgotten, and getting to know him a bit made me respect him even more.
paragraphsZh: 我想说的这个人是我们家乡的一位老爷爷，王爷爷。 大概一个月前，我在网上刷到了当地电视台对他的一个采访。
通过这个采访我了解到，他以前是一名历史老师——这也是他这么喜欢历史的原因，历史几十年来一直是他生活的一部分。 退休之后，他开始做实地研究，而不只是看书。
这个过程并不容易——很多经历过那段历史的老人年纪都很大了，有些已经去世了，资料越来越难找。 他也没有太多经费，家里人也不是很支持，但他还是一点一点坚持了下来，一年又一年，最后出版了一本关于他研究的书，还办了一个展览——这也是他在我们家乡出名的原因。
那个采访让我印象特别深，一直记了很久。 我意识到他的成功不是靠运气，而是因为他对历史真正的热爱。
后来，我去了他的展览，见到了他本人。 我们聊了一会儿，但我还是很想多了解一下他这些年是怎么坚持下来的。
王爷爷人特别友好——他邀请我去他家，我们一起翻看他的老照片，听他讲照片背后的故事。 我真的很佩服这位老爷爷——他做的事情并不容易，没有钱也没有名利，纯粹是出于热爱，最后他成功了。
他保留了很多本来可能会被遗忘的本地历史，认识他之后，我对他更尊敬了。

entries.text: What should people wear to a job interview?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think people should wear something formal and professional to a job interview, like a suit or a neat shirt.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我认为人们参加工作面试应该穿一些正式又专业的衣服，比如西装或整洁的衬衫。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: This is because the way you dress gives the interviewer a first impression of how serious and organized you are, even before you say anything.
ideaNotes.textZh: 这是因为你的穿着会给面试官留下第一印象，让他们在你开口之前就感受到你有多认真、多有条理。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For example, someone applying for a job at a law firm would probably wear a suit, while someone interviewing at a creative agency might dress a bit more casually but still neat.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，去律师事务所应聘的人可能会穿西装，而去创意公司面试的人可能穿得随意一些，但仍然要整洁。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: So basically, the outfit should match the company culture, but always stay on the safe, presentable side.
ideaNotes.textZh: 所以基本上，穿着应该符合公司文化，但始终要保持稳妥、得体。

paragraphs: I think people should wear something formal and professional to a job interview, like a suit or a neat shirt.
This is because the way you dress gives the interviewer a first impression of how serious and organized you are, even before you say anything.
For example, someone applying for a job at a law firm would probably wear a suit, while someone interviewing at a creative agency might dress a bit more casually but still neat.
So basically, the outfit should match the company culture, but always stay on the safe, presentable side.
paragraphsZh: 我认为人们参加工作面试应该穿一些正式又专业的衣服，比如西装或整洁的衬衫。
这是因为你的穿着会给面试官留下第一印象，让他们在你开口之前就感受到你有多认真、多有条理。
例如，去律师事务所应聘的人可能会穿西装，而去创意公司面试的人可能穿得随意一些，但仍然要整洁。
所以基本上，穿着应该符合公司文化，但始终要保持稳妥、得体。

entries.text: Why do we need to attend interviews when applying for jobs?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: Well, interviews are necessary because they give companies a chance to check if a candidate has the right skills and personality for the job.
ideaNotes.textZh: 嗯，面试是必要的，因为它能让公司有机会确认候选人是否具备这份工作所需的技能和性格。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: A resume can only show so much, but an interview allows employers to see how someone communicates, thinks under pressure, and fits into the team.
ideaNotes.textZh: 一份简历能展示的信息有限，而面试能让雇主看到一个人如何沟通、在压力下如何思考，以及能否融入团队。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, two candidates might have similar qualifications on paper, but during the interview, one might show much better problem-solving ability or enthusiasm for the role.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，两位候选人在纸面上的资历可能差不多，但在面试中，一个人可能表现出更强的解决问题能力或对这份工作的热情。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: At the same time, it also gives candidates a chance to learn more about the company and decide if it's the right fit.
ideaNotes.textZh: 同时，这也给了候选人一个机会去了解这家公司，判断是否适合自己。

paragraphs: Well, interviews are necessary because they give companies a chance to check if a candidate has the right skills and personality for the job.
A resume can only show so much, but an interview allows employers to see how someone communicates, thinks under pressure, and fits into the team.
For instance, two candidates might have similar qualifications on paper, but during the interview, one might show much better problem-solving ability or enthusiasm for the role.
At the same time, it also gives candidates a chance to learn more about the company and decide if it's the right fit.

entries.text: Why do some people think interviews are a waste of time?

entries.text: Why do some people dislike being interviewed?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think a lot of people dislike being interviewed because it can feel really stressful and like they're being constantly judged.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得很多人不喜欢被面试，是因为这会让人感到非常有压力，而且感觉自己一直在被评判。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: During an interview, people often worry about saying the wrong thing, which creates a lot of anxiety and makes it hard to relax and be themselves.

ideaNotes.label: 例子

ideaNotes.text: So it's really the fear of being judged and the pressure to perform perfectly that makes interviews uncomfortable for many people.

entries.text: Describe a person you know who did something difficult and was successful

paragraphs: The person I'd like to talk about is an old man in my hometown, Mr Wang. About a month ago, I came across a local TV interview with him online.

Through that interview, I found out that he used to be a history teacher — that's actually why he loves history so much, it's been part of his life for decades. After retiring, he started doing hands-on research instead of just reading books.

It wasn't easy — a lot of the old people who lived through that time were very old, some had already passed away, so it got harder to find information. He didn't have much money or support from his family, but he just kept going, little by little, year after year, and eventually published a book and held an exhibition about his research — and that's how he became popular in my hometown.
That interview really stayed with me for a long time. I realized his success didn't come from luck, but from genuine passion for history.
Later, I went to his exhibition and got to meet him in person. We talked for a bit, but I still wanted to know more about how he'd kept going all these years.

Mr Wang was really friendly — he invited me to his house, and we spent some time going through his old photos together, listening to him talk about the stories behind them. I really admire this old man — what he did wasn't easy, there was no money or fame in it, just real passion, and he succeeded in the end.
He saved a lot of local history that could've been forgotten, and getting to know him a bit made me respect him even more.
paragraphsZh: 我想说的这个人是我们家乡的一位老爷爷，王爷爷。 大概一个月前，我在网上刷到了当地电视台对他的一个采访。
通过这个采访我了解到，他以前是一名历史老师——这也是他这么喜欢历史的原因，历史几十年来一直是他生活的一部分。 退休之后，他开始做实地研究，而不只是看书。
这个过程并不容易——很多经历过那段历史的老人年纪都很大了，有些已经去世了，资料越来越难找。 他也没有太多经费，家里人也不是很支持，但他还是一点一点坚持了下来，一年又一年，最后出版了一本关于他研究的书，还办了一个展览——这也是他在我们家乡出名的原因。
那个采访让我印象特别深，一直记了很久。 我意识到他的成功不是靠运气，而是因为他对历史真正的热爱。
后来，我去了他的展览，见到了他本人。 我们聊了一会儿，但我还是很想多了解一下他这些年是怎么坚持下来的。
王爷爷人特别友好——他邀请我去他家，我们一起翻看他的老照片，听他讲照片背后的故事。 我真的很佩服这位老爷爷——他做的事情并不容易，没有钱也没有名利，纯粹是出于热爱，最后他成功了。
他保留了很多本来可能会被遗忘的本地历史，认识他之后，我对他更尊敬了。

entries.text: Is it easy to start up a company?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I don't think it's really that easy to start up a company, even though the process itself might seem simple on paper.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我不觉得创办公司真的那么容易，尽管手续本身看起来可能很简单。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: The tricky part is finding enough funding, building a good team, and figuring out how to attract customers in a competitive market.
ideaNotes.textZh: 难点在于找到足够的资金、组建好的团队，以及在竞争激烈的市场中吸引客户。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, many new entrepreneurs manage to register their company quickly, but then struggle for months just to get their first few clients or make a profit.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，很多新创业者能很快完成公司注册，但之后却要苦苦挣扎好几个月才能拿到最初的几个客户或实现盈利。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: So overall, starting a company is easy on paper, but keeping it running successfully is the real challenge.
ideaNotes.textZh: 所以总的来说，创办公司在纸面上很容易，但让它持续成功运营才是真正的挑战。

entries.text: Does money equal success ?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: Well, I don't think money is exactly the same as success, though it definitely plays a role. To me, success is more about feeling fulfilled in what you do.
ideaNotes.textZh: 呃，我不觉得金钱和成功完全画等号，虽然它确实起作用。对我来说，成功更多是在做的事情中感到满足。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Success can mean different things depending on a person's values, like having a stable career, or good relationships with family. Money's just one part of it, not everything.
ideaNotes.textZh: 成功可以根据一个人的价值观有不同定义，比如拥有稳定的事业，或者和家人有良好的关系。金钱只是其中一部分，不是全部。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, some rich business owners end up feeling burned out, while people with average incomes often feel happier because they have time for family.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如说，一些有钱的企业主最终感到身心俱疲，而收入普通的人往往更快乐，因为他们有陪伴家人的时间。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: So I'd say money is more like a tool that supports success, rather than success itself.
ideaNotes.textZh: 所以我觉得金钱更像是支持成功的工具，而不是成功本身。

entries.text: How can companies help protect the environment?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: Well, I think there are quite a few ways companies can help protect the environment, like reducing pollution and using eco-friendly materials.
ideaNotes.textZh: 呃，我觉得公司有很多方式可以帮助保护环境，比如减少污染、使用环保材料。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: This matters because companies, especially factories, are often major sources of waste and carbon emissions, so if they take responsibility, it can make a real difference.

ideaNotes.text: If more companies followed this kind of practice, it could really help slow down environmental damage in the long run.

entries.text: Is it difficult to do business in today's world?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: Yeah, I'd say it's actually quite difficult to do business nowadays, mainly because of the intense competition.
ideaNotes.textZh: 嗯，我觉得现在做生意其实挺困难的，主要是因为激烈的竞争。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: With so many companies offering similar products, it's hard to stand out, and things like changing market trends and rising costs make it even tougher.
ideaNotes.textZh: 由于有太多公司提供类似的产品，很难脱颖而出，再加上不断变化的市场趋势和上涨的成本，让情况更加艰难。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, a lot of small businesses struggle to survive after just a few years because they can't compete with bigger corporations or keep up with online competition.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，很多小企业开业几年后就难以生存，因为无法与大企业竞争，也跟不上线上竞争。

entries.text: Describe someone who is older than you that you admire

paragraphs: The person I'd like to talk about is an old man in my hometown, Mr Wang. About a month ago, I came across a local TV interview with him online.

Through that interview, I found out that he used to be a history teacher — that's actually why he loves history so much, it's been part of his life for decades. After retiring, he started doing hands-on research instead of just reading books.

It wasn't easy — a lot of the old people who lived through that time were very old, some had already passed away, so it got harder to find information. He didn't have much money or support from his family, but he just kept going, little by little, year after year, and eventually published a book and held an exhibition about his research — and that's how he became popular in my hometown.
That interview really stayed with me for a long time. I realized his success didn't come from luck, but from genuine passion for history.
Later, I went to his exhibition and got to meet him in person. We talked for a bit, but I still wanted to know more about how he'd kept going all these years.

Mr Wang was really friendly — he invited me to his house, and we spent some time going through his old photos together, listening to him talk about the stories behind them. I really admire this old man — what he did wasn't easy, there was no money or fame in it, just real passion, and he succeeded in the end.
He saved a lot of local history that could've been forgotten, and getting to know him a bit made me respect him even more.
paragraphsZh: 我想说的这个人是我们家乡的一位老爷爷，王爷爷。 大概一个月前，我在网上刷到了当地电视台对他的一个采访。
通过这个采访我了解到，他以前是一名历史老师——这也是他这么喜欢历史的原因，历史几十年来一直是他生活的一部分。 退休之后，他开始做实地研究，而不只是看书。
这个过程并不容易——很多经历过那段历史的老人年纪都很大了，有些已经去世了，资料越来越难找。 他也没有太多经费，家里人也不是很支持，但他还是一点一点坚持了下来，一年又一年，最后出版了一本关于他研究的书，还办了一个展览——这也是他在我们家乡出名的原因。
那个采访让我印象特别深，一直记了很久。 我意识到他的成功不是靠运气，而是因为他对历史真正的热爱。
后来，我去了他的展览，见到了他本人。 我们聊了一会儿，但我还是很想多了解一下他这些年是怎么坚持下来的。
王爷爷人特别友好——他邀请我去他家，我们一起翻看他的老照片，听他讲照片背后的故事。 我真的很佩服这位老爷爷——他做的事情并不容易，没有钱也没有名利，纯粹是出于热爱，最后他成功了。
他保留了很多本来可能会被遗忘的本地历史，认识他之后，我对他更尊敬了。

entries.text: What do old people usually do in their daily life?

ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得大多数老年人的一天过得比较悠闲，比如散步、种花或者陪伴家人。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Since they're usually retired, they no longer need to follow a strict work schedule, so their time naturally shifts toward things that bring comfort and enjoyment rather than productivity.

entries.text: Why is there a generation gap between the young and the old?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think the generation gap mainly comes from the fact that young and old people grew up in very different environments.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得代沟主要来自于年轻人和老年人成长的环境非常不同。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: The world changes so fast that each generation is shaped by different social conditions and technology, so they naturally develop different values, habits, and ways of thinking, which can make it hard to fully understand each other.
ideaNotes.textZh: 世界变化太快，每一代人都受到不同社会环境和科技的影响，所以自然会形成不同的价值观、习惯和思维方式，这会让彼此很难完全理解对方。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, older generations who grew up valuing stability and hard work might not understand why young people today prioritize work-life balance or switch jobs frequently.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，老一辈从小就重视稳定和努力工作，可能不理解为什么现在的年轻人更看重工作与生活的平衡，或者频繁换工作。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: Technology plays a huge role too — older people who didn't grow up with smartphones or social media sometimes struggle to relate to how younger people communicate and socialize today.
ideaNotes.textZh: 科技也起了很大作用——没有从小接触智能手机或社交媒体的老年人，有时很难理解现在年轻人交流和社交的方式。

entries.text: Has old people's life quality improved when compared to the past?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: Yes, I definitely think old people's life quality has improved a lot compared to the past.
ideaNotes.textZh: 是的，我确实认为老年人的生活质量和过去相比提高了很多。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Advances in healthcare mean people not only live longer but also stay healthier for more of their later years, and improved social welfare systems also provide more financial security than before.
ideaNotes.textZh: 医疗的进步让人们不仅活得更长，晚年也能保持更健康的状态，而更完善的社会保障体系也提供了比过去更多的经济保障。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, diseases that used to be life-threatening in the past can now often be treated or managed effectively, and pension systems also allow many elderly people to retire without relying entirely on their children for support.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，过去可能危及生命的疾病，现在往往可以得到有效的治疗或控制，而养老金制度也让很多老年人退休后不用完全依赖子女的经济支持。

entries.text: What can young and old people learn from each other?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think young people can learn valuable life experience from the old, while older people can learn about new technology and fresh perspectives from the young.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得年轻人可以从老年人身上学到宝贵的人生经验，而老年人也可以从年轻人身上学到新科技和新观念。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Older people have gone through decades of real-life situations, so they often have practical wisdom that can't be learned from books, while young people grow up alongside rapid technological and social changes, giving them a more up-to-date understanding of the modern world.
ideaNotes.textZh: 老年人经历过几十年的真实生活情境，往往拥有书本上学不到的实用智慧，而年轻人是伴随着快速的科技和社会变化成长的，因此对现代世界有更新的理解。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, a grandparent might share advice on handling difficult relationships or staying patient during hard times, while a grandchild might teach them how to use a smartphone or video call family members.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，祖辈可能会分享如何处理复杂的人际关系或在困难时期保持耐心的经验，而孙辈可能会教他们怎么用智能手机或视频通话联系家人。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: This kind of mutual learning also helps strengthen family bonds, since it gives both generations a reason to spend time together and appreciate what the other brings.
ideaNotes.textZh: 这种互相学习也有助于加深家庭纽带，因为这让两代人都有理由花时间在一起，欣赏对方的价值。

entries.text: Do you think people should learn ancient history before learning modern history?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: Yes, I think it makes sense to learn ancient history first, before moving on to modern history.
ideaNotes.textZh: 是的，我觉得先学古代史，再学现代史是比较合理的顺序。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Historical events don't happen in isolation — modern situations are often the direct result of what came before, so without a basic understanding of the past, it's hard to fully grasp why things are the way they are today.
ideaNotes.textZh: 历史事件不是孤立发生的——现代的很多状况往往是之前事件直接造成的结果，如果不了解过去的基本情况，就很难真正理解今天的事情为什么会是这样。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, it's hard to understand why certain countries have complicated relationships today without first knowing about colonial history or past wars between them.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，如果不先了解它们之间的殖民历史或历次战争，就很难理解为什么某些国家今天的关系会如此复杂。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: That said, I don't think this needs to be super strict — sometimes jumping into a recent event first can actually spark curiosity, which then motivates someone to go back and explore its roots.
ideaNotes.textZh: 不过，我觉得这个顺序也不用太死板——有时候先接触一个近期事件，反而能激发好奇心，从而促使人们回头去探索它的根源。

Historical events don't happen in isolation — modern situations are often the direct result of what came before, so without a basic understanding of the past, it's hard to fully grasp why things are the way they are today.
For instance, it's hard to understand why certain countries have complicated relationships today without first knowing about colonial history or past wars between them.
That said, I don't think this needs to be super strict — sometimes jumping into a recent event first can actually spark curiosity, which then motivates someone to go back and explore its roots.
paragraphsZh: 是的，我觉得先学古代史，再学现代史是比较合理的顺序。
历史事件不是孤立发生的——现代的很多状况往往是之前事件直接造成的结果，如果不了解过去的基本情况，就很难真正理解今天的事情为什么会是这样。
比如，如果不先了解它们之间的殖民历史或历次战争，就很难理解为什么某些国家今天的关系会如此复杂。
不过，我觉得这个顺序也不用太死板——有时候先接触一个近期事件，反而能激发好奇心，从而促使人们回头去探索它的根源。

entries.text: How do children learn history before they attend school?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think before starting school, children mostly learn history through family stories and traditional celebrations, rather than any formal lessons.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得在上学之前，孩子大多是通过家庭故事和传统节日来接触历史，而不是通过任何正式的课程。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: At that age, kids absorb information best through things that feel personal and emotional, so hearing a grandparent talk about the past sticks with them far more than reading a fact from a book would.
ideaNotes.textZh: 在这个年龄段，孩子最容易通过贴近个人、带有情感的方式吸收信息，所以听祖辈讲过去的事，会比从书本上读到一个事实更让他们印象深刻。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, a grandparent telling a child what life was like when they were young, or a family celebrating a traditional festival, quietly introduces the idea that things used to be different.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，祖辈告诉孩子他们年轻时的生活是什么样的，或者一家人一起庆祝传统节日，都会不知不觉地让孩子明白过去的生活和现在不一样。

entries.text: Do you think children should begin learning history from an early age?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: Yes, I think it's a good idea for children to be introduced to history from an early age, even in a very simple way.
ideaNotes.textZh: 是的，我觉得孩子从小就接触历史是件好事，哪怕方式非常简单。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Learning history early helps children build a sense of where they come from, and this kind of foundation is much easier to plant when kids are still forming their sense of identity, rather than trying to introduce it later.
ideaNotes.textZh: 从小学习历史能帮助孩子建立一种自己从何而来的意识，而这种基础在孩子还在形成身份认同的阶段更容易培养起来，而不是等长大后才引入。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, a child who grows up hearing simple stories about their country's past or their own family history tends to develop a stronger sense of belonging than one who's never exposed to it until a school textbook shows up.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，一个从小听着关于国家过去或自己家族历史简单故事长大的孩子，往往会比一个直到课本出现才第一次接触历史的孩子，拥有更强的归属感。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: That said, the approach really matters — forcing memorization too early could actually make kids associate history with boredom instead of curiosity.
ideaNotes.textZh: 不过，方式其实很关键——如果太早强迫死记硬背，反而可能让孩子把历史和无聊联系在一起，而不是好奇心。

entries.text: Describe a popular person

paragraphs: The person I'd like to talk about is an old man in my hometown, Mr Wang. About a month ago, I came across a local TV interview with him online.

Through that interview, I found out that he used to be a history teacher — that's actually why he loves history so much, it's been part of his life for decades. After retiring, he started doing hands-on research instead of just reading books.

It wasn't easy — a lot of the old people who lived through that time were very old, some had already passed away, so it got harder to find information. He didn't have much money or support from his family, but he just kept going, little by little, year after year, and eventually published a book and held an exhibition about his research — and that's how he became popular in my hometown.
That interview really stayed with me for a long time. I realized his success didn't come from luck, but from genuine passion for history.
Later, I went to his exhibition and got to meet him in person. We talked for a bit, but I still wanted to know more about how he'd kept going all these years.

Mr Wang was really friendly — he invited me to his house, and we spent some time going through his old photos together, listening to him talk about the stories behind them. I really admire this old man — what he did wasn't easy, there was no money or fame in it, just real passion, and he succeeded in the end.
He saved a lot of local history that could've been forgotten, and getting to know him a bit made me respect him even more.
paragraphsZh: 我想说的这个人是我们家乡的一位老爷爷，王爷爷。 大概一个月前，我在网上刷到了当地电视台对他的一个采访。
通过这个采访我了解到，他以前是一名历史老师——这也是他这么喜欢历史的原因，历史几十年来一直是他生活的一部分。 退休之后，他开始做实地研究，而不只是看书。
这个过程并不容易——很多经历过那段历史的老人年纪都很大了，有些已经去世了，资料越来越难找。 他也没有太多经费，家里人也不是很支持，但他还是一点一点坚持了下来，一年又一年，最后出版了一本关于他研究的书，还办了一个展览——这也是他在我们家乡出名的原因。
那个采访让我印象特别深，一直记了很久。 我意识到他的成功不是靠运气，而是因为他对历史真正的热爱。
后来，我去了他的展览，见到了他本人。 我们聊了一会儿，但我还是很想多了解一下他这些年是怎么坚持下来的。
王爷爷人特别友好——他邀请我去他家，我们一起翻看他的老照片，听他讲照片背后的故事。 我真的很佩服这位老爷爷——他做的事情并不容易，没有钱也没有名利，纯粹是出于热爱，最后他成功了。
他保留了很多本来可能会被遗忘的本地历史，认识他之后，我对他更尊敬了。

entries.text: Why do people want to be popular?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think people want to be popular mainly because it gives them a sense of belonging and being liked by others.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得人们想要受欢迎，主要是因为这能带给他们一种归属感和被别人喜欢的感觉。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Humans are naturally social creatures, so when others enjoy being around us, it confirms that we're accepted, which feels good on a basic emotional level.
ideaNotes.textZh: 人类天生就是社会性动物，所以当别人喜欢和我们相处时，这证明我们是被接纳的，这种感觉在情感层面很基本也很好。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, someone who's often invited to social gatherings or has people reach out to them just to catch up tends to feel that warm, reassuring sense of being truly wanted.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，一个经常被邀请参加社交聚会，或者常有人主动联系闲聊近况的人，往往会有一种温暖、安心的感觉，觉得自己真的被需要。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: That said, chasing popularity too much can backfire, since it might push someone to change who they are just to please others.
ideaNotes.textZh: 不过，过度追求受欢迎也可能适得其反，因为这可能会让一个人为了取悦别人而改变自己本来的样子。

entries.text: Is it easier to become popular nowadays?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: Yes, I think it's actually become easier to become popular nowadays, mainly because of social media.
ideaNotes.textZh: 是的，我觉得现在变得受欢迎其实更容易了，主要是因为社交媒体。

ideaNotes.text: In the past, popularity was limited to the people you physically interacted with, but now a single post can reach thousands of strangers, so gaining attention doesn't take nearly as much time.

entries.text: What are the qualities of being a good teacher?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think the most important quality of a good teacher is patience, along with genuinely caring about students.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得一位好老师最重要的品质是耐心，再加上真正地关心学生。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Real learning requires students to feel comfortable enough to fail, and a teacher's patience and care are what create that kind of safe space. Without it, students often get too scared to even try.
ideaNotes.textZh: 真正的学习需要学生有足够的安全感去犯错，而老师的耐心和关心正是营造这种安全空间的关键。没有这种氛围，学生常常会害怕到根本不敢尝试。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, a student who's confused about a topic might stay quiet in a strict classroom, but feel comfortable raising their hand and asking "silly" questions in a class led by a patient, caring teacher.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，一个对某个知识点感到困惑的学生，在一个严格的课堂上可能会保持沉默，但在一位耐心、关心学生的老师带领的课堂上，会更愿意举手提出一些"傻问题"。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: Beyond patience, a good teacher also needs to be able to explain things clearly, since even the most caring teacher won't help much if students can't follow the lesson.
ideaNotes.textZh: 除了耐心，好老师还需要能够清晰地讲解内容，因为即使是最关心学生的老师，如果学生跟不上课，也帮不上太大的忙。

entries.text: Do you think good teachers are always popular among students?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: No, I don't think good teachers are always popular among students.
ideaNotes.textZh: 不，我不认为好老师总是受学生欢迎。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: A good teacher sometimes has to push students or hold them accountable, and students don't always enjoy that in the moment, even if it's genuinely for their own benefit.
ideaNotes.textZh: 一位好老师有时候必须督促学生或让他们承担责任，而学生当下并不总是喜欢这样，即使这确实是为了他们好。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, a teacher who gives strict deadlines and doesn't accept late homework might be seen as too harsh by some students, even though this actually helps them build good habits.

entries.text: Which group pays more attention to health , young people or old people ?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think older people generally pay more attention to their health than young people.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得老年人通常比年轻人更关注自己的健康。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: As people age, they often start experiencing physical decline or health issues firsthand, which makes health feel urgent and real, rather than just something to worry about later.
ideaNotes.textZh: 随着年龄增长，人们常常会亲身经历身体机能的衰退或健康问题，这会让健康感觉变得紧迫而真实，而不只是以后才需要担心的事。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, an older person might carefully track their blood pressure and adjust their diet accordingly, while a young person might ignore minor symptoms and just push through them.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，一位老年人可能会仔细监测自己的血压并相应调整饮食，而一个年轻人可能会忽视一些小症状，直接硬扛过去。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: That said, more young people today are also becoming health-conscious, especially with the rise of fitness culture and social media promoting healthy lifestyles.
ideaNotes.textZh: 不过，现在也有越来越多年轻人开始注重健康，尤其是随着健身文化的兴起，以及社交媒体对健康生活方式的宣传。

entries.text: Describe an enjoyable evening you had with your friends

paragraphs: An enjoyable evening I had with a friend was the night of her birthday. We were classmates in high school, and we've known each other for five or six years.

After graduation, she didn't end up working in her original major — instead, she followed her interest in photography and became a professional photographer. Her job now is basically traveling to different tourist spots in China to take portrait photos.
I really admire her for that — not many people have the courage to go after what they're passionate about. I remember once she posted on WeChat Moments saying she really wanted a new lens.

She said the lens takes really nice photos, especially for portraits, but it was pretty expensive, so she kept putting it off. It happened to be close to her birthday, so I decided to save up and buy her that lens.
Honestly, it wasn't as hard as I thought — I just cut back on bubble tea, and started cooking instead of ordering takeout. And it actually made me healthier too, which I didn't really expect.
Right before her birthday, I finally saved up enough money and bought the lens. Even though it was a gift for someone else, I felt genuinely happy myself — like I couldn't wait to see her reaction.
On the night of her birthday, I organized a small gathering for her — we went to a Western restaurant inside a shopping mall in the city centre. There were about five or six of us, all close friends.
We ordered loads of food, talked and laughed for ages. Then came the gift — I pulled out the lens, and she was so surprised.

She said it was exactly what she'd been wanting, and we immediately tested it out by taking loads of photos together. It was such an enjoyable and memorable evening for me — not just because of the food or the photos, but because of the moment we all shared together.
Seeing her that happy and surprised made everything — all the saving up, all the planning — feel completely worth it.
paragraphsZh: 我和朋友度过的一个愉快夜晚，是她生日那天晚上。 我们是高中同学，认识五六年了。
毕业之后，她并没有从事本专业，而是追随自己对摄影的兴趣，成为了一名职业摄影师。 她现在的工作基本就是去中国各地的旅游景点拍人像照片。
我真的很佩服她——不是每个人都有勇气去追求自己热爱的事情。 我记得有一次她在朋友圈发说很想要一个新镜头。
她说这个镜头拍出来的照片特别好，尤其适合拍人像，但是价格挺贵的，所以她一直没舍得买。 当时刚好快到她生日了，所以我就决定攒钱给她买那个镜头。
说实话，没有我想象中那么难——我就是少喝点奶茶，开始自己做饭而不是点外卖。 而且这样也意外地让我变得更健康了。
生日前，我终于攒够了钱，买到了这个镜头。 虽然这是送给别人的礼物，但我自己也真的很开心——就是那种迫不及待想看她反应的感觉。
在她生日的晚上，我为她组织了一个小型聚会——我们去了市中心一家商场里的西餐厅。 大概有五六个人，都是好朋友。
我们点了很多食物，聊天、大笑了好久。 然后到了送礼物的环节——我拿出了镜头，她非常惊讶。
她说这正是她一直想要的，我们立刻就试用了起来，一起拍了很多照片。 这真的是一个非常愉快、让我印象深刻的夜晚——不只是因为美食或照片，而是因为我们一起分享的那个特别时刻。
看到她那么开心和惊喜，让我觉得之前所有的攒钱和计划都完全值得了。

entries.text: Why do people need friends?

ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得人们需要朋友，主要是因为朋友能提供家庭或工作关系有时无法给予的情感支持。

ideaNotes.text: Friends are chosen freely, rather than being tied by blood or obligation, so the connection often feels more genuine, giving people a safe space to be themselves.

entries.text: Do older people prefer spending time with family or with friends?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think older people generally prefer spending time with family, rather than friends.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得老年人通常更喜欢和家人待在一起，而不是朋友。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: As people get older, many of their old friends may have moved away, gotten sick, or passed away, while family, especially children and grandchildren, tend to stay a constant presence in their lives.
ideaNotes.textZh: 随着年龄增长，很多老朋友可能搬走了、生病了，或者已经过世了，而家人，尤其是子女和孙辈，往往会一直持续陪伴在他们身边。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, an elderly person might have lost touch with several old classmates over the years due to distance or health issues, but their grandchildren are still just a phone call or short drive away.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，一位老年人可能因为距离或健康问题，多年来和几位老同学渐渐失去了联系，但他们的孙辈依然近在咫尺，一个电话或短途车程就能见到。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: That said, friendships still matter for older people, since peers who share similar life experiences can offer a kind of understanding that family sometimes can't.

entries.text: What are the differences between young people’s leisure time activities and those of old people?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think young people tend to enjoy more active and social activities, while older people usually prefer something calmer and slower-paced.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得年轻人往往更喜欢活跃、社交性强的活动，而老年人通常更喜欢平静、节奏慢一些的活动。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Younger people often have more physical energy and enjoy new stimulation, so they're drawn to things that are exciting or social, while older people tend to value comfort and relaxation more after years of a busier life.
ideaNotes.textZh: 年轻人往往有更多体力，也喜欢新鲜的刺激，所以更容易被那些令人兴奋或社交性强的活动吸引，而老年人在经历了多年更忙碌的生活后，往往更看重舒适和放松。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, a young person might spend their weekend at a concert or playing sports with friends, while an older person might prefer gardening or having tea with a few close friends.

entries.text: What can we do to bring family members closer together?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think one of the best ways to bring family members closer is to do shared activities together on a regular basis.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得让家人更亲密的最好方法之一，就是定期一起做一些共同的活动。

ideaNotes.label: 解释

entries.text: How do people get along in a big family?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think people in a big family get along mainly by practicing mutual respect and being willing to compromise.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得在大家庭中，人们主要是通过相互尊重和愿意妥协来相处的。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: With more people involved, there are naturally more different opinions and habits, so without some level of tolerance, small disagreements could easily turn into bigger conflicts.

entries.text: Describe a person you know who really likes taking photos

paragraphs: The person I'd like to talk about is my friend — she really loves taking photos. We were classmates in high school, and we've known each other for five or six years.

After graduation, she didn't end up working in her original major — instead, she followed her interest in photography and became a professional photographer. Her job now is basically traveling to different tourist spots in China to take portrait photos.
I really admire her for that — not many people have the courage to go after what they're passionate about. I remember once she posted on WeChat Moments saying she really wanted a new lens.

She said the lens takes really nice photos, especially for portraits, but it was pretty expensive, so she kept putting it off. It happened to be close to her birthday, so I decided to save up and buy her that lens.
Honestly, it wasn't as hard as I thought — I just cut back on bubble tea, and started cooking instead of ordering takeout. And it actually made me healthier too, which I didn't really expect.
Right before her birthday, I finally saved up enough money and bought the lens. Even though it was a gift for someone else, I felt genuinely happy myself — like I couldn't wait to see her reaction.
On the night of her birthday, I organized a small gathering for her — we went to a Western restaurant inside a shopping mall in the city centre. There were about five or six of us, all close friends.
We ordered loads of food, talked and laughed for ages. Then came the gift — I pulled out the lens, and she was so surprised.

She said it was exactly what she'd been wanting, and we immediately tested it out by taking loads of photos together. It was such an enjoyable and memorable evening for me — not just because of the food or the photos, but because of the moment we all shared together.
Seeing her that happy and surprised made everything — all the saving up, all the planning — feel completely worth it.
paragraphsZh: 我想说的这个人是我的朋友——她非常喜欢拍照。 我们是高中同学，认识五六年了。
毕业之后，她并没有从事本专业，而是追随自己对摄影的兴趣，成为了一名职业摄影师。 她现在的工作基本就是去中国各地的旅游景点拍人像照片。
我真的很佩服她——不是每个人都有勇气去追求自己热爱的事情。 我记得有一次她在朋友圈发说很想要一个新镜头。
她说这个镜头拍出来的照片特别好，尤其适合拍人像，但是价格挺贵的，所以她一直没舍得买。 当时刚好快到她生日了，所以我就决定攒钱给她买那个镜头。
说实话，没有我想象中那么难——我就是少喝点奶茶，开始自己做饭而不是点外卖。 而且这样也意外地让我变得更健康了。
生日前，我终于攒够了钱，买到了这个镜头。 虽然这是送给别人的礼物，但我自己也真的很开心——就是那种迫不及待想看她反应的感觉。
在她生日的晚上，我为她组织了一个小型聚会——我们去了市中心一家商场里的西餐厅。 大概有五六个人，都是好朋友。
我们点了很多食物，聊天、大笑了好久。 然后到了送礼物的环节——我拿出了镜头，她非常惊讶。
她说这正是她一直想要的，我们立刻就试用了起来，一起拍了很多照片。 这真的是一个非常愉快、让我印象深刻的夜晚——不只是因为美食或照片，而是因为我们一起分享的那个特别时刻。
看到她那么开心和惊喜，让我觉得之前所有的攒钱和计划都完全值得了。

entries.text: Some people don't mind others walking into their shot when they're taking photos.What do you think ?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think whether someone minds this has a lot to do with their general personality, rather than the situation itself.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得一个人会不会介意这件事，很大程度上跟他们的整体性格有关，而不只是当下的情况。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: People who are naturally more easy-going tend to let small things slide without getting bothered, while people who are more detail-oriented notice these little disruptions more easily and find it harder to just let go.
ideaNotes.textZh: 天生比较随和的人往往不会因为小事而心烦，而更注重细节的人则更容易注意到这些小干扰，也更难释怀。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, a laid-back person might just keep the photo as it is, even with a stranger in the background, while someone more particular would feel genuinely frustrated and insist on redoing the shot until it looks right.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，一个随和的人可能会直接留着这张照片，哪怕背景里有个陌生人，而一个比较讲究的人则会真的感到沮丧，坚持要重新拍一张直到满意为止。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: This attitude can also reflect how someone deals with imperfection in other areas of life, like being fine with a messy room or a small mistake in their work.
ideaNotes.textZh: 这种态度也能反映一个人在生活其他方面如何看待不完美，比如能不能接受房间有点乱，或者工作中的一点小失误。

entries.text: What are the downsides of constantly taking photos while traveling ?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think the biggest downside of constantly taking photos while traveling is that it can take away from actually experiencing the moment.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得旅行时不停拍照最大的坏处，就是会让人无法真正沉浸在当下。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: When someone is too focused on capturing the perfect shot, their attention shifts from the actual scene in front of them to the screen of their phone or camera, so they end up remembering the trip through photos rather than genuine memories.
ideaNotes.textZh: 当一个人太专注于拍出完美的照片，注意力就会从眼前真实的场景转移到手机或相机屏幕上，结果他们记住这趟旅行靠的是照片，而不是真实的记忆。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, someone visiting a beautiful waterfall might spend the whole time adjusting angles and filters to get the right shot, and later realize they can't even recall what it felt like standing there in person.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，一个去参观美丽瀑布的人可能整段时间都在调整角度和滤镜来拍出好照片，之后才发现自己甚至不记得亲身站在那里的感受是什么。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: On top of that, constantly stopping to take photos can also slow down the whole group, especially when traveling with others who are eager to keep moving and see more places.
ideaNotes.textZh: 除此之外，不停停下来拍照也会拖慢整个团队的节奏，尤其是和急着继续前进、想看更多地方的同伴一起旅行时。
