entries.text: Do you think it’s ok to take photos everywhere?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: No, I don't think it's okay to take photos everywhere — it really depends on the location and whether it respects other people's privacy.
ideaNotes.textZh: 不，我不觉得可以到处拍照——这其实要看地点，以及是否尊重了别人的隐私。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Some places have rules against photography for safety or legal reasons, and even where it's technically allowed, snapping photos of strangers without asking can make people feel uncomfortable or like their privacy is being invaded.
ideaNotes.textZh: 有些地方出于安全或法律原因禁止拍照，即使在允许拍照的地方，未经允许拍摄陌生人也会让对方感到不舒服，觉得自己的隐私被侵犯了。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, many museums or religious sites ban photography to protect the artwork or maintain a respectful atmosphere, and taking a photo of a stranger's child at a park without permission could easily make the parents feel uneasy.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，很多博物馆或宗教场所禁止拍照，是为了保护展品或维护庄重的氛围，而在公园里未经允许拍陌生人的孩子，也很容易让家长感到不安。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: That said, in public spaces where there's no clear rule, I think it comes down to being mindful — like avoiding people's faces or asking first if you want to include someone in your shot.
ideaNotes.textZh: 不过，在没有明确规定的公共场所，我觉得关键在于有分寸——比如避免拍到别人的脸，或者想把某人拍进画面时先问一下对方。

entries.text: What kind of photos do people often take?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think people mostly take photos of everyday moments, like food, pets, or scenery, but also of special occasions like birthdays or trips.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得人们大多拍的是日常瞬间，比如美食、宠物或风景，但也会拍特殊场合，比如生日或旅行。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: This is because photos are basically a way to hold onto something, so people naturally photograph whatever feels worth remembering at that moment, whether it's something small and fun or a bigger milestone.
ideaNotes.textZh: 这是因为照片本质上是一种留住某样东西的方式，所以人们自然会拍下当下觉得值得记住的东西，不管是小小的有趣瞬间还是重大的里程碑。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, someone might snap a quick photo of their coffee at a cute cafe just because it looks nice, but also take dozens of photos during a wedding to make sure the important moments are properly captured.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，有人可能只是因为好看就随手拍一张咖啡店里的咖啡，但在婚礼上却会拍几十张照片，确保重要的瞬间都被好好记录下来。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: With social media now being such a big part of life, a lot of photos are also taken specifically to be shared online, rather than just kept for personal memory.
ideaNotes.textZh: 随着社交媒体成为生活中很重要的一部分，很多照片现在也是专门为了分享到网上而拍的，而不只是留作个人记忆。

This is because photos are basically a way to hold onto something, so people naturally photograph whatever feels worth remembering at that moment, whether it's something small and fun or a bigger milestone.

For instance, someone might snap a quick photo of their coffee at a cute cafe just because it looks nice, but also take dozens of photos during a wedding to make sure the important moments are properly captured.
With social media now being such a big part of life, a lot of photos are also taken specifically to be shared online, rather than just kept for personal memory.

entries.text: Describe a time when you saved money to buy something you wanted

paragraphs: We were classmates in high school, and we've known each other for five or six years. After graduation, she didn't end up working in her original major — instead, she followed her interest in photography and became a professional photographer.

Her job now is basically traveling to different tourist spots in China to take portrait photos. I really admire her for that — not many people have the courage to go after what they're passionate about.

I remember once she posted on WeChat Moments saying she really wanted a new lens. She said the lens takes really nice photos, especially for portraits, but it was pretty expensive, so she kept putting it off.

It happened to be close to her birthday, so I decided to save up and buy her that lens. Honestly, it wasn't as hard as I thought — I just cut back on bubble tea, and started cooking instead of ordering takeout.
And it actually made me healthier too, which I didn't really expect. Right before her birthday, I finally saved up enough money and bought the lens.

Even though it was a gift for someone else, I felt genuinely happy myself — like I couldn't wait to see her reaction. On the night of her birthday, I organized a small gathering for her — we went to a Western restaurant inside a shopping mall in the city centre.
There were about five or six of us, all close friends. We ordered loads of food, talked and laughed for ages.
Then came the gift — I pulled out the lens, and she was so surprised. She said it was exactly what she'd been wanting, and we immediately tested it out by taking loads of photos together.

It was such an enjoyable and memorable evening for me — not just because of the food or the photos, but because of the moment we all shared together. Seeing her that happy and surprised made everything — all the saving up, all the planning — feel completely worth it.
paragraphsZh: 我们是高中同学，认识五六年了。 毕业之后，她并没有从事本专业，而是追随自己对摄影的兴趣，成为了一名职业摄影师。
她现在的工作基本就是去中国各地的旅游景点拍人像照片。 我真的很佩服她——不是每个人都有勇气去追求自己热爱的事情。
我记得有一次她在朋友圈发说很想要一个新镜头。 她说这个镜头拍出来的照片特别好，尤其适合拍人像，但是价格挺贵的，所以她一直没舍得买。
当时刚好快到她生日了，所以我就决定攒钱给她买那个镜头。 说实话，没有我想象中那么难——我就是少喝点奶茶，开始自己做饭而不是点外卖。
而且这样也意外地让我变得更健康了。 生日前，我终于攒够了钱，买到了这个镜头。
虽然这是送给别人的礼物，但我自己也真的很开心——就是那种迫不及待想看她反应的感觉。 在她生日的晚上，我为她组织了一个小型聚会——我们去了市中心一家商场里的西餐厅。
大概有五六个人，都是好朋友。 我们点了很多食物，聊天、大笑了好久。
然后到了送礼物的环节——我拿出了镜头，她非常惊讶。 她说这正是她一直想要的，我们立刻就试用了起来，一起拍了很多照片。
这真的是一个非常愉快、让我印象深刻的夜晚——不只是因为美食或照片，而是因为我们一起分享的那个特别时刻。 看到她那么开心和惊喜，让我觉得之前所有的攒钱和计划都完全值得了。

entries.text: What kind of things do people usually save money for?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think people usually save money for big purchases, like a house or a car, but also for future security, like emergencies or retirement.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得人们通常会为大件消费存钱，比如买房买车，但也会为未来保障存钱，比如应急或养老。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: These goals usually require more money than someone earns in a single month, so saving becomes the only realistic way to actually afford them over time.
ideaNotes.textZh: 这些目标通常需要比一个月收入多得多的钱，所以存钱就成了长期下来能真正负担得起的唯一现实方式。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, someone planning to buy an apartment might save a portion of their salary every month for years, while others might build up a rainy-day fund in case they lose their job.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，一个计划买房子的人可能会连续好几年每月存一部分工资，而另一些人可能会存一笔应急资金，以防失业。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: Beyond necessities, some people also save for experiences, like a big trip, since they'd rather spend the money on memories than material things.
ideaNotes.textZh: 除了必需品之外，有些人也会为体验存钱，比如一次大旅行，因为他们更愿意把钱花在回忆上，而不是物质上。

entries.text: Is it easier to spend money or save money?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think it's definitely easier to spend money than to save it.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得花钱肯定比存钱容易得多。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Spending gives people instant satisfaction, while saving requires giving up something enjoyable now for a reward that's far off in the future, and that kind of delayed payoff is naturally harder for people to stick to.
ideaNotes.textZh: 花钱能带来即时的满足感，而存钱需要放弃眼下的享受，去换取一个遥远未来的回报，这种延迟的回报天然就更难让人坚持。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, someone might plan to save a fixed amount every month, but end up breaking that plan the moment they see something they really want, like a new phone.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，有人可能计划每月存固定金额，但一看到自己真正想要的东西，比如新手机，就会打破这个计划。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: That said, saving can become easier with the right habits, like automatically transferring money into a separate account before it can be spent.
ideaNotes.textZh: 不过，如果养成正确的习惯，存钱也能变得容易一些，比如在钱花掉之前，就自动转到一个单独的账户里。

entries.text: Do you think it is easier to teach teenagers how to manage money when they are around 16 or 17 years old?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: Yes, I think 16 or 17 is actually a pretty good age to start teaching teenagers about managing money.
ideaNotes.textZh: 是的，我觉得16、17岁其实是开始教青少年理财挺不错的年龄。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: By this age, teenagers can already understand abstract concepts like saving and budgeting, and many of them are starting to earn or handle their own money, like allowances, which gives the lessons real practical value.
ideaNotes.textZh: 到了这个年龄，青少年已经能理解抽象的概念，比如储蓄和预算，很多人也开始自己挣钱或管理自己的钱，比如零花钱，这让这些道理有了实际的意义。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, a 16-year-old with a part-time job can immediately apply lessons about saving a portion of every paycheck, rather than just hearing the theory without any real experience.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，一个有兼职工作的16岁孩子，能立刻把关于每笔工资都存一部分的道理用起来，而不是只听理论、没有实际体验。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: On the other hand, waiting too late, like into someone's 20s, could mean they've already picked up some bad spending habits that are much harder to unlearn by then.
ideaNotes.textZh: 另一方面，如果等得太晚，比如拖到20多岁才开始教，可能那时他们已经养成了一些不良消费习惯，到那时再改就难得多了。

entries.text: Should parents teach their children to spend money freely or to save money?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think parents should teach a balance between the two, rather than pushing children toward only saving or only spending freely.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得父母应该教孩子在两者之间找到平衡，而不是一味推着孩子只存钱或只自由花钱。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: If a child only learns to save, they might grow up feeling anxious about spending on anything, but if they only learn to spend, they'll likely struggle later with financial planning.
ideaNotes.textZh: 如果孩子只学会存钱，长大后可能会对花任何钱都感到焦虑，但如果只学会花钱，以后很可能在财务规划上遇到困难。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, parents might give a child a set amount of pocket money and let them decide how much to spend on fun things versus how much to put toward a savings goal, like a toy they really want.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，父母可能会给孩子一笔固定的零花钱，让他们自己决定花多少在有趣的事情上，存多少去达成一个储蓄目标，比如他们真正想要的一个玩具。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: This approach also teaches children that money is a tool to manage, not something to fear or chase, which is a healthier mindset in the long run.
ideaNotes.textZh: 这种方式也能让孩子明白，钱是一种需要管理的工具，而不是要害怕或一味追逐的东西，这从长远来看是更健康的心态。

这种方式也能让孩子明白，钱是一种需要管理的工具，而不是要害怕或一味追逐的东西，这从长远来看是更健康的心态。

entries.text: Should schools teach children how to manage money from a young age?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: Yes, I think schools should definitely teach children how to manage money from a young age.
ideaNotes.textZh: 是的，我认为学校确实应该从小教孩子理财。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Money management is a practical life skill that almost everyone needs, yet it's often left out of formal education, so many people end up learning it the hard way, through mistakes, as adults.
ideaNotes.textZh: 理财是一项几乎每个人都需要的实用生活技能，但它却常常没有被纳入正规教育，所以很多人最终是长大后通过犯错、走弯路才学会的。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, a school might teach kids to create a simple budget for a class trip, helping them understand concepts like planning ahead and prioritizing spending in a hands-on way.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，学校可能会教孩子为一次班级旅行制定一份简单的预算，通过实际操作帮助他们理解提前规划和分配开支优先级这些概念。

entries.text: Describe an enjoyable evening you had with your friends

paragraphs: A party that really impressed me was a small birthday gathering I organized for my friend. We were classmates in high school, and we've known each other for five or six years.

After graduation, she didn't end up working in her original major — instead, she followed her interest in photography and became a professional photographer. Her job now is basically traveling to different tourist spots in China to take portrait photos.
I really admire her for that — not many people have the courage to go after what they're passionate about. I remember once she posted on WeChat Moments saying she really wanted a new lens.

She said the lens takes really nice photos, especially for portraits, but it was pretty expensive, so she kept putting it off. It happened to be close to her birthday, so I decided to save up and buy her that lens.
Honestly, it wasn't as hard as I thought — I just cut back on bubble tea, and started cooking instead of ordering takeout. And it actually made me healthier too, which I didn't really expect.
Right before her birthday, I finally saved up enough money and bought the lens. Even though it was a gift for someone else, I felt genuinely happy myself — like I couldn't wait to see her reaction.
On the night of her birthday, I organized a small gathering for her — we went to a Western restaurant inside a shopping mall in the city centre. There were about five or six of us, all close friends.
We ordered loads of food, talked and laughed for ages. Then came the gift — I pulled out the lens, and she was so surprised.

She said it was exactly what she'd been wanting, and we immediately tested it out by taking loads of photos together. It was such an enjoyable and memorable evening for me — not just because of the food or the photos, but because of the moment we all shared together.
Seeing her that happy and surprised made everything — all the saving up, all the planning — feel completely worth it.
paragraphsZh: 一个让我印象深刻的聚会，是我为朋友组织的一个小型生日聚会。 我们是高中同学，认识五六年了。
毕业之后，她并没有从事本专业，而是追随自己对摄影的兴趣，成为了一名职业摄影师。 她现在的工作基本就是去中国各地的旅游景点拍人像照片。
我真的很佩服她——不是每个人都有勇气去追求自己热爱的事情。 我记得有一次她在朋友圈发说很想要一个新镜头。
她说这个镜头拍出来的照片特别好，尤其适合拍人像，但是价格挺贵的，所以她一直没舍得买。 当时刚好快到她生日了，所以我就决定攒钱给她买那个镜头。
说实话，没有我想象中那么难——我就是少喝点奶茶，开始自己做饭而不是点外卖。 而且这样也意外地让我变得更健康了。
生日前，我终于攒够了钱，买到了这个镜头。 虽然这是送给别人的礼物，但我自己也真的很开心——就是那种迫不及待想看她反应的感觉。
在她生日的晚上，我为她组织了一个小型聚会——我们去了市中心一家商场里的西餐厅。 大概有五六个人，都是好朋友。
我们点了很多食物，聊天、大笑了好久。 然后到了送礼物的环节——我拿出了镜头，她非常惊讶。
她说这正是她一直想要的，我们立刻就试用了起来，一起拍了很多照片。 这真的是一个非常愉快、让我印象深刻的夜晚——不只是因为美食或照片，而是因为我们一起分享的那个特别时刻。
看到她那么开心和惊喜，让我觉得之前所有的攒钱和计划都完全值得了。

entries.text: What special events are celebrated in your country?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think Chinese New Year and the Mid-Autumn Festival are probably the most important special events celebrated in China.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得春节和中秋节大概是中国最重要的两个特殊节日。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: These festivals are deeply tied to family reunion and tradition, so they're not just holidays off work, but occasions when people make a real effort to come together.
ideaNotes.textZh: 这些节日和家庭团聚、传统文化紧密相连，所以它们不只是放假休息，更是人们真正努力聚在一起的时刻。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, during Chinese New Year, families gather for a big reunion dinner and set off fireworks, while during the Mid-Autumn Festival, people eat mooncakes together while looking at the full moon.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，在春节期间，家人会聚在一起吃年夜饭、放烟花，而在中秋节，人们会一起吃月饼、赏月。

entries.text: Do most people prefer to hold a party in a restaurant or in a pub?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think it really depends on the type of occasion, rather than one place always being preferred.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得这其实取决于场合的性质，而不是某一种场地永远更受欢迎。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: A restaurant feels more suitable for occasions that involve eating together and conversation, while a pub fits a more casual, relaxed vibe with drinks and music playing in the background.
ideaNotes.textZh: 餐厅更适合以一起吃饭、聊天为主的场合，而酒吧则更适合那种带着酒水和背景音乐、更随意放松的氛围。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, a birthday dinner with family would likely be held at a restaurant, while a casual gathering to celebrate finishing a big project might happen at a pub with coworkers.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，和家人一起过的生日晚餐通常会选在餐厅，而为了庆祝完成一个大项目、和同事一起的随性小聚则可能选在酒吧。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: That said, younger people in cities seem to be choosing pubs more often these days, as this kind of nightlife culture continues to grow.
ideaNotes.textZh: 不过，现在城市里的年轻人似乎越来越常选择酒吧，因为这种夜生活文化正在不断兴起。

entries.text: Do most people prefer to hold a party in a public place or a private place?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think most people actually prefer holding a party in a private place, like someone's home.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得大多数人其实更倾向于在私人场所办派对，比如某人的家里。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: A private space gives people more control and freedom, since they don't have to worry about noise complaints, closing times, or other strangers being around.
ideaNotes.textZh: 私人空间能给人更多的掌控权和自由，因为不用担心噪音投诉、打烊时间，或者周围有陌生人在场。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, someone hosting a small gathering at their apartment can play loud music and stay up as late as they want, unlike at a public venue that has fixed closing hours.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，一个在自己公寓举办小型聚会的人，可以随意播放大声音乐、想待多晚就待多晚，而不像公共场所那样有固定的打烊时间。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: That said, for bigger celebrations with lots of guests, a public venue is often more practical, simply because most homes don't have enough space.
ideaNotes.textZh: 不过，对于宾客较多的大型庆祝活动，公共场所往往更实用，单纯是因为大多数家里没有足够的空间。

entries.text: When do people like to hold a party?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think most people prefer to hold parties on weekends, or on days that mark something special, like a birthday.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得大多数人更喜欢在周末办派对，或者在有特殊意义的日子，比如生日。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Weekends give people the freedom to stay up late and enjoy themselves without worrying about work the next day, and special occasions naturally give people a reason to celebrate in the first place.
ideaNotes.textZh: 周末能给人自由，让人不用担心第二天上班就可以熬夜尽情享受，而特殊场合本身就自然给了人们一个庆祝的理由。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, a Saturday night is a popular choice for a casual get-together, while something like a wedding or graduation almost always calls for its own celebration regardless of the day of the week.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，周六晚上是举办随意小聚的热门选择，而像婚礼或毕业这样的事情，几乎总是会单独安排一场庆祝，不受星期几的限制。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: Public holidays are another popular time, since everyone already has time off, making it easier to gather a large group together.
ideaNotes.textZh: 公共假期也是另一个受欢迎的时机，因为大家都已经放假了，更容易把一大群人聚到一起。

entries.text: Describe a person who taught you a new skill

paragraphs: We were classmates in primary school and basically grew up together, so we've known each other for a really long time. She's probably the one who's best at making things by hand among all my friends.

She makes all kinds of things, like paper cuttings, little clay figures and handmade decorations. Her work is always really delicate, with lots of little details, even though she mainly uses basic materials like colored paper, scissors, glue and clay.
What impresses me most is the creativity she shows in her handicrafts. She notices little things in everyday life and combines different elements in unexpected ways to come up with her own designs.

She's not just following the same steps over and over again, but putting her own ideas and imagination into every piece. Her creativity helped her stand out in all kinds of handicraft competitions, and she won top prizes.

Inspired by her, I also became interested in handicrafts, especially paper cutting, so I asked her to teach me. She gave me a series of structured lessons on paper cutting at her home after school, and it was honestly one of the most memorable courses I've ever taken.

She started with the basics, showing me how to fold the paper properly and draw simple patterns before cutting them out. Then, as I got better, she taught me how to create more complicated designs with different shapes and layers.
She would demonstrate each step first, then let me try it on my own. I spent a lot of time practicing, and gradually, I got the hang of it.
The whole experience was not only fun but also gave me a real sense of achievement. I'm really grateful to her for teaching me this skill and encouraging me along the way.
paragraphsZh: 我想聊的这个人是我的童年好友。 我们是小学同学，基本上是一起长大的，所以我们已经认识很长时间了。
她可能是我所有朋友中最擅长手工制作的那一个。 她会制作各种各样的东西，比如剪纸、小泥塑和手工装饰品。
她的作品总是非常精致，有很多细节，尽管她主要使用一些基础材料，比如彩纸、剪刀、胶水和黏土。 最让我印象深刻的是她在手工作品中展现出的创造力。
她会留意日常生活中的小事，并以出人意料的方式将不同的元素结合起来，从而设计出自己的作品。 她并不是只会一遍又一遍地重复相同的步骤，而是会把自己的想法和想象力融入每一件作品中。
她的创造力帮助她在各种手工比赛中脱颖而出，并且获得了最高级别的奖项。 受到她的启发，我也开始对手工制作感兴趣，尤其是剪纸，所以我请她教我。
放学后，她在家里给我上了一系列系统的剪纸课程。 说实话，这是我上过的最令人难忘的课程之一。
她从基础知识开始教起，向我展示如何正确地折纸，以及如何画出简单的图案，然后再把它们剪下来。 后来，随着我的技术越来越好，她开始教我如何运用不同的形状和层次来制作更复杂的设计。
她会先示范每一个步骤，然后让我自己尝试。 我花了很多时间练习，渐渐地，我就掌握了窍门。
整个经历不仅很有趣，还让我获得了真正的成就感。 我真的很感激她教会我这项技能，并且一路上不断地鼓励我。

entries.text: Why is self-discipline important when learning a new skill?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think self-discipline is important because learning a new skill takes time, and not every day feels fun or motivating.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得自律很重要，因为学习一项新技能需要时间，不是每天都感觉有趣或有动力。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Without self-discipline, people tend to quit as soon as it gets boring or hard. But with it, they can keep going even when they don't feel like it.
ideaNotes.textZh: 没有自律，人们往往会一遇到无聊或困难就放弃。但有了自律，他们能在没有动力的时候也坚持下去。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, someone learning the piano might feel excited the first week, but self-discipline is what makes them keep practicing even when progress feels slow.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，一个学钢琴的人可能第一周会很兴奋，但让他们即使在进步很慢时也能坚持练习的，正是自律。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: Interestingly, self-discipline is also what helps people push through the hardest part, which is often right before things finally start to click.
ideaNotes.textZh: 有意思的是，自律也能帮助人们熬过最难的阶段，而这个阶段往往就在事情终于开窍之前。

entries.text: What are the differences between learning from a teacher and learning by oneself?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think the biggest difference is that a teacher gives you feedback, while learning by yourself gives you more freedom and flexibility.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得最大的区别是老师能给你反馈，而自学能给你更多自由和灵活性。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: A teacher can spot your mistakes right away and correct them, so you don't keep practicing the wrong thing. Learning alone means you decide your own pace and direction, but you might not notice your own mistakes.
ideaNotes.textZh: 老师能立刻发现你的错误并纠正，所以你不会一直练错。自学则是你自己决定节奏和方向，但可能注意不到自己的错误。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, someone learning guitar with a teacher will get corrected the moment their finger position is wrong, while someone learning from videos alone might repeat the same mistake for weeks without knowing it.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，一个跟老师学吉他的人，手指姿势一错就会被纠正，而一个只靠看视频自学的人，可能好几周都在重复同一个错误却不自知。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: That said, self-learning can build stronger problem-solving skills, since you're forced to figure things out on your own instead of relying on someone else.
ideaNotes.textZh: 不过，自学能培养更强的解决问题的能力，因为你被迫要靠自己去搞清楚问题，而不是依赖别人。

entries.text: How do adults learn a new skill?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think adults usually learn a new skill through structured practice, like taking a course or following an online plan, rather than just playing around.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得成年人学习新技能通常是通过结构化的练习，比如上课或跟着网课计划来学，而不是随便瞎摸索。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Adults have limited free time, so they tend to look for the most efficient way to learn, instead of learning through trial and error like a child might.
ideaNotes.textZh: 成年人空闲时间有限，所以他们更倾向于寻找最有效率的方式来学习，而不是像孩子那样靠不断试错。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, an adult wanting to learn cooking might follow a structured recipe course step by step, rather than just experimenting randomly in the kitchen.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，一个想学做饭的成年人可能会按部就班地跟着一套结构化的菜谱课程学，而不是在厨房里随意瞎试。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: On the other hand, adults often have to balance learning with work and family, so they may progress more slowly than someone with more free time.
ideaNotes.textZh: 另一方面，成年人常常要在学习和工作家庭之间找平衡，所以他们的进步可能比时间更充裕的人更慢一些。

entries.text: How can parents and teachers teach children new skills?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think the best way for parents and teachers to teach a new skill is by demonstrating it themselves and then giving encouragement as the child tries.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得父母和老师教孩子新技能最好的方式，就是亲自示范，然后在孩子尝试时给予鼓励。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Children learn a lot by watching and copying, so seeing an adult do something correctly gives them a clear model to follow. But without encouragement, kids might give up quickly when they struggle.
ideaNotes.textZh: 孩子很多时候是通过观察和模仿来学习的，所以看到大人正确地做某件事，能给他们一个清晰的模仿对象。但如果没有鼓励，孩子遇到困难时可能会很快放弃。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, a parent teaching a child to ride a bike might show them how to balance first, then keep cheering them on even after a few falls.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，一个教孩子骑自行车的家长可能会先示范怎么保持平衡，然后即使孩子摔了几次也一直给他们加油打气。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: Breaking the skill into small, manageable steps also helps a lot, since kids don't feel as overwhelmed trying to learn everything at once.
ideaNotes.textZh: 把技能拆成小而容易掌握的步骤也很有帮助，因为孩子不会因为要一次学会所有东西而感到不知所措。

entries.text: Where can children learn new skills?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think children mostly learn new skills at school and at home, though nowadays they can also learn through online videos.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得孩子学新技能主要是在学校和家里，不过现在他们也能通过网上视频来学习。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: School gives kids a structured environment with a teacher guiding them, while home is where they usually get more one-on-one attention and can practice without pressure.
ideaNotes.textZh: 学校给孩子提供了一个有老师指导的结构化环境，而在家通常能得到更多一对一的关注，也可以没有压力地练习。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, a child might learn basic swimming techniques at school during PE class, but then get extra help from a parent at a local pool on weekends.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，一个孩子可能在学校体育课上学习基本的游泳技巧，然后周末在附近的泳池得到家长额外的帮助。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: These days, kids can also pick up skills from social media tutorials, like on Xiaohongshu, which gives them access to things their school or family might not be able to teach.
ideaNotes.textZh: 现在，孩子也能从社交媒体教程中学到技能，比如在小红书上，这让他们能接触到学校或家庭可能教不了的东西。

entries.text: Why should children learn new skills?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think children should learn new skills because it helps build their confidence and gives them more options later in life.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得孩子应该学习新技能，因为这能帮助他们建立自信，也能让他们以后有更多选择。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Every time a child masters something new, they prove to themselves that effort actually leads to results, and this feeling carries over into how they approach other challenges too.
ideaNotes.textZh: 每次孩子掌握一项新技能，都会让他们证明给自己看，努力真的能带来结果，而这种感觉也会延续到他们面对其他挑战的方式上。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, a child who learns to play an instrument and gets better over time might start believing they can also improve at other difficult things, like math or sports.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，一个学习演奏乐器并逐渐进步的孩子，可能会开始相信自己在其他困难的事情上也能进步，比如数学或体育。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: Learning a variety of skills when young can also help kids discover what they're naturally good at, which can guide them toward a future career or hobby.
ideaNotes.textZh: 从小学习各种技能，也能帮助孩子发现自己天生擅长什么，这能引导他们未来的职业或爱好方向。

paragraphs: I think children should learn new skills because it helps build their confidence and gives them more options later in life.
Every time a child masters something new, they prove to themselves that effort actually leads to results, and this feeling carries over into how they approach other challenges too.
For instance, a child who learns to play an instrument and gets better over time might start believing they can also improve at other difficult things, like math or sports.
Learning a variety of skills when young can also help kids discover what they're naturally good at, which can guide them toward a future career or hobby.

entries.text: Describe a person who is good at making things by hand

paragraphs: The person I'd like to talk about is my childhood friend. We were classmates in primary school and basically grew up together, so we've known each other for a really long time.
She's probably the one who's best at making things by hand among all my friends. She makes all kinds of things, like paper cuttings, little clay figures and handmade decorations.

Her work is always really delicate, with lots of little details, even though she mainly uses basic materials like colored paper, scissors, glue and clay. What impresses me most is the creativity she shows in her handicrafts.

She notices little things in everyday life and combines different elements in unexpected ways to come up with her own designs. She's not just following the same steps over and over again, but putting her own ideas and imagination into every piece.

Her creativity helped her stand out in all kinds of handicraft competitions, and she won top prizes. Inspired by her, I also became interested in handicrafts, especially paper cutting, so I asked her to teach me.

She gave me a series of structured lessons on paper cutting at her home after school, and it was honestly one of the most memorable courses I've ever taken. She started with the basics, showing me how to fold the paper properly and draw simple patterns before cutting them out.
Then, as I got better, she taught me how to create more complicated designs with different shapes and layers. She would demonstrate each step first, then let me try it on my own.
I spent a lot of time practicing, and gradually, I got the hang of it. The whole experience was not only fun but also gave me a real sense of achievement.
I'm really grateful to her for teaching me this skill and encouraging me along the way.
paragraphsZh: 我想聊的这个人是我的童年好友。 我们是小学同学，基本上是一起长大的，所以我们已经认识很长时间了。
她可能是我所有朋友中最擅长手工制作的那一个。 她会制作各种各样的东西，比如剪纸、小泥塑和手工装饰品。
她的作品总是非常精致，有很多细节，尽管她主要使用一些基础材料，比如彩纸、剪刀、胶水和黏土。 最让我印象深刻的是她在手工作品中展现出的创造力。
她会留意日常生活中的小事，并以出人意料的方式将不同的元素结合起来，从而设计出自己的作品。 她并不是只会一遍又一遍地重复相同的步骤，而是会把自己的想法和想象力融入每一件作品中。
她的创造力帮助她在各种手工比赛中脱颖而出，并且获得了最高级别的奖项。 受到她的启发，我也开始对手工制作感兴趣，尤其是剪纸，所以我请她教我。
放学后，她在家里给我上了一系列系统的剪纸课程。 说实话，这是我上过的最令人难忘的课程之一。
她从基础知识开始教起，向我展示如何正确地折纸，以及如何画出简单的图案，然后再把它们剪下来。 后来，随着我的技术越来越好，她开始教我如何运用不同的形状和层次来制作更复杂的设计。
她会先示范每一个步骤，然后让我自己尝试。 我花了很多时间练习，渐渐地，我就掌握了窍门。
整个经历不仅很有趣，还让我获得了真正的成就感。 我真的很感激她教会我这项技能，并且一路上不断地鼓励我。

entries.text: Does art, like music or theater, have an impact on society?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: Yes, I think art definitely has a real impact on society, since it goes beyond just entertainment.
ideaNotes.textZh: 是的，我觉得艺术对社会确实有真实的影响，因为它不只是娱乐那么简单。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Art gives people a shared way to express emotions and ideas that are hard to put into everyday words, so it often brings people together around a common feeling or message, even if they've never met.
ideaNotes.textZh: 艺术给了人们一种共同的方式来表达情感和想法，这些东西在日常语言中很难表达，所以艺术常常能让人们围绕一种共同的情感或信息聚在一起，即使彼此素不相识。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, a powerful play about social injustice can spark public conversation and even influence people's opinions, while a popular song about mental health can help people feel less alone in what they're going through.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，一部关于社会不公的话剧能引发公众讨论，甚至影响人们的看法，而一首关于心理健康的热门歌曲能让正在经历相似困境的人感觉不那么孤单。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: Beyond individual feelings, art can also shape a country's cultural identity, since traditional music or theater often carries history and values passed down through generations.

entries.text: Is it good to have creative people in a team?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: Yes, I think having creative people in a team is really valuable, especially when a team needs to solve problems in new ways.
ideaNotes.textZh: 是的，我觉得团队里有有创造力的人非常有价值，尤其是当团队需要用新方式解决问题的时候。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Most people naturally stick to familiar, safe solutions. But a creative person likes to question the usual approach, which pushes the team to think of other options.
ideaNotes.textZh: 大多数人天生倾向于选择熟悉、稳妥的方案。但有创造力的人喜欢质疑常规做法，这会推动团队去思考其他选项。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, in a marketing team, a creative member might suggest an unconventional campaign idea that seems risky at first, but ends up standing out far more than a typical, safe advertisement would.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，在一个营销团队里，一个有创意的成员可能会提出一个一开始看起来有风险的非常规活动创意，但最终会比一个普通、稳妥的广告更引人注目。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: That said, a team probably shouldn't be made up of only creative types, since practical, detail-focused members are just as needed to actually execute the ideas properly.
ideaNotes.textZh: 不过，团队大概也不应该全是有创造力的人，因为务实、注重细节的成员同样重要，需要他们来真正把想法落实好。

entries.text: What impact can artistic buildings have on society?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think artistic buildings can have a big impact by shaping how people feel about a city and even bringing in tourism.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得有艺术感的建筑能带来很大影响，它会改变人们对一座城市的感受，甚至能带动旅游业。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: A visually striking building becomes more than just a structure — it turns into a symbol people recognize, and that recognition can attract visitors and give locals a stronger sense of pride in their city.
ideaNotes.textZh: 一座视觉上令人惊艳的建筑不再只是一栋建筑物——它会变成人们一眼就能认出的象征，而这种认知能吸引游客，也能让当地人对自己的城市产生更强的自豪感。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, buildings like the Sydney Opera House draw millions of tourists every year simply because of their unique design, and they end up appearing on postcards and social media as a symbol of the whole city.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，悉尼歌剧院这样的建筑仅凭其独特的设计，每年就能吸引数百万游客，最终成为出现在明信片和社交媒体上、代表整座城市的象征。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: On the other hand, if a city becomes too focused on flashy architecture, it might end up neglecting more practical needs, like affordable housing or basic infrastructure.
ideaNotes.textZh: 另一方面，如果一座城市过度追求炫目的建筑，最终可能会忽视更实际的需求，比如经济适用房或基础设施建设。

entries.text: Do children these days still like doing arts and ?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think a lot of children still enjoy arts and crafts, though maybe not as much as before, since there are now so many digital distractions competing for their attention.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得很多孩子仍然喜欢手工艺术，不过可能没有以前那么普遍了，因为现在有太多电子产品的干扰在争夺他们的注意力。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Crafts need patience and focus over time, while phones and games give instant fun, so kids often go for whatever feels quicker and easier.
ideaNotes.textZh: 手工需要长时间的耐心和专注，而手机和游戏能带来即时的乐趣，所以孩子常常会选择感觉更快、更容易的那个。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, a child might enjoy painting or building something with their hands during a school activity, but at home they'll often choose to watch videos or play games instead if given the choice.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，孩子在学校活动中可能会喜欢画画或动手做东西，但在家里如果可以自己选择，他们往往会更倾向于看视频或玩游戏。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: That said, when parents or teachers actively create opportunities for hands-on activities, kids usually still respond really well and get fully absorbed in the process.
ideaNotes.textZh: 不过，当父母或老师主动创造机会让孩子参与动手活动时，孩子们通常还是会反应很好，并完全沉浸在这个过程中。

entries.text: Why do some children enjoy making things by hand?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think some children enjoy making things by hand because it gives them a strong sense of accomplishment once they finish something.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得有些孩子喜欢动手制作东西，是因为完成后能给他们带来强烈的成就感。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: When kids create something themselves, they can see the direct result of their own effort, which feels much more rewarding than passively watching or consuming something someone else made.
ideaNotes.textZh: 当孩子自己创造出一样东西时，他们能看到自己努力的直接成果，这比被动地看或使用别人做的东西要有满足感得多。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, a child who builds a small model out of blocks or clay can proudly show it off to their parents, feeling like they created something real with their own hands.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，一个用积木或黏土搭出一个小模型的孩子，会自豪地拿给父母看，感觉自己是用双手创造出了真实存在的东西。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: This kind of activity can also build problem-solving skills, since making something often involves trial and error, like figuring out why a structure keeps falling apart.
ideaNotes.textZh: 这种活动也能培养解决问题的能力，因为动手制作往往需要不断试错，比如弄清楚一个结构为什么总是散架。

entries.text: Do you think art classes are important for children?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: Yes, I think art classes are quite important for children, not necessarily to make them artists, but to help them develop creativity.
ideaNotes.textZh: 是的，我觉得艺术课对孩子来说相当重要，不一定是要把他们培养成艺术家，而是帮助他们培养创造力。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Unlike subjects with fixed answers, art allows kids to experiment freely without worrying about being wrong, which encourages them to think in more flexible and imaginative ways.
ideaNotes.textZh: 和有固定答案的科目不同，艺术让孩子可以自由尝试，不用担心答案是否正确，这能鼓励他们用更灵活、更有想象力的方式思考。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, a child asked to draw "my family" might paint everyone with different colored skin or give their dad wings, and no one tells them it's "wrong" — this freedom is exactly what encourages them to keep thinking outside the box.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，一个被要求画"我的家人"的孩子，可能会把每个人涂成不同的颜色，或者给爸爸画上翅膀，没有人会说这是"错的"——正是这种自由，鼓励他们持续保持跳出常规的思考。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: Art also gives children a healthy outlet to express emotions they might not yet have the words for, which can be especially valuable for shy or quiet kids.
ideaNotes.textZh: 艺术也能给孩子一个健康的渠道去表达情感，有些情感他们可能还没有语言能力去描述，这对内向、安静的孩子来说尤其宝贵。

entries.text: Describe a new skill you learned when you were a child

paragraphs: One skill I learned as a child was paper cutting, which I learned from my childhood friend. We were classmates in primary school and basically grew up together, so we've known each other for a really long time.
She's probably the one who's best at making things by hand among all my friends. She makes all kinds of things, like paper cuttings, little clay figures and handmade decorations.

Her work is always really delicate, with lots of little details, even though she mainly uses basic materials like colored paper, scissors, glue and clay. What impresses me most is the creativity she shows in her handicrafts.

She notices little things in everyday life and combines different elements in unexpected ways to come up with her own designs. She's not just following the same steps over and over again, but putting her own ideas and imagination into every piece.

Her creativity helped her stand out in all kinds of handicraft competitions, and she won top prizes. Inspired by her, I also became interested in handicrafts, especially paper cutting, so I asked her to teach me.

She gave me a series of structured lessons on paper cutting at her home after school, and it was honestly one of the most memorable courses I've ever taken. She started with the basics, showing me how to fold the paper properly and draw simple patterns before cutting them out.
Then, as I got better, she taught me how to create more complicated designs with different shapes and layers. She would demonstrate each step first, then let me try it on my own.
I spent a lot of time practicing, and gradually, I got the hang of it. The whole experience was not only fun but also gave me a real sense of achievement.
I'm really grateful to her for teaching me this skill and encouraging me along the way.
paragraphsZh: 我小时候学的一项技能是剪纸，是跟我的童年好友学的。 我们是小学同学，基本上是一起长大的，所以我们已经认识很长时间了。
她可能是我所有朋友中最擅长手工制作的那一个。 她会制作各种各样的东西，比如剪纸、小泥塑和手工装饰品。
她的作品总是非常精致，有很多细节，尽管她主要使用一些基础材料，比如彩纸、剪刀、胶水和黏土。 最让我印象深刻的是她在手工作品中展现出的创造力。
她会留意日常生活中的小事，并以出人意料的方式将不同的元素结合起来，从而设计出自己的作品。 她并不是只会一遍又一遍地重复相同的步骤，而是会把自己的想法和想象力融入每一件作品中。
她的创造力帮助她在各种手工比赛中脱颖而出，并且获得了最高级别的奖项。 受到她的启发，我也开始对手工制作感兴趣，尤其是剪纸，所以我请她教我。
放学后，她在家里给我上了一系列系统的剪纸课程。 说实话，这是我上过的最令人难忘的课程之一。
她从基础知识开始教起，向我展示如何正确地折纸，以及如何画出简单的图案，然后再把它们剪下来。 后来，随着我的技术越来越好，她开始教我如何运用不同的形状和层次来制作更复杂的设计。
她会先示范每一个步骤，然后让我自己尝试。 我花了很多时间练习，渐渐地，我就掌握了窍门。
整个经历不仅很有趣，还让我获得了真正的成就感。 我真的很感激她教会我这项技能，并且一路上不断地鼓励我。

entries.text: Is it important for everyone to have a specialized skill?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: Yes, I think having a specialized skill is really important, especially in today's competitive job market.
ideaNotes.textZh: 是的，我觉得拥有一项专业技能真的很重要，尤其是在如今竞争激烈的就业市场中。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Being average at many things makes it hard to stand out, but having deep expertise in one area gives someone a clear advantage that's harder for others to easily replicate.
ideaNotes.textZh: 什么都会一点、只是平庸的水平很难脱颖而出，但在某个领域拥有深厚的专长，能给一个人带来明显的优势，别人很难轻易复制。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, someone who becomes highly skilled in data analysis is more likely to get hired than someone who knows a little bit of everything, simply because companies need that specific expertise.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，一个在数据分析方面技能出众的人，比一个什么都懂一点的人更容易被公司录用，单纯是因为公司需要那种特定的专业能力。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: That said, having a specialized skill shouldn't mean ignoring basic knowledge in other areas, since some level of general understanding still helps someone adapt to different situations.
ideaNotes.textZh: 不过，拥有专业技能不代表可以忽视其他领域的基础知识，因为一定程度的通识理解仍然能帮助一个人适应不同的情况。

entries.text: Can a child learn skills from another child?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: Yes, I think children can definitely learn skills from other children, sometimes even more easily than from adults.
ideaNotes.textZh: 是的，我觉得孩子确实可以从其他孩子身上学到技能，有时甚至比从成年人身上学得更容易。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Kids often feel more comfortable and relaxed around peers their own age, so they're more willing to try, fail, and ask questions without worrying about looking silly in front of an adult.
ideaNotes.textZh: 孩子在同龄伙伴面前通常会感觉更放松自在，所以他们更愿意尝试、失败、提问，而不用担心在大人面前显得很傻。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, a child might learn how to ride a bike faster by watching and copying a friend who already knows how, picking up small tricks that a parent's instructions might not fully explain.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，一个孩子可能通过观察和模仿一个已经会骑车的朋友，更快学会骑自行车，学到一些父母的口头指导可能没能完全说清楚的小技巧。

entries.text: Do you think it is easier for children to learn new skills than for adults?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: Yes, I think it's generally easier for children to learn new skills compared to adults.
ideaNotes.textZh: 是的，我觉得总体来说，孩子学习新技能确实比成年人更容易。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: A child's brain is still highly adaptable, so new information gets absorbed almost naturally, while adults often have to unlearn old habits first, which slows down the whole process.
ideaNotes.textZh: 孩子的大脑仍然具有很强的适应能力，所以新信息几乎能自然地被吸收，而成年人往往得先改掉旧习惯，这会拖慢整个学习过程。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, a young child can pick up a new language just by being surrounded by it, while an adult usually needs structured lessons and still ends up speaking with an accent.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，一个小孩子只需要处在新语言的环境中就能自然学会，而成年人通常需要系统的课程学习，最后说出来往往还是带口音。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: That said, adults do have an advantage in understanding concepts more quickly, since they can connect new skills to knowledge they already have.
ideaNotes.textZh: 不过，成年人在理解概念方面确实更有优势，因为他们能把新技能和已有的知识联系起来。

ideaNotes.text: I think children mostly learn through imitation and play, while adults tend to learn through logical explanation and structure.

ideaNotes.text: Children absorb information naturally without needing to understand the reasoning behind it, but adults usually want to know why something works before they can fully accept and remember it.

entries.text: What are the differences between learning in a group and learning by yourself ?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think group learning relies more on interaction and discussion, while learning alone relies more on focus and self-discipline.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得小组学习更依赖互动和讨论，而独自学习更依赖专注力和自律。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: In a group, people can bounce ideas off each other and get immediate feedback, but this also means the pace depends on everyone else, whereas learning alone lets someone go entirely at their own speed.
ideaNotes.textZh: 在小组里，大家可以互相碰撞想法，得到即时反馈，但这也意味着进度取决于其他所有人，而独自学习则能让一个人完全按照自己的节奏来。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, in a group, one person might quickly grasp a concept while others are still struggling, which can create pressure to keep up, but studying alone means someone can slow down on a tricky part without feeling rushed by anyone else.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，在小组里，可能有人很快就理解了某个概念，而其他人还在挣扎，这会带来一种要跟上进度的压力，而独自学习则能让一个人在难点上放慢速度，不会被任何人催促。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: That said, some people naturally do better with one method over the other, depending on their personality — more outgoing people might thrive in groups, while introverted people often prefer studying alone.
ideaNotes.textZh: 不过，有些人天生就更适合其中一种方式，这取决于他们的性格——性格比较外向的人可能在小组里表现更好，而内向的人通常更喜欢独自学习。

entries.text: What skills should children learn before they go to school ?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think children should learn basic self-care skills, like dressing themselves or using the bathroom independently, before starting school.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得孩子在上学前应该学会基本的自理技能，比如自己穿衣服或独立上厕所。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Teachers can't give one-on-one attention to every student, so children need to be able to handle these small, everyday tasks on their own to keep up with a classroom setting.
ideaNotes.textZh: 老师没办法给每个学生一对一的关注，所以孩子需要能够独立处理这些日常小事，才能跟上课堂的节奏。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, a child who can already tie their own shoelaces or open their own lunch box won't need to interrupt the teacher constantly for help with these small tasks.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，一个已经会自己系鞋带、打开自己午餐盒的孩子，就不需要为了这些小事一直打断老师寻求帮助。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: Beyond physical tasks, basic social skills, like sharing and taking turns, are also important for adjusting smoothly to a classroom full of other kids.
ideaNotes.textZh: 除了这些身体力行的小事之外，基本的社交技能，比如分享和轮流，对顺利适应一个满是其他孩子的教室也很重要。

entries.text: Describe a friend of yours who is creative

paragraphs: The person I'd like to talk about is my childhood friend. We were classmates in primary school and basically grew up together, so we've known each other for a really long time.
She's probably the one who's best at making things by hand among all my friends. She makes all kinds of things, like paper cuttings, little clay figures and handmade decorations.

Her work is always really delicate, with lots of little details, even though she mainly uses basic materials like colored paper, scissors, glue and clay. What impresses me most is the creativity she shows in her handicrafts.

She notices little things in everyday life and combines different elements in unexpected ways to come up with her own designs. She's not just following the same steps over and over again, but putting her own ideas and imagination into every piece.

Her creativity helped her stand out in all kinds of handicraft competitions, and she won top prizes. Inspired by her, I also became interested in handicrafts, especially paper cutting, so I asked her to teach me.

She gave me a series of structured lessons on paper cutting at her home after school, and it was honestly one of the most memorable courses I've ever taken. She started with the basics, showing me how to fold the paper properly and draw simple patterns before cutting them out.
Then, as I got better, she taught me how to create more complicated designs with different shapes and layers. She would demonstrate each step first, then let me try it on my own.
I spent a lot of time practicing, and gradually, I got the hang of it. The whole experience was not only fun but also gave me a real sense of achievement.
I'm really grateful to her for teaching me this skill and encouraging me along the way.
paragraphsZh: 我们是小学同学，基本上是一起长大的，所以我们已经认识很长时间了。 她可能是我所有朋友中最擅长手工制作的那一个。
她会制作各种各样的东西，比如剪纸、小泥塑和手工装饰品。 她的作品总是非常精致，有很多细节，尽管她主要使用一些基础材料，比如彩纸、剪刀、胶水和黏土。
最让我印象深刻的是她在手工作品中展现出的创造力。 她会留意日常生活中的小事，并以出人意料的方式将不同的元素结合起来，从而设计出自己的作品。
她并不是只会一遍又一遍地重复相同的步骤，而是会把自己的想法和想象力融入每一件作品中。 她的创造力帮助她在各种手工比赛中脱颖而出，并且获得了最高级别的奖项。
受到她的启发，我也开始对手工制作感兴趣，尤其是剪纸，所以我请她教我。 放学后，她在家里给我上了一系列系统的剪纸课程。
说实话，这是我上过的最令人难忘的课程之一。 她从基础知识开始教起，向我展示如何正确地折纸，以及如何画出简单的图案，然后再把它们剪下来。
后来，随着我的技术越来越好，她开始教我如何运用不同的形状和层次来制作更复杂的设计。 她会先示范每一个步骤，然后让我自己尝试。
我花了很多时间练习，渐渐地，我就掌握了窍门。 整个经历不仅很有趣，还让我获得了真正的成就感。
我真的很感激她教会我这项技能，并且一路上不断地鼓励我。

entries.text: Describe a happy person you know

paragraphs: The person I'd like to talk about is my grandmother. She lives in the countryside and has her own land — these days, she basically spends her whole day growing things in the garden. I think that's a big part of why she's such a happy person.

She's the kind of person who's always smiling, never really gets stressed about anything, and just has this really calm, easy-going energy about her — nothing seems to bother her much. She shows her happiness in pretty simple ways, actually. Like, she hums little songs while she's watering her plants, and whenever she picks a really good harvest, she gets genuinely excited, almost like a kid, and can't wait to show it to the neighbours.

Every time I go back home to see her, my mood always gets better too — it's like her happiness is kind of contagious. I think the reason she's such a happy person is that she's found something she truly loves doing, and gets to do it every day. She's not chasing anything big or complicated, just enjoying the small, everyday moments, like watching her plants grow or sharing a meal with neighbours.

I think that's honestly what real happiness looks like — you don't need much to feel content. She is also one of the most organized people I know, especially when it comes to gardening. She always keeps a little notebook — before every year starts, she makes a long-term plan for the whole year, deciding what to grow in each season to make the best use of her land, and on top of that, she has a detailed daily plan covering things like when to water certain plants or when to add fertilizer.

Even though she's so organized, she's not rigid about it at all — she often changes things depending on the condition of her plants. I remember visiting her once, right when it started raining heavily, and she'd already covered up all her plants and moved the pots inside — I was really impressed. And she's able to do this because being organized really matters to her — with gardening, timing is everything, and if you miss the right moment, the whole plant could get damaged, and she'd lose a whole season's work.

That's why checking the weather forecast is pretty much the first thing she does every morning. 有健康习惯和作息的人 She is honestly one of the healthiest people I know. She's up every morning at five or six — feeding the animals, making breakfast, and most importantly, heading out to her garden to check on her plants, digging, watering, and pulling weeds — which naturally keeps her physically active without it feeling like a boring workout at the gym. When it comes to food, she basically eats what she grows — fresh vegetables straight from her own garden, all natural, nothing processed.

And unlike a lot of older people in the countryside focus only on vegetables and overlook protein, she makes sure to cook a proper balanced meal every day — different dishes, making sure she's getting all the nutrients she needs. And one more thing — she barely uses her phone or scrolls through social media. So whatever's going on online, it just doesn't reach her — and I think that's a big part of why she stays so calm and mentally healthy. 喜欢在家/花园种植物的人 She grows a really wide variety of things — flowers like roses and sunflowers, and vegetables like tomatoes, cucumbers and all kinds of leafy greens.

She looks after her plants every single day, watering them, checking on their condition, and adjusting things depending on the weather. She treats every plant really carefully, almost like they're her own children, and she always talks about them with so much love and pride. And the way she gardens is actually really eco-friendly too — she never uses any chemical fertilisers.

Instead, she makes her own compost from kitchen scraps like vegetable peels and leftover food, and mixes it back into the soil to keep it healthy and full of nutrients. She also collects rainwater in big buckets outside to use on her plants instead of tap water. Everything is done very naturally and carefully.

I think she loves it so much because for her, it's more than just a hobby — since she retired and the kids moved away, gardening gives her a real sense of purpose and keeps her from feeling too lonely. And there's something really satisfying about watching things grow from a tiny seed — you put in the effort, and you see the results. Not everything in life works that way.
paragraphsZh: 万能背景 我想说的这个人是我的奶奶。 她住在农村，有自己的土地——这些天，她基本上整天都在花园里种东西。 快乐人士 我觉得这在很大程度上是她之所以是一个如此快乐的人的原因。
她是那种总是微笑的人，从来不会为任何事情感到有压力，有一种非常平静、随和的气质——什么都不太能让她烦恼。 她以非常简单的方式表达她的快乐。 比如，她一边给植物浇水一边哼着小曲，每次收获特别好的时候，她会真的很兴奋，像个小孩一样，迫不及待地想拿去给邻居们看。
每次我回家看她，我的心情也会跟着变好——她的快乐好像真的很有感染力。 我觉得她之所以是这样一个快乐的人，是因为她找到了自己真正热爱做的事，而且每天都能做这件事。 她不在追逐什么大的或复杂的东西，只是享受这些平凡的小日常时刻，比如看着植物生长，或者和邻居们一起吃顿饭。
我觉得这就是真正的快乐——不需要太多就能感到满足。 有条理的人 她也是我认识的最有条理的人之一，尤其是在种植方面。 她总是随身带着一个小本子——每年开始之前，她都会为全年制定一个长期计划，决定每个季节种什么，以充分利用她的土地。
除此之外，她还有一个详细的日常计划，涵盖比如什么时候给某些植物浇水或者什么时候施肥。 即使她这么有条理，她也完全不死板——她经常根据植物的状态来调整安排。 我记得有一次去她家，刚好赶上开始下大雨，她已经把所有植物都盖好、把花盆都搬进屋里了——我真的很佩服。
她之所以能做到这些，是因为有条理这件事对她真的很重要——种植这件事，时机就是一切，如果错过了最佳时机，整株植物可能就毁了，她可能会损失一整季的劳动成果。 这就是为什么查看天气预报几乎是她每天早上做的第一件事。 有健康习惯和作息的人 她是我认识的最健康的人之一。
她每天早上五六点就起床——给动物喂食、做早饭，最重要的是，出去花园里查看她的植物，挖土、浇水、除草——这自然而然地让她保持身体活跃，而不像在健身房做枯燥的锻炼。 说到饮食，她基本上吃自己种的东西——从自己花园里摘的新鲜蔬菜，全是天然的，没有任何加工食品。 而且，不像农村里很多只注重蔬菜而忽视蛋白质的老人，她确保每天都做一顿适当均衡的饭菜——各种菜肴，确保自己摄入所需的所有营养。
还有一点——她几乎不用手机，也不刷社交媒体。 所以网上发生的一切，就是传不到她那里——我认为这在很大程度上是她保持如此平静和心理健康的原因。 喜欢在家/花园种植物的人 她种了各种各样的东西——玫瑰、向日葵等花卉，以及番茄、黄瓜和各种绿叶蔬菜。
她每天都照料她的植物，浇水、检查状态，并根据天气调整安排。 她对每株植物都非常用心，几乎把它们当作自己的孩子，总是带着满满的爱和自豪感谈论它们。 她的种植方式其实也非常环保——她从不使用任何化学肥料。
她用厨余垃圾（比如蔬菜皮和剩余食物）自制堆肥，混入土壤使其保持健康和营养丰富。 她还在外面放了几个大桶收集雨水，用来浇灌植物而不是用自来水。 一切都做得非常自然、仔细。
我觉得她如此热爱种植，是因为对她来说，这不只是一个爱好——自从她退休后孩子们也都离开了，种植给了她真正的目标感，让她不会感到太孤单。 而且看着东西从一粒小小的种子真正生长起来，有一种真正的满足感——你付出了努力，你就能看到结果。 生活中不是所有事情都是这样的。

entries.text: When do you think people are happiest?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think people are happiest when they're spending time with loved ones, like family or close friends.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得人们和亲近的人在一起时最快乐，比如家人或好朋友。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: This is because humans are naturally social creatures, and having strong emotional connections gives us a sense of belonging and support.
ideaNotes.textZh: 这是因为人类天生是社会性动物，拥有牢固的情感联系能带给我们一种归属感和支持。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For example, many people say their happiest memories are simple moments, like having a meal together or chatting with close friends, rather than big achievements.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，很多人说他们最快乐的回忆都是简单的时刻，比如一起吃饭或和好朋友聊天，而不是什么重大成就。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: So I'd say true happiness often comes from relationships rather than money or career success.
ideaNotes.textZh: 所以我认为真正的快乐往往来自人际关系，而不是金钱或事业上的成功。

entries.text: How can the arts spread positive emotions in society?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think the arts, like music, painting, or films, can spread positive emotions by helping people express and share feelings.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得艺术，比如音乐、绘画或电影，能通过帮助人们表达和分享情感来传播积极情绪。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: This works because art often creates an emotional resonance, allowing people to feel understood or inspired, even without direct communication.
ideaNotes.textZh: 这是因为艺术往往能引起情感共鸣，让人们感到被理解或受到启发，即使没有直接的交流。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, an uplifting song or a touching movie can instantly improve someone's mood, and public art performances often bring people together in a joyful atmosphere.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，一首振奋人心的歌曲或一部感人的电影能立刻改善一个人的心情，公开的艺术表演也常常能让大家聚在一起，营造出欢乐的氛围。

ideaNotes.text: So art isn't just entertainment — it plays a real role in boosting mental wellbeing across society.
ideaNotes.textZh: 所以艺术不只是娱乐——它在提升整个社会的心理健康方面确实起着作用。

entries.text: Do you think teachers are able to spot the unhappy children?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think most teachers are able to spot unhappy children, but it's not always guaranteed, especially in large classes.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得大部分老师能够发现不开心的孩子，但这并不总是能做到，尤其是在大班教学中。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: This is because experienced teachers usually pay attention to behavioral changes, like a student suddenly becoming quiet or losing interest, which can be signs of emotional struggles.
ideaNotes.textZh: 这是因为有经验的老师通常会关注行为变化，比如一个学生突然变得沉默或失去兴趣，这些都可能是情绪困扰的迹象。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For example, a caring teacher might notice a normally active student sitting alone during break time and check in with them, while an overworked teacher in a crowded classroom might not have time to notice.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，一位关心学生的老师可能会注意到一个平时活泼的学生在课间独自坐着，从而主动关心他们，而在人数众多的班级里，负担过重的老师可能没时间注意到。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: So it really depends on class size and how much attention each teacher is able to give to individual students.
ideaNotes.textZh: 所以这其实取决于班级规模，以及每位老师能给学生多少关注。

entries.text: Should teachers know what children are doing all the time?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I don't think teachers need to know what children are doing all the time, but they should keep a general sense of awareness.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我不认为老师需要一直知道孩子们在做什么，但他们应该保持一种大致的关注意识。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Constantly monitoring students could feel like too much surveillance and might make children uncomfortable, taking away their sense of independence.
ideaNotes.textZh: 一直监控学生可能会让人感觉像是过度监视，也可能让孩子感到不舒服，剥夺他们的独立性。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For example, giving students some freedom during break time helps them relax and develop social skills on their own, without a teacher watching every move.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，在课间给学生一些自由，能帮助他们放松并自主发展社交技能，而不需要老师盯着他们的一举一动。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: That said, teachers should still step in when there are signs of bullying or serious problems.
ideaNotes.textZh: 不过，当出现欺凌或严重问题的迹象时，老师仍然应该介入。

entries.text: What would make a student happy at school?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think having good friendships and feeling recognized by teachers are the main things that make students happy at school.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得拥有良好的友谊以及得到老师的认可，是让学生在学校感到快乐的主要因素。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: This is because school takes up so much of a student's day, so having supportive peers and positive feedback really affects their overall mood and motivation.
ideaNotes.textZh: 这是因为学校占据了学生一天中大量的时间，所以拥有支持自己的同伴和积极的反馈，会真正影响他们整体的情绪和学习动力。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, a student who has close friends to eat lunch and chat with usually feels more comfortable, while getting praised for even a small improvement can boost their confidence a lot.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，一个有好朋友一起吃午饭聊天的学生通常会感觉更自在，而哪怕只是一点小小的进步得到表扬，也能大大提升他们的自信心。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: So it's really the combination of social connection and encouragement that shapes a happy school experience.
ideaNotes.textZh: 所以真正塑造快乐校园体验的是社交联系和鼓励的结合。

entries.text: Do you think doing a job that you like is more important than other things?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I do think doing a job you like is really important, but I wouldn't say it's more important than everything else, like salary or work-life balance.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我确实认为做一份自己喜欢的工作很重要，但我不会说它比其他一切都更重要，比如薪水或工作生活平衡。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: This is because enjoying your job can boost your motivation and reduce stress, but if the pay is too low or the hours are too long, even a job you love can become exhausting.
ideaNotes.textZh: 这是因为喜欢自己的工作能提升积极性并减少压力，但如果薪水太低或工时太长，即使是喜欢的工作也会让人身心俱疲。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For example, someone might love working as a graphic designer, but if the job doesn't offer stable income, they may still feel stressed and unsatisfied overall.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，有人可能很喜欢做平面设计师，但如果这份工作没有稳定的收入，他们整体上可能仍然感到压力和不满足。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: So I'd say passion for a job matters a lot, but it needs to be balanced with practical factors like financial stability.
ideaNotes.textZh: 所以我认为对工作的热情很重要，但也需要与经济稳定等现实因素相平衡。

paragraphs: I do think doing a job you like is really important, but I wouldn't say it's more important than everything else, like salary or work-life balance.
This is because enjoying your job can boost your motivation and reduce stress, but if the pay is too low or the hours are too long, even a job you love can become exhausting.
For example, someone might love working as a graphic designer, but if the job doesn't offer stable income, they may still feel stressed and unsatisfied overall.
So I'd say passion for a job matters a lot, but it needs to be balanced with practical factors like financial stability.

例如，有人可能很喜欢做平面设计师，但如果这份工作没有稳定的收入，他们整体上可能仍然感到压力和不满足。
所以我认为对工作的热情很重要，但也需要与经济稳定等现实因素相平衡。

entries.text: Describe a person you know who is very organized

paragraphs: The person I'd like to talk about is my grandmother. She lives in the countryside and has her own land — these days, she basically spends her whole day growing things in the garden. I think that's a big part of why she's such a happy person.

She's the kind of person who's always smiling, never really gets stressed about anything, and just has this really calm, easy-going energy about her — nothing seems to bother her much. She shows her happiness in pretty simple ways, actually. Like, she hums little songs while she's watering her plants, and whenever she picks a really good harvest, she gets genuinely excited, almost like a kid, and can't wait to show it to the neighbours.

Every time I go back home to see her, my mood always gets better too — it's like her happiness is kind of contagious. I think the reason she's such a happy person is that she's found something she truly loves doing, and gets to do it every day. She's not chasing anything big or complicated, just enjoying the small, everyday moments, like watching her plants grow or sharing a meal with neighbours.

I think that's honestly what real happiness looks like — you don't need much to feel content. She is also one of the most organized people I know, especially when it comes to gardening. She always keeps a little notebook — before every year starts, she makes a long-term plan for the whole year, deciding what to grow in each season to make the best use of her land, and on top of that, she has a detailed daily plan covering things like when to water certain plants or when to add fertilizer.

Even though she's so organized, she's not rigid about it at all — she often changes things depending on the condition of her plants. I remember visiting her once, right when it started raining heavily, and she'd already covered up all her plants and moved the pots inside — I was really impressed. And she's able to do this because being organized really matters to her — with gardening, timing is everything, and if you miss the right moment, the whole plant could get damaged, and she'd lose a whole season's work.

That's why checking the weather forecast is pretty much the first thing she does every morning. 有健康习惯和作息的人 She is honestly one of the healthiest people I know. She's up every morning at five or six — feeding the animals, making breakfast, and most importantly, heading out to her garden to check on her plants, digging, watering, and pulling weeds — which naturally keeps her physically active without it feeling like a boring workout at the gym. When it comes to food, she basically eats what she grows — fresh vegetables straight from her own garden, all natural, nothing processed.

And unlike a lot of older people in the countryside focus only on vegetables and overlook protein, she makes sure to cook a proper balanced meal every day — different dishes, making sure she's getting all the nutrients she needs. And one more thing — she barely uses her phone or scrolls through social media. So whatever's going on online, it just doesn't reach her — and I think that's a big part of why she stays so calm and mentally healthy. 喜欢在家/花园种植物的人 She grows a really wide variety of things — flowers like roses and sunflowers, and vegetables like tomatoes, cucumbers and all kinds of leafy greens.

She looks after her plants every single day, watering them, checking on their condition, and adjusting things depending on the weather. She treats every plant really carefully, almost like they're her own children, and she always talks about them with so much love and pride. And the way she gardens is actually really eco-friendly too — she never uses any chemical fertilisers.

Instead, she makes her own compost from kitchen scraps like vegetable peels and leftover food, and mixes it back into the soil to keep it healthy and full of nutrients. She also collects rainwater in big buckets outside to use on her plants instead of tap water. Everything is done very naturally and carefully.

I think she loves it so much because for her, it's more than just a hobby — since she retired and the kids moved away, gardening gives her a real sense of purpose and keeps her from feeling too lonely. And there's something really satisfying about watching things grow from a tiny seed — you put in the effort, and you see the results. Not everything in life works that way.
paragraphsZh: 万能背景 我想说的这个人是我的奶奶。 她住在农村，有自己的土地——这些天，她基本上整天都在花园里种东西。 快乐人士 我觉得这在很大程度上是她之所以是一个如此快乐的人的原因。
她是那种总是微笑的人，从来不会为任何事情感到有压力，有一种非常平静、随和的气质——什么都不太能让她烦恼。 她以非常简单的方式表达她的快乐。 比如，她一边给植物浇水一边哼着小曲，每次收获特别好的时候，她会真的很兴奋，像个小孩一样，迫不及待地想拿去给邻居们看。
每次我回家看她，我的心情也会跟着变好——她的快乐好像真的很有感染力。 我觉得她之所以是这样一个快乐的人，是因为她找到了自己真正热爱做的事，而且每天都能做这件事。 她不在追逐什么大的或复杂的东西，只是享受这些平凡的小日常时刻，比如看着植物生长，或者和邻居们一起吃顿饭。
我觉得这就是真正的快乐——不需要太多就能感到满足。 有条理的人 她也是我认识的最有条理的人之一，尤其是在种植方面。 她总是随身带着一个小本子——每年开始之前，她都会为全年制定一个长期计划，决定每个季节种什么，以充分利用她的土地。
除此之外，她还有一个详细的日常计划，涵盖比如什么时候给某些植物浇水或者什么时候施肥。 即使她这么有条理，她也完全不死板——她经常根据植物的状态来调整安排。 我记得有一次去她家，刚好赶上开始下大雨，她已经把所有植物都盖好、把花盆都搬进屋里了——我真的很佩服。
她之所以能做到这些，是因为有条理这件事对她真的很重要——种植这件事，时机就是一切，如果错过了最佳时机，整株植物可能就毁了，她可能会损失一整季的劳动成果。 这就是为什么查看天气预报几乎是她每天早上做的第一件事。 有健康习惯和作息的人 她是我认识的最健康的人之一。
她每天早上五六点就起床——给动物喂食、做早饭，最重要的是，出去花园里查看她的植物，挖土、浇水、除草——这自然而然地让她保持身体活跃，而不像在健身房做枯燥的锻炼。 说到饮食，她基本上吃自己种的东西——从自己花园里摘的新鲜蔬菜，全是天然的，没有任何加工食品。 而且，不像农村里很多只注重蔬菜而忽视蛋白质的老人，她确保每天都做一顿适当均衡的饭菜——各种菜肴，确保自己摄入所需的所有营养。
还有一点——她几乎不用手机，也不刷社交媒体。 所以网上发生的一切，就是传不到她那里——我认为这在很大程度上是她保持如此平静和心理健康的原因。 喜欢在家/花园种植物的人 她种了各种各样的东西——玫瑰、向日葵等花卉，以及番茄、黄瓜和各种绿叶蔬菜。
她每天都照料她的植物，浇水、检查状态，并根据天气调整安排。 她对每株植物都非常用心，几乎把它们当作自己的孩子，总是带着满满的爱和自豪感谈论它们。 她的种植方式其实也非常环保——她从不使用任何化学肥料。
她用厨余垃圾（比如蔬菜皮和剩余食物）自制堆肥，混入土壤使其保持健康和营养丰富。 她还在外面放了几个大桶收集雨水，用来浇灌植物而不是用自来水。 一切都做得非常自然、仔细。
我觉得她如此热爱种植，是因为对她来说，这不只是一个爱好——自从她退休后孩子们也都离开了，种植给了她真正的目标感，让她不会感到太孤单。 而且看着东西从一粒小小的种子真正生长起来，有一种真正的满足感——你付出了努力，你就能看到结果。 生活中不是所有事情都是这样的。

entries.text: Do you think it is important for managers to be well organized?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: Yes, I definitely think it's important for managers to be well organized, especially since their decisions directly affect the whole team's workflow.
ideaNotes.textZh: 是的，我确实认为经理有条理非常重要，尤其是因为他们的决策会直接影响整个团队的工作流程。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Unlike an employee whose mistakes stay contained to their own work, a manager's disorganization gets passed down to the whole team, and small delays can quickly snowball.
ideaNotes.textZh: 和普通员工不同，员工的失误通常只局限在自己的工作范围内，而经理没条理会传递给整个团队，小的延误也会很快越滚越大。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, if a manager forgets to update the team on a changed deadline, some members might keep working on the old plan, wasting time and effort that could've been avoided.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如说，如果一个经理忘记告诉团队截止日期变了，有些成员可能还在按旧计划继续工作，白白浪费了本可以避免的时间和精力。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: On the flip side, being too rigidly organized might also make a manager less flexible when unexpected problems come up.
ideaNotes.textZh: 反过来说，过度追求条理也可能让经理在遇到突发问题时缺乏灵活性。

On the flip side, being too rigidly organized might also make a manager less flexible when unexpected problems come up.

entries.text: Should parents teach their children to be organized?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: Yes, I think parents should teach their children to be organized, as it's a skill that benefits them throughout life.
ideaNotes.textZh: 是的，我认为父母应该教孩子有条理，因为这是一项能让他们受益终身的技能。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Being organized isn't useful for just one task — it carries over into every stage of life, from school to work to family, so once a child builds this habit, it just keeps helping them.
ideaNotes.textZh: 有条理不只是对一件事有用——它能贯穿人生每个阶段，从学业到工作再到家庭，所以孩子一旦养成这个习惯，就会一直受益。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, a child who organizes their schoolwork well might later use the same habit to manage work deadlines, or even to run a household smoothly as an adult.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，一个把学业整理得井井有条的孩子，长大后可能会用同样的习惯来管理工作截止日期，甚至用来打理家庭。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: That said, parents should guide gently rather than force it, or the child might see being organized as a chore instead of a useful habit they actually want to keep.
ideaNotes.textZh: 不过，父母应该温和引导而不是强迫，否则孩子可能会把有条理当成一种负担，而不是他们真正愿意保持的有用习惯。

keyPhrases.phrase: Carries over into every stage of life
Useful habit they actually want to keep

paragraphs: Yes, I think parents should teach their children to be organized, as it's a skill that benefits them throughout life.

For instance, a child who organizes their schoolwork well might later use the same habit to manage work deadlines, or even to run a household smoothly as an adult.
That said, parents should guide gently rather than force it, or the child might see being organized as a chore instead of a useful habit they actually want to keep.

entries.text: What can people do to become more organized?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think one of the best ways to become more organized is to write things down, like making a to-do list.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得变得更有条理的最好方法之一就是把事情写下来，比如列一份待办清单。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Our brains can only hold so much information at once, so when everything is just floating in our heads, it's easy to forget things or lose track of priorities. Writing it down takes that pressure off our memory.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我们的大脑一次能记住的东西是有限的，所以当所有事情都只存在脑子里时，很容易忘事或搞不清楚优先级。把事情写下来能减轻大脑记忆的负担。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, someone who writes down their tasks for the day can just glance at the list whenever they feel unsure what to do next, instead of trying to recall everything from memory and possibly missing something.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，一个把当天任务写下来的人，只要看一眼清单就知道接下来该做什么，而不用全靠脑子回忆，还可能漏掉一些事情。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: Besides writing lists, breaking bigger tasks into smaller steps also helps, since it makes things feel more manageable instead of overwhelming.
ideaNotes.textZh: 除了列清单，把大任务拆成更小的步骤也很有帮助，因为这样事情会显得更容易应付，而不是让人感到不知所措。

Besides writing lists, breaking bigger tasks into smaller steps also helps, since it makes things feel more manageable instead of overwhelming.

entries.text: Are organized people more likely to be successful at work or in their studies?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: Yes, I'd say organized people are generally more likely to succeed, both at work and in their studies.
ideaNotes.textZh: 是的，我认为有条理的人通常更容易成功，无论是在工作还是学习上。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Success usually depends on making good use of limited time and energy, and organized people are better at directing their effort toward what actually matters, instead of wasting it on confusion or repeated mistakes.
ideaNotes.textZh: 成功通常取决于如何善用有限的时间和精力，而有条理的人更擅长把精力用在真正重要的事情上，而不是浪费在混乱或重复犯错上。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, a student who organizes their notes and study time can spend exam week actually reviewing and practicing, while a disorganized student might spend that same time just trying to figure out what to study.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，一个把笔记和学习时间安排得井井有条的学生，考试周能真正用来复习和练习，而一个没条理的学生可能同样的时间都花在搞清楚自己该学什么上。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: That said, being organized alone doesn't guarantee success — qualities like hard work or creativity still play a big role too.
ideaNotes.textZh: 不过，光有条理并不能保证成功——努力或创造力等其他因素同样很重要。

paragraphs: Yes, I'd say organized people are generally more likely to succeed, both at work and in their studies.

Success usually depends on making good use of limited time and energy, and organized people are better at directing their effort toward what actually matters, instead of wasting it on confusion or repeated mistakes.

For instance, a student who organizes their notes and study time can spend exam week actually reviewing and practicing, while a disorganized student might spend that same time just trying to figure out what to study.

entries.text: Do you think children should learn to be organized from a young age?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: Yes, I believe children should start learning to be organized from a young age, rather than waiting until they're older.
ideaNotes.textZh: 是的，我认为孩子应该从小就开始学习有条理，而不是等到长大了才学。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Habits formed in childhood tend to stick more naturally, since kids haven't yet developed fixed routines the way adults have, so it's much easier to build good habits early than to change existing ones later.
ideaNotes.textZh: 童年时期养成的习惯往往更自然地保持下去，因为孩子还没有像成年人那样形成固定的行为模式，所以从小培养好习惯要比长大后再改变已有习惯容易得多。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, a child who gets used to putting things back in place after using them will likely carry that same habit into adulthood, automatically tidying their desk or workspace without having to force themselves to do it.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，一个习惯用完东西就物归原位的孩子，长大后很可能会把这个习惯延续下去，自然而然地整理自己的桌面或工作空间，而不需要强迫自己去做。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: However, it's worth pointing out that some people develop strong organizational skills later in life too, often when they're pushed by real responsibilities like a demanding job.
ideaNotes.textZh: 不过，也有些人是在长大后才培养出很强的条理性，往往是被繁重的工作等现实责任逼出来的。

entries.text: Why is it important for people to be organized?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think being organized is important mainly because it helps people use their time and energy more wisely.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得有条理很重要，主要是因为它能帮助人们更明智地利用时间和精力。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Without organization, people often end up spending energy on the wrong things, like searching for lost items or redoing tasks, instead of putting that same energy toward what they actually need to accomplish.
ideaNotes.textZh: 如果没有条理，人们常常会把精力花在不该花的地方，比如找丢失的东西或重复做同一件事，而不是把这些精力用在他们真正需要完成的事情上。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, someone who keeps their documents neatly filed can find what they need in seconds, while a disorganized person might spend the whole morning digging through piles of paper just to locate one file.
