entries.text: Describe a person you know who has healthy habits and a healthy daily routine

paragraphs: The person I'd like to talk about is my grandmother. She lives in the countryside and has her own land — these days, she basically spends her whole day growing things in the garden. I think that's a big part of why she's such a happy person.

She's the kind of person who's always smiling, never really gets stressed about anything, and just has this really calm, easy-going energy about her — nothing seems to bother her much. She shows her happiness in pretty simple ways, actually. Like, she hums little songs while she's watering her plants, and whenever she picks a really good harvest, she gets genuinely excited, almost like a kid, and can't wait to show it to the neighbours.

Every time I go back home to see her, my mood always gets better too — it's like her happiness is kind of contagious. I think the reason she's such a happy person is that she's found something she truly loves doing, and gets to do it every day. She's not chasing anything big or complicated, just enjoying the small, everyday moments, like watching her plants grow or sharing a meal with neighbours.

I think that's honestly what real happiness looks like — you don't need much to feel content. She is also one of the most organized people I know, especially when it comes to gardening. She always keeps a little notebook — before every year starts, she makes a long-term plan for the whole year, deciding what to grow in each season to make the best use of her land, and on top of that, she has a detailed daily plan covering things like when to water certain plants or when to add fertilizer.

Even though she's so organized, she's not rigid about it at all — she often changes things depending on the condition of her plants. I remember visiting her once, right when it started raining heavily, and she'd already covered up all her plants and moved the pots inside — I was really impressed. And she's able to do this because being organized really matters to her — with gardening, timing is everything, and if you miss the right moment, the whole plant could get damaged, and she'd lose a whole season's work.

That's why checking the weather forecast is pretty much the first thing she does every morning. 有健康习惯和作息的人 She is honestly one of the healthiest people I know. She's up every morning at five or six — feeding the animals, making breakfast, and most importantly, heading out to her garden to check on her plants, digging, watering, and pulling weeds — which naturally keeps her physically active without it feeling like a boring workout at the gym. When it comes to food, she basically eats what she grows — fresh vegetables straight from her own garden, all natural, nothing processed.

And unlike a lot of older people in the countryside focus only on vegetables and overlook protein, she makes sure to cook a proper balanced meal every day — different dishes, making sure she's getting all the nutrients she needs. And one more thing — she barely uses her phone or scrolls through social media. So whatever's going on online, it just doesn't reach her — and I think that's a big part of why she stays so calm and mentally healthy. 喜欢在家/花园种植物的人 She grows a really wide variety of things — flowers like roses and sunflowers, and vegetables like tomatoes, cucumbers and all kinds of leafy greens.

She looks after her plants every single day, watering them, checking on their condition, and adjusting things depending on the weather. She treats every plant really carefully, almost like they're her own children, and she always talks about them with so much love and pride. And the way she gardens is actually really eco-friendly too — she never uses any chemical fertilisers.

Instead, she makes her own compost from kitchen scraps like vegetable peels and leftover food, and mixes it back into the soil to keep it healthy and full of nutrients. She also collects rainwater in big buckets outside to use on her plants instead of tap water. Everything is done very naturally and carefully.

I think she loves it so much because for her, it's more than just a hobby — since she retired and the kids moved away, gardening gives her a real sense of purpose and keeps her from feeling too lonely. And there's something really satisfying about watching things grow from a tiny seed — you put in the effort, and you see the results. Not everything in life works that way.
paragraphsZh: 万能背景 我想说的这个人是我的奶奶。 她住在农村，有自己的土地——这些天，她基本上整天都在花园里种东西。 快乐人士 我觉得这在很大程度上是她之所以是一个如此快乐的人的原因。
她是那种总是微笑的人，从来不会为任何事情感到有压力，有一种非常平静、随和的气质——什么都不太能让她烦恼。 她以非常简单的方式表达她的快乐。 比如，她一边给植物浇水一边哼着小曲，每次收获特别好的时候，她会真的很兴奋，像个小孩一样，迫不及待地想拿去给邻居们看。
每次我回家看她，我的心情也会跟着变好——她的快乐好像真的很有感染力。 我觉得她之所以是这样一个快乐的人，是因为她找到了自己真正热爱做的事，而且每天都能做这件事。 她不在追逐什么大的或复杂的东西，只是享受这些平凡的小日常时刻，比如看着植物生长，或者和邻居们一起吃顿饭。
我觉得这就是真正的快乐——不需要太多就能感到满足。 有条理的人 她也是我认识的最有条理的人之一，尤其是在种植方面。 她总是随身带着一个小本子——每年开始之前，她都会为全年制定一个长期计划，决定每个季节种什么，以充分利用她的土地。
除此之外，她还有一个详细的日常计划，涵盖比如什么时候给某些植物浇水或者什么时候施肥。 即使她这么有条理，她也完全不死板——她经常根据植物的状态来调整安排。 我记得有一次去她家，刚好赶上开始下大雨，她已经把所有植物都盖好、把花盆都搬进屋里了——我真的很佩服。
她之所以能做到这些，是因为有条理这件事对她真的很重要——种植这件事，时机就是一切，如果错过了最佳时机，整株植物可能就毁了，她可能会损失一整季的劳动成果。 这就是为什么查看天气预报几乎是她每天早上做的第一件事。 有健康习惯和作息的人 她是我认识的最健康的人之一。
她每天早上五六点就起床——给动物喂食、做早饭，最重要的是，出去花园里查看她的植物，挖土、浇水、除草——这自然而然地让她保持身体活跃，而不像在健身房做枯燥的锻炼。 说到饮食，她基本上吃自己种的东西——从自己花园里摘的新鲜蔬菜，全是天然的，没有任何加工食品。 而且，不像农村里很多只注重蔬菜而忽视蛋白质的老人，她确保每天都做一顿适当均衡的饭菜——各种菜肴，确保自己摄入所需的所有营养。
还有一点——她几乎不用手机，也不刷社交媒体。 所以网上发生的一切，就是传不到她那里——我认为这在很大程度上是她保持如此平静和心理健康的原因。 喜欢在家/花园种植物的人 她种了各种各样的东西——玫瑰、向日葵等花卉，以及番茄、黄瓜和各种绿叶蔬菜。
她每天都照料她的植物，浇水、检查状态，并根据天气调整安排。 她对每株植物都非常用心，几乎把它们当作自己的孩子，总是带着满满的爱和自豪感谈论它们。 她的种植方式其实也非常环保——她从不使用任何化学肥料。
她用厨余垃圾（比如蔬菜皮和剩余食物）自制堆肥，混入土壤使其保持健康和营养丰富。 她还在外面放了几个大桶收集雨水，用来浇灌植物而不是用自来水。 一切都做得非常自然、仔细。
我觉得她如此热爱种植，是因为对她来说，这不只是一个爱好——自从她退休后孩子们也都离开了，种植给了她真正的目标感，让她不会感到太孤单。 而且看着东西从一粒小小的种子真正生长起来，有一种真正的满足感——你付出了努力，你就能看到结果。 生活中不是所有事情都是这样的。

还有一点——她几乎不用手机，也不刷社交媒体。 所以网上发生的一切，就是传不到她那里——我认为这在很大程度上是她保持如此平静和心理健康的原因。 喜欢在家/花园种植物的人 她种了各种各样的东西——玫瑰、向日葵等花卉，以及番茄、黄瓜和各种绿叶蔬菜。
她每天都照料她的植物，浇水、检查状态，并根据天气调整安排。 她对每株植物都非常用心，几乎把它们当作自己的孩子，总是带着满满的爱和自豪感谈论它们。 她的种植方式其实也非常环保——她从不使用任何化学肥料。
她用厨余垃圾（比如蔬菜皮和剩余食物）自制堆肥，混入土壤使其保持健康和营养丰富。 她还在外面放了几个大桶收集雨水，用来浇灌植物而不是用自来水。 一切都做得非常自然、仔细。
我觉得她如此热爱种植，是因为对她来说，这不只是一个爱好——自从她退休后孩子们也都离开了，种植给了她真正的目标感，让她不会感到太孤单。 而且看着东西从一粒小小的种子真正生长起来，有一种真正的满足感——你付出了努力，你就能看到结果。 生活中不是所有事情都是这样的。

entries.text: What are the advantages of growing vegetables or flowers at home?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think one of the biggest advantages is that it's really good for both your physical and mental health — it gives you something calming and rewarding to do at home.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我认为最大的好处之一是它对你的身心健康都非常有益，它给你一件在家平静而有成就感的事情做。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Well, growing your own vegetables means you know exactly what goes into your food — no chemicals or pesticides — so it's much fresher and healthier than what you buy at the supermarket. And for flowers, just having something green and alive around the house makes the whole place feel more warm and pleasant.
ideaNotes.textZh: 嗯，自己种蔬菜意味着你确切地知道食物里有什么，没有化学品或农药，所以比你在超市买的更新鲜更健康。而种花，只是在家里有一些绿色和有生命的东西，就能让整个地方感觉更加温馨和舒适。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, my mum started growing tomatoes and herbs on our balcony a few years ago, and she always says that eating something you grew yourself just tastes so much better — and honestly it really does.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，我妈妈几年前开始在我们阳台上种西红柿和香草，她总是说吃自己种的东西味道就是好那么多，说实话确实是这样。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸
ideaNotes.textZh: 可选】 And also, gardening is actually a really great way to slow down and switch off from the stress of daily life — when you're focused on watering plants and watching them grow, you're not thinking about work or your phone, which is a nice break. 而且，园艺实际上是一个非常好的方式来放慢脚步、从日常压力中抽离，当你专注于浇水和看植物生长时，你不会想着工作或手机，这是一个很好的休息。

entries.text: Do many people grow vegetables or flowers at home in your country?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think it's becoming more and more popular, but it's still not something the majority of people do, especially those living in big cities.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我认为这越来越流行了，但仍然不是大多数人都会做的事情，尤其是住在大城市的人。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Basically, most people in China live in apartments without much outdoor space, so growing vegetables or flowers is just not that easy or practical for them. But for people who have a balcony or a garden, it's actually quite a common hobby, especially among older generations who grew up doing it.
ideaNotes.textZh: 基本上，中国大多数人住在公寓里，没有太多户外空间，所以种蔬菜或花卉对他们来说不那么容易或实际。但对于有阳台或花园的人来说，这实际上是相当普遍的爱好，尤其是在从小就这样做的老一辈中。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, almost every older person I know has some kind of plant or vegetable patch on their balcony — my grandparents grow spring onions, chillies, and tomatoes and they pretty much use them every day when cooking. But my friends my age? Most of them wouldn't even know where to start.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，我认识的几乎每个老年人阳台上都有某种植物或蔬菜，我的祖父母种葱、辣椒和西红柿，他们做饭时几乎每天都会用到。但我这个年纪的朋友？大多数人甚至不知道从哪里开始。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸
ideaNotes.textZh: 可选】 Still, I've noticed that younger people are slowly getting into it too, partly because of the trend of slow living and wanting to get back to something simple and natural after spending all day staring at screens. 不过，我注意到年轻人也在慢慢开始尝试，部分原因是慢生活的趋势，以及在盯着屏幕一整天后想要回归简单自然的东西。

entries.text: Is it easy to grow plants at home?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think it really depends on what you're growing — some plants are really easy and hard to kill, while others need a lot more attention and care.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我认为这真的取决于你种什么，有些植物非常容易养活，而另一些则需要更多关注和照料。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: For beginners, simple plants like succulents, spring onions, or basic herbs are pretty low maintenance — you just water them occasionally and they do their own thing. But things like fruit trees or flowers that need specific conditions can be really tricky if you don't know what you're doing.
ideaNotes.textZh: 对于初学者来说，像多肉植物、葱或基本香草这样的简单植物相当好打理，你只需偶尔浇水，它们就能自己生长。但像果树或需要特定条件的花卉，如果你不知道自己在做什么，可能真的很棘手。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, I once tried to grow roses at home and they kept dying on me no matter what I did — too much water, not enough sun, wrong soil — there were just too many things to get right. But the spring onions I threw in a cup of water? Those grew perfectly fine without me doing anything.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，我曾经尝试在家种玫瑰，不管我做什么它们一直在枯死，水太多、阳光不够、土壤不对，需要做对的事情太多了。但我扔在水杯里的葱？那些没有我做任何事就长得很好。• 转折【可选】 Even so, once you get the hang of it and understand what each plant needs, it becomes much more enjoyable and less stressful than it first seems. 即便如此，一旦你掌握了诀窍并了解每种植物需要什么，它就会变得比最初看起来更有趣、压力更小。

entries.text: Why do some people like to grow plants?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think some people enjoy growing plants because it gives them a sense of calm and something to nurture.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得有些人喜欢种植物，是因为这能带给他们一种平静感，也能给他们一个照顾的对象。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Taking care of a plant requires slowing down and paying attention to something living, which can feel very relaxing, especially for people with busy or stressful lives.
ideaNotes.textZh: 照顾一株植物需要放慢脚步，去关注一个有生命的东西，这会让人感觉非常放松，尤其是对生活忙碌、压力大的人来说。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, someone might find it satisfying to water their plants every morning and watch them slowly grow, feeling proud when a plant finally produces a new leaf or flower.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，有人可能会觉得每天早上给植物浇水、看着它们慢慢生长是一件很有满足感的事，当植物终于长出新叶子或开花时会感到自豪。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: Beyond the emotional benefits, growing plants indoors can also improve air quality, giving people a practical reason to keep doing it.
ideaNotes.textZh: 除了情感上的好处之外，在室内种植物还能改善空气质量，这也给了人们一个继续养护植物的实际理由。

entries.text: Describe a sucessful sports person you admire

paragraphs: The athlete I deeply admire is Ma Long, a Chinese table tennis player who is widely considered one of the greatest in the history of the sport.
Table tennis is huge in China — it's something people grow up with, whether it's a casual game in the park or watching matches on TV.
Growing up in that environment, I naturally got into following professional games, and that's how I first came across Ma Long and his incredible career.
He started playing at just five years old and joined the national team at fifteen.
Over the years, he's collected an impressive list of titles — Olympic gold medals, World Championships — you name it, he's won it.
But what really sets him apart isn't just his achievements on the court.
Outside of the sport, he's known for being incredibly humble — despite being one of the most famous athletes in the country, he never shows off, and always treats everyone with respect.
What I admire about him isn't just his victories — it's how he handles challenges.
A few years back, he went through a serious injury that kept him off the court for a long time, and a lot of people wondered if he'd ever come back.
But he did — through sheer hard work and determination, he made a full comeback and kept on winning.
That kind of resilience really motivates me to keep going when things get tough in my own life.
paragraphsZh: 我深深敬佩的运动员是马龙，一位中国乒乓球运动员，被广泛认为是这项运动史上最伟大的球员之一。
乒乓球在中国非常普及——是人们从小耳濡目染的运动，不管是在公园里打着玩，还是在电视上看比赛。
在这样的环境里长大，我自然而然地开始关注职业比赛，也就是这样认识了马龙和他精彩的职业生涯。
他从五岁就开始打球，十五岁加入国家队。
多年来，他赢得了一长串令人印象深刻的荣誉——奥运金牌、世界锦标赛冠军——你能想到的他基本都拿过了。
但真正让他与众不同的，不只是他在球场上的成就。
在运动之外，他以极度谦逊著称——尽管是全国最出名的运动员之一，他从不炫耀，对每个人都始终保持尊重。
我敬佩他的，不只是他的胜利——更是他面对挑战的方式。
几年前，他经历了一次严重的受伤，让他长时间离开了球场，很多人都在怀疑他是否还能回来。
但他做到了——凭借坚定的努力和决心，他成功复出并继续赢得比赛。
这种韧性真的很激励我，让我在自己的生活遇到困难时也能坚持下去。

entries.text: Why are there so few top athletes?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think there are so few top athletes because it takes a rare combination of natural talent and extreme dedication.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得顶尖运动员这么少，是因为这需要天赋和极致努力这两者非常罕见的结合。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Even someone with natural ability will fall behind without years of intense training, but someone who trains hard without the right physical potential also hits a ceiling.
ideaNotes.textZh: 即使一个人有天赋，如果没有多年的高强度训练也会落后，而一个训练很刻苦但没有合适身体条件的人，也会遇到瓶颈。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, thousands of kids might start playing football with dreams of going pro, but only a tiny fraction have both the physical gifts and the mental toughness to actually make it to the top.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，成千上万的孩子可能都怀着职业梦开始踢足球，但只有极少数人同时具备身体天赋和心理韧性，真正走到顶尖。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: On top of that, injuries or lack of access to good training resources can end even a talented athlete's career before they ever reach the top.
ideaNotes.textZh: 除此之外，受伤或缺乏优质训练资源，也可能让一个有天赋的运动员的职业生涯还没到达顶尖就结束了。

paragraphs: I think there are so few top athletes because it takes a rare combination of natural talent and extreme dedication.
Even someone with natural ability will fall behind without years of intense training, but someone who trains hard without the right physical potential also hits a ceiling.
For instance, thousands of kids might start playing football with dreams of going pro, but only a tiny fraction have both the physical gifts and the mental toughness to actually make it to the top.
On top of that, injuries or lack of access to good training resources can end even a talented athlete's career before they ever reach the top.
paragraphsZh: 我觉得顶尖运动员这么少，是因为这需要天赋和极致努力这两者非常罕见的结合。
即使一个人有天赋，如果没有多年的高强度训练也会落后，而一个训练很刻苦但没有合适身体条件的人，也会遇到瓶颈。
比如，成千上万的孩子可能都怀着职业梦开始踢足球，但只有极少数人同时具备身体天赋和心理韧性，真正走到顶尖。
除此之外，受伤或缺乏优质训练资源，也可能让一个有天赋的运动员的职业生涯还没到达顶尖就结束了。

entries.text: What is the most popular sport in your country?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I'd say table tennis and basketball are probably the most popular sports in China.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得乒乓球和篮球大概是中国最受欢迎的运动。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Table tennis has strong historical roots here, with China consistently dominating international competitions, while basketball became huge thanks to media exposure and star players people could look up to.
ideaNotes.textZh: 乒乓球在中国有很深的历史渊源，中国在国际赛事中一直处于统治地位，而篮球则因为媒体曝光和让人崇拜的明星球员而变得非常流行。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, almost every school has a ping pong table, and many neighborhoods have outdoor basketball courts where people play casually after school or work.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，几乎每所学校都有乒乓球桌，很多社区也有户外篮球场，人们放学或下班后会随意打上一场。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: More recently, sports like badminton have also been gaining popularity, especially among younger people looking for a fun way to stay active.

entries.text: Is it easy to identify children’s talents?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: No, I don't think it's easy to identify a child's talents, especially at a very young age.
ideaNotes.textZh: 不，我不认为发现孩子的天赋容易，尤其是在年纪很小的时候。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: A child might enjoy something without actually being naturally gifted at it, and it's hard to tell the difference between simple enthusiasm and real ability until they're tested over time.
ideaNotes.textZh: 孩子可能喜欢做某件事，但并不一定真的对此有天赋，在经过一段时间的考验之前，很难分辨这只是单纯的热情还是真正的能力。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, a child who loves singing might just enjoy the attention it brings, rather than having exceptional musical talent, and this often only becomes clear after years of lessons.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，一个喜欢唱歌的孩子可能只是喜欢这带来的关注，而不是真的有出色的音乐天赋，这通常要经过多年的学习才会真正明朗。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: That said, exposing children to many different activities early on can help parents notice patterns, like which skills a child picks up faster than expected.
ideaNotes.textZh: 不过，让孩子早期接触多种不同的活动，能帮助父母注意到一些规律，比如孩子哪些技能学得比预期更快。

entries.text: Is talent important in sports?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: Yes, I think talent definitely matters in sports, but it's not the only factor for success.
ideaNotes.textZh: 是的，我认为天赋在体育运动中确实很重要，但它不是成功的唯一因素。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Talent basically sets a person's potential ceiling, but without enough hard work, even a talented athlete won't actually reach that ceiling.
ideaNotes.textZh: 天赋基本上决定了一个人的潜力上限，但如果没有足够的努力，即使是有天赋的运动员也不会真正达到那个上限。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, a naturally talented runner might have incredible speed, but if they don't put in the training, someone with less talent but stronger work ethic could actually outperform them.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，一个天生有天赋的跑步选手可能拥有惊人的速度，但如果不投入训练，一个天赋较弱但更努力的人反而可能表现得更好。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: So really, talent gives someone a head start, but consistent effort is what determines how far they actually go.
ideaNotes.textZh: 所以说，天赋能给人一个领先的起点，但真正决定能走多远的是持续的努力。

So really, talent gives someone a head start, but consistent effort is what determines how far they actually go.

entries.text: What qualities should an athlete have?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think the most important quality an athlete needs is perseverance, the ability to keep going even after failure.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我觉得运动员最重要的品质是坚持不懈，也就是即使经历失败也能继续前进的能力。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Sports involve constant setbacks, like losing a game or getting injured, so athletes who give up easily never get the chance to actually improve over time.
ideaNotes.textZh: 体育运动中不断会遇到挫折，比如输掉比赛或受伤，所以那些容易放弃的运动员，永远没有机会真正得到长期的进步。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, a swimmer who fails to qualify for a competition might feel devastated at first, but the ones who keep training anyway are the ones who eventually break through.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，一个没能拿到比赛资格的游泳运动员，一开始可能会感到很沮丧，但那些依然坚持训练的人，才是最终能取得突破的人。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: Beyond perseverance, having strong mental focus during competition is just as crucial, since even physically gifted athletes can lose if they get too nervous.
ideaNotes.textZh: 除了坚持不懈，比赛中强大的心理专注力同样至关重要，因为即使身体条件出色的运动员，也可能因为过于紧张而输掉比赛。

entries.text: Should students have physical education and do sports at school?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: Yes, I definitely think students should have physical education at school, alongside their regular academic subjects.
ideaNotes.textZh: 是的，我确实认为学生应该在学校和常规学科一起上体育课。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: Sitting through classes all day can lead to physical inactivity, which affects not just students' health but also their ability to concentrate in other subjects.
ideaNotes.textZh: 一整天坐着上课会导致缺乏运动，这不仅影响学生的健康，也会影响他们在其他科目上的专注力。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, a school that includes regular PE classes often sees students come back to the classroom feeling more alert and energized, rather than sluggish from sitting all day.
ideaNotes.textZh: 比如，一所定期安排体育课的学校，学生上完体育课回到教室后往往感觉更清醒、更有活力，而不是因为一整天久坐而昏昏欲睡。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸[可选]
ideaNotes.text: Beyond physical health, playing sports also teaches valuable social skills like teamwork, which classroom learning alone often can't provide.
ideaNotes.textZh: 除了身体健康之外，参加体育运动还能教会学生宝贵的社交技能，比如团队合作，而这往往是单靠课堂学习给不了的。

entries.text: Describe a friend from your childhood

paragraphs: The person I'd like to talk about is my childhood best friend, [Name]. We've known each other for a long time — actually, more than 20 years.

We first met in kindergarten as classmates, and just got closer and closer from then on. When we were little, we were basically together every single day, just doing all sorts of things like playing games and watching cartoons.
Even though life is much busier now and there isn't as much free time as before, meeting up on weekends for a meal is still something we never skip. It's just a great way to relax and catch up.

Honestly, she's one of the most important people in my life — after all these years, I just can't imagine life without her around. She now runs a really successful company — it's actually a family business, and she took over right after graduation.
The company mainly sells cultural and creative products. Her job is product design, which is honestly the most important part of the whole business.

She really enjoys working there — product design has always been her passion, and having her own company gives her more freedom to bring all kinds of ideas to life. To do it well, she spent a whole year teaching herself cultural and creative design, just figuring things out on her own.

She didn't just learn it for the job — she's genuinely passionate about it. It wasn't easy, but it really paid off — she used everything she learned to create a unique product that quickly became a top-selling item online.
I really admire her creativity — she can take an idea and turn it into a modern product that people actually want to buy. And I think that's exactly what makes her business so successful.
To me, that's a really impressive achievement.万能结尾 So overall, I'm really grateful for our friendship, and I hope we can keep growing together.
paragraphsZh: 我想聊的是我的童年好友，[名字]。 我们认识很久了——其实已经超过20年了。
我们在幼儿园作为同班同学第一次相识，从那以后就越来越亲近。 小时候，我们几乎每天都在一起，做各种各样的事情，比如玩游戏、看动画片。
虽然现在生活忙碌了很多，没有以前那么多空闲时间，但周末见面吃顿饭还是我们雷打不动的习惯。 这真的是一种很好的放松和叙旧的方式。
说真的，她是我生命中最重要的人之一——这么多年过去了，我真的无法想象没有她的生活。 她现在经营着一家非常成功的公司——其实是家族企业，她一毕业就接手了。
公司主要销售文创产品。 她的工作是产品设计，说真的这是整个公司最重要的部分。
她很享受在那里工作——产品设计一直是她的热情所在，而且自己的公司给了她更多自由度去实现各种想法。 为了做好这份工作，她花了整整一年自学文创设计，完全靠自己摸索。
她学习不只是为了工作——她是真心热爱这个领域。 过程并不容易，但真的很值得——她把所学到的一切都用上了，做出了一款独特的产品，很快就成为了网上的爆款。
我真的很佩服她的创造力——她能把一个想法变成人们真正想买的现代产品。 我觉得这正是她生意如此成功的原因。
对我来说，这真的是非常了不起的成就。 总的来说，我真的很感激我们之间的友谊，希望我们能一起继续成长。

entries.text: What do you think of communicating via social media?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think communicating through social media is really convenient, but honestly it can also feel quite shallow compared to talking in person.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我认为通过社交媒体交流非常方便，但说实话，与当面交谈相比，它也可能感觉相当表面。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: The thing is, on social media you can stay in touch with lots of people at once and it doesn't matter where they are in the world, but most of the time it's just liking posts and sending short messages rather than having a real deep conversation.
ideaNotes.textZh: 问题在于，在社交媒体上你可以同时与很多人保持联系，不管他们在世界哪里，但大多数时候只是点赞帖子和发送简短消息，而不是进行真正深入的对话。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For example, I might have hundreds of followers online but only actually talk properly with maybe five or six of them, which makes you wonder how many of those connections are real friendships.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，我可能在网上有数百个粉丝，但实际上只和其中五六个人好好交谈，这让你不禁思考这些联系中有多少是真正的友谊。转折【可选】 However, for people who live far apart or have busy schedules, social media is actually a really good way to stay connected and make sure friendships don't just fade away. 然而，对于住得很远或日程繁忙的人来说，社交媒体实际上是一个很好的方式来保持联系，确保友谊不会就这样慢慢消失。

entries.text: Can't be there in personWhat's the difference between having younger friends and older friends?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think the biggest difference is that younger friends bring a lot of fun and energy into your life, while older friends tend to offer more wisdom and life experience.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我认为最大的区别是年轻朋友给你的生活带来很多乐趣和活力，而年长朋友往往提供更多智慧和人生经验。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: The thing is, with younger friends you tend to try new things, go on adventures, and just have a good time, whereas with older friends you can have much deeper conversations about life and they can give you advice based on what they've already been through.
ideaNotes.textZh: 问题在于，和年轻朋友在一起你往往会尝试新事物，去冒险，只是玩得开心；而和年长朋友在一起，你可以进行更深入的人生对话，他们可以根据自己已经经历的事情给你建议。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For example, my younger friends are the ones I call when I want to go out and do something exciting, but when I'm going through something tough or confusing, I always turn to my older friends because they just get it in a way others don't.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，当我想出去做些刺激的事时，我会打电话给年轻朋友；但当我遇到艰难或困惑的事情时，我总是转向年长朋友，因为他们以一种别人无法理解的方式懂得。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸
ideaNotes.textZh: 可选】 On top of that, I think having both types of friends actually makes your life much richer and more balanced, because they each bring something completely different to the table. 除此之外，我认为同时拥有两种类型的朋友实际上让你的生活更加丰富和平衡，因为他们各自带来完全不同的东西。

keyPhrases.phrase: Go out and do something exciting

paragraphs: I think the biggest difference is that younger friends bring a lot of fun and energy into your life, while older friends tend to offer more wisdom and life experience.

The thing is, with younger friends you tend to try new things, go on adventures, and just have a good time, whereas with older friends you can have much deeper conversations about life and they can give you advice based on what they've already been through.

For example, my younger friends are the ones I call when I want to go out and do something exciting, but when I'm going through something tough or confusing, I always turn to my older friends because they just get it in a way others don't.
paragraphsZh: 我认为最大的区别是年轻朋友给你的生活带来很多乐趣和活力，而年长朋友往往提供更多智慧和人生经验。
问题在于，和年轻朋友在一起你往往会尝试新事物，去冒险，只是玩得开心；而和年长朋友在一起，你可以进行更深入的人生对话，他们可以根据自己已经经历的事情给你建议。
例如，当我想出去做些刺激的事时，我会打电话给年轻朋友；但当我遇到艰难或困惑的事情时，我总是转向年长朋友，因为他们以一种别人无法理解的方式懂得。

可选】 On top of that, I think having both types of friends actually makes your life much richer and more balanced, because they each bring something completely different to the table. 除此之外，我认为同时拥有两种类型的朋友实际上让你的生活更加丰富和平衡，因为他们各自带来完全不同的东西。

entries.text: Describe a person you know who would like to choose a career in the medical field (e.g. a doctor, a nurse)

paragraphs: The person I'd like to talk about is Dr Tao Yong, a famous eye doctor in China. I first heard about him through a news report — he was attacked by a patient, and his hands were badly injured.

But not long after recovering, he returned to the hospital and went back to work. I was a bit curious about what kept him going after such a tragedy, so I did some research online to find out more about his story.
I learned that his dream of working in medicine started when he was just a kid. His mother suffered from a serious eye disease and went to the hospital for treatment.

Thanks to the doctors, she recovered really well, and that experience made him decide to become an eye doctor. He worked incredibly hard, studied both in Beijing and Germany, and eventually became a top specialist at a leading hospital.

In his interviews, he mentioned that his ultimate dream is a world where no one has to suffer from blindness. To achieve this, he keeps pushing for free eye treatment in poor areas who can't afford it, and continues doing research to advance eye medicine.

Actually, Dr Tao Yong isn't a typical celebrity from the entertainment industry. But I think he's exactly the kind of person who truly deserves to be famous, because of his great contribution to medicine and society.
If I ever got the chance, I'd love to meet him face to face — maybe at one of his charity talks or public events. I really just want to tell him that he is a true role model for me.

He has a real belief in his profession, a genuine love for every patient, and a positive attitude towards life. [ Honestly, his story made me think deeply about what it really means to be dedicated to work — it's not just about earning a living, but treating your career as a true calling. ] That's something really rare nowadays, and meeting him in person would mean a lot to me.
paragraphsZh: 我想聊的人是陶勇医生，中国一位著名的眼科医生。 我第一次听说他是通过一篇新闻报道——他被一名患者袭击，双手严重受伤。
但在康复后不久，他回到了医院，重新开始工作。 我有些好奇是什么让他在经历这样的悲剧后坚持下去，于是我上网搜索了更多关于他的故事。
我了解到，他从事医疗行业的梦想从小就开始了。 他的母亲患有严重的眼科疾病，去医院接受治疗。
多亏了医生，她恢复得很好，那次经历让他决定成为一名眼科医生。 他努力学习，先后在北京和德国求学，最终成为了一家顶尖医院的顶级专科医生。
在他的采访中，他提到自己的终极梦想是一个没有人因失明而痛苦的世界。 为此，他不断推动为负担不起费用的贫困地区提供免费眼科治疗，并继续做科研以推进眼科医学的发展。
其实，陶勇医生不是娱乐圈那种典型的名人。 但我认为他正是那种真正值得出名的人，因为他对医学和社会的巨大贡献。
如果有机会，我很想与他面对面相见——也许是在他的某场公益讲座或公开活动上。 我真的很想告诉他，他是我真正的榜样。

entries.text: Do you think being a doctor is easy or difficult?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: Honestly, I think being a doctor is one of the hardest jobs out there — not just physically but also mentally and emotionally.
ideaNotes.textZh: 说实话，我认为当医生是最艰难的工作之一，不仅仅是体力上，精神和情感上也是。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: I mean, doctors have to spend years and years studying and training before they even start working, and then once they do, they're dealing with people's lives every single day — that kind of pressure and responsibility never really goes away.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我的意思是，医生在开始工作之前必须花费多年时间学习和训练，而一旦开始工作，他们每天都在面对人们的生命，这种压力和责任从未真正消失。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For example, I have a cousin who is a doctor and she often works twelve-hour shifts, comes home completely worn out, and still has to study new medical updates in her spare time just to keep up. It looks really tough from the outside.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，我有一个做医生的表姐，她经常上十二小时的班，回家时完全精疲力竭，空闲时间还要学习新的医学知识才能跟上。从外面看真的很辛苦。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸
ideaNotes.textZh: 可选】 That said, I think most doctors would say it is also incredibly rewarding — knowing that you genuinely helped someone or even saved a life is something most jobs just can't give you. 话虽如此，我认为大多数医生也会说这非常有成就感，知道你真正帮助了某人甚至救了一条命是大多数工作无法给你的。

entries.text: Do you think learning biology is interesting for children?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think biology can actually be really fascinating for children if it's taught in the right way, because kids are naturally curious about living things around them.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我认为如果教学方式正确，生物对孩子来说实际上可以非常有趣，因为孩子天生对周围的生物充满好奇。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: After all, biology is basically about life itself — animals, plants, the human body — and these are things children already wonder about all the time. The problem is when it gets turned into just memorising long lists of words instead of actually exploring and discovering.
ideaNotes.textZh: 毕竟，生物基本上是关于生命本身的，动物、植物、人体，这些都是孩子们一直在好奇的事情。问题是当它变成只是背长串单词而不是真正探索和发现的时候。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, I remember in middle school biology we once got to look at cells under a real microscope, and everyone was so excited and curious — people were actually fighting over who got to look first.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，我记得在初中生物课上，我们有一次用真正的显微镜观察细胞，每个人都非常兴奋和好奇，大家甚至在抢着第一个看。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸
ideaNotes.textZh: 可选】 Plus, biology connects really naturally to everyday life — things like why we get sick, how food gives us energy, or why animals behave a certain way — and when children can see that link to real life, they get genuinely hooked. 而且，生物与日常生活联系得非常自然，比如为什么我们会生病、食物如何给我们能量或为什么动物会有某种行为，当孩子们能看到与现实生活的联系时，他们会真正着迷。

entries.text: Why do some children want to become doctors?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think children who want to become doctors are usually motivated by a genuine desire to help people and a sense that it's a job that really matters and makes a difference.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我认为想成为医生的孩子通常是出于真正想帮助他人的愿望，以及觉得这是一份真正重要且有意义的工作。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: A lot of children are inspired by someone close to them — maybe a family member got sick and a doctor helped them recover, or they watched a medical drama on TV and found it exciting. At that age, becoming a doctor feels like becoming a hero — someone who saves lives and is respected by everyone around them.
ideaNotes.textZh: 很多孩子受到身边人的启发，也许家人生病了，医生帮助他们康复，或者他们在电视上看了医疗剧觉得很刺激。在那个年龄，成为医生感觉就像成为英雄，一个拯救生命、受到周围每个人尊敬的人。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, I remember when I was young I wanted to be a doctor too — my grandfather was ill and I saw how the doctors took care of him and how grateful our whole family was. It just made me think that's the kind of person I want to be.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，我记得小时候我也想成为医生，我祖父生病了，我看到医生如何照顾他，我们全家是多么感激。这让我觉得那就是我想成为的那种人。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸
ideaNotes.textZh: 可选】 And also, being a doctor is seen as a very stable and respected career in China, so parents often encourage their children towards it from a young age — which naturally plants the idea in kids' heads early on. 另外，在中国当医生被认为是非常稳定和受尊敬的职业，所以父母经常从小就鼓励孩子朝这个方向发展，这自然很早就在孩子心中种下了这个想法。

entries.text: Do you think governments should put a large amount of money into medical research?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: Yes, I genuinely think governments should invest heavily in medical research — it's one of the most directly useful things money can be spent on because it affects everyone's health and lives.
ideaNotes.textZh: 是的，我真心认为政府应该大力投资医学研究，这是资金可以花在的最直接有用的事情之一，因为它影响每个人的健康和生命。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: I mean, diseases like cancer, diabetes, and new viruses aren't going away on their own — without proper funding, researchers simply can't do the work needed to find treatments and cures. And when a government invests in medical research, the benefits don't just go to one group of people, they eventually reach the whole population — which makes it a really worthwhile use of public money.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我的意思是，像癌症、糖尿病和新病毒这样的疾病不会自行消失，没有适当的资金，研究人员根本无法完成寻找治疗方法和治愈方法所需的工作。当政府投资医学研究时，好处不只是惠及一个群体，最终会惠及整个人口，这使它成为公共资金非常值得的用途。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, a lot of the vaccines and treatments we rely on today only exist because governments and institutions put serious money into research decades ago — without that investment, we simply wouldn't have the medicine we take for granted now.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，我们今天依赖的很多疫苗和治疗方法之所以存在，是因为政府和机构几十年前认真投入了资金进行研究，没有那些投资，我们根本不会有现在认为理所当然的药物。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸
ideaNotes.textZh: 可选】 And also, investing in medical research actually saves money in the long run — if you can prevent or cure diseases more effectively, you spend less on treating sick people later, which benefits the whole healthcare system. 另外，投资医学研究实际上从长远来看节省了资金，如果你能更有效地预防或治愈疾病，以后在治疗病人上花的钱就更少，这有利于整个医疗体系。

keyPhrases.phrase: Proper funding can't do the work

entries.text: Describe a person you know who has a successful business

paragraphs: The person I'd like to talk about is my childhood best friend, [Name]. We've known each other for a long time — actually, more than 20 years.

We first met in kindergarten as classmates, and just got closer and closer from then on. When we were little, we were basically together every single day, just doing all sorts of things like playing games and watching cartoons.
Even though life is much busier now and there isn't as much free time as before, meeting up on weekends for a meal is still something we never skip. It's just a great way to relax and catch up.

Honestly, she's one of the most important people in my life — after all these years, I just can't imagine life without her around. She now runs a really successful company — it's actually a family business, and she took over right after graduation.
The company mainly sells cultural and creative products. Her job is product design, which is honestly the most important part of the whole business.

She really enjoys working there — product design has always been her passion, and having her own company gives her more freedom to bring all kinds of ideas to life. To do it well, she spent a whole year teaching herself cultural and creative design, just figuring things out on her own.

She didn't just learn it for the job — she's genuinely passionate about it. It wasn't easy, but it really paid off — she used everything she learned to create a unique product that quickly became a top-selling item online.
I really admire her creativity — she can take an idea and turn it into a modern product that people actually want to buy. And I think that's exactly what makes her business so successful.
To me, that's a really impressive achievement.万能结尾 So overall, I'm really grateful for our friendship, and I hope we can keep growing together.
paragraphsZh: 我想聊的是我的童年好友，[名字]。 我们认识很久了——其实已经超过20年了。
我们在幼儿园作为同班同学第一次相识，从那以后就越来越亲近。 小时候，我们几乎每天都在一起，做各种各样的事情，比如玩游戏、看动画片。
虽然现在生活忙碌了很多，没有以前那么多空闲时间，但周末见面吃顿饭还是我们雷打不动的习惯。 这真的是一种很好的放松和叙旧的方式。
说真的，她是我生命中最重要的人之一——这么多年过去了，我真的无法想象没有她的生活。 她现在经营着一家非常成功的公司——其实是家族企业，她一毕业就接手了。
公司主要销售文创产品。 她的工作是产品设计，说真的这是整个公司最重要的部分。
她很享受在那里工作——产品设计一直是她的热情所在，而且自己的公司给了她更多自由度去实现各种想法。 为了做好这份工作，她花了整整一年自学文创设计，完全靠自己摸索。
她学习不只是为了工作——她是真心热爱这个领域。 过程并不容易，但真的很值得——她把所学到的一切都用上了，做出了一款独特的产品，很快就成为了网上的爆款。
我真的很佩服她的创造力——她能把一个想法变成人们真正想买的现代产品。 我觉得这正是她生意如此成功的原因。
对我来说，这真的是非常了不起的成就。 总的来说，我真的很感激我们之间的友谊，希望我们能一起继续成长。

entries.text: Why do some people start their own business?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think the main reason people start their own business is because they want to be their own boss and have the freedom to do things their own way.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我认为人们创业的主要原因是想成为自己的老板，有自由按自己的方式做事。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: This is because working for someone else means you have to follow other people's rules, stick to a fixed schedule, and your income has a ceiling. Running your own business gives you the chance to break out of that.
ideaNotes.textZh: 这是因为为别人工作意味着你必须遵守他人的规则，遵循固定的时间表，而且收入有上限。自己创业让你有机会突破这些限制。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For example, a friend of mine quit her office job because she was tired of being told what to do, and she opened her own bakery which now makes her much happier and more money than before.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，我的一个朋友辞掉了她的办公室工作，因为她厌倦了被人指挥，她开了自己的烘焙店，现在比以前更快乐也赚得更多。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸
ideaNotes.textZh: 可选】 On top of that, some people also start a business because they have a passion or idea they really believe in and just want to give it a shot and see where it goes. 除此之外，有些人创业也是因为他们有一个真正相信的热情或想法，只是想试一试，看看会走到哪里。

This is because working for someone else means you have to follow other people's rules, stick to a fixed schedule, and your income has a ceiling. Running your own business gives you the chance to break out of that.
For example, a friend of mine quit her office job because she was tired of being told what to do, and she opened her own bakery which now makes her much happier and more money than before.

entries.text: Should governments provide financial support to start-ups?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think governments should support start-ups, especially ones with good ideas but no money to get off the ground.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我认为政府应该支持初创企业，尤其是那些有好想法但没有资金起步的企业。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: This is because many people have brilliant ideas but simply can't afford the initial costs like renting a space, hiring staff, or buying equipment, and without some help they just give up before they even start.
ideaNotes.textZh: 这是因为很多人有绝妙的想法，但根本负担不起初始成本，比如租场地、雇员工或购买设备，如果没有一些帮助，他们在开始之前就放弃了。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For example, a lot of the big tech companies we use today, like some apps and platforms, actually received government funding early on which gave them the push they needed to grow.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，我们今天使用的很多大型科技公司，比如一些应用和平台，实际上在早期都获得了政府资金，这给了他们成长所需的推动力。• 转折【可选】 However, the government should also make sure the money goes to businesses with a solid plan, not just hand it out to anyone, otherwise it's just a waste of public money. 然而，政府也应该确保资金流向有可靠计划的企业，而不是随便发给任何人，否则只是浪费公共资金。

entries.text: Do most people prefer shopping at big stores or small stores?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think most people these days tend to prefer big stores simply because they are more convenient and offer more choices.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我认为如今大多数人倾向于选择大商店，仅仅是因为它们更方便且提供更多选择。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: This is because in a big store you can get everything in one go, the prices are usually cheaper, and you don't have to run around to different places. It just saves a lot of time and effort.
ideaNotes.textZh: 这是因为在大商店你可以一次买齐所有东西，价格通常更便宜，不需要跑到不同的地方。这节省了大量时间和精力。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For example, I personally always go to the big supermarket near my house for the weekly shop because I can get my food, cleaning products, and even clothes all in one trip.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，我个人每次都去家附近的大超市做每周采购，因为我可以在一次出行中买到食物、清洁用品甚至衣服。

ideaNotes.label: 延伸
ideaNotes.textZh: 可选】 That said, small stores still have their own charm because they often feel more personal and friendly, and some people really enjoy that local community feeling you just can't get in a big chain. 话虽如此，小商店仍然有自己的魅力，因为它们通常感觉更亲切友好，有些人真的很享受那种在大连锁店里感受不到的本地社区感。

entries.text: Is it easy to set up a new business in your country?

ideaNotes.label: 观点
ideaNotes.text: I think it's become much easier than before in many ways, but that doesn't mean it's simple — there's still a lot of competition and pressure involved.
ideaNotes.textZh: 我认为在很多方面已经比以前容易多了，但这不意味着简单，仍然涉及很多竞争和压力。

ideaNotes.label: 解释
ideaNotes.text: On one hand, the government has made the registration process simpler over the years, and there are now more funding options and support programmes for new businesses than before. On the other hand, the market is extremely crowded — whatever idea you have, there are probably already hundreds of people doing the same thing, which makes it really hard to stand out and survive.
ideaNotes.textZh: 一方面，政府多年来简化了注册流程，现在比以前有更多资金选择和扶持项目。另一方面，市场极其拥挤，无论你有什么想法，可能已经有数百人在做同样的事情，这使得脱颖而出和生存真的很难。

ideaNotes.label: 例子
ideaNotes.text: For instance, I've seen so many people open bubble tea shops or small restaurants with a lot of excitement, only to shut down within a year because the competition was just too fierce and the costs were higher than they expected.
ideaNotes.textZh: 例如，我见过很多人满怀热情地开奶茶店或小餐厅，却在不到一年内就关门，因为竞争太激烈，成本比他们预期的高。转折【可选】 That said, with the rise of e-commerce and social media, it's now much easier to start something small online without needing a physical shop or a huge amount of money upfront — which has really lowered the barrier for a lot of people. 话虽如此，随着电商和社交媒体的兴起，现在无需实体店或大量前期资金就能在网上小规模创业，这真的为很多人降低了门槛。
